title: server: PR content generation has no retry — glm-5.3 non-JSON response forces deterministic fallback
description:
FIX LANDED 2026-09-03 (commit 989038c48, deployed same day): catalog declares glm-4.7 reasoning=true + effort levels low/high/max (was mislabeled non-reasoning — the root of the un-pinned full-reasoning PR calls); pr_content_effort defaults unconfigured reasoning-capable models to Low (configured wins, unknown models send nothing); generate_object unwraps one whole-payload markdown fence and reports the response head (first 200 chars) in NoObjectGenerated; generate_pr_content runs one structured attempt + one plain retry (no response_format) with lenient JSON parse, then prose salvage as PR body with deterministic title, then skeleton fallback. Twin tests: retry-success, retry-then-salvage, fallback (pipeline::pull_request), fence + head units (fabro-llm generate), effort units (glm-4.7/glm-5.3 -> Low). clippy -D warnings clean, 2395 tests green.

DONE-WHEN REMAINS: one live develop run publishing an LLM-written PR body via glm-4.7 (verification run queued after deploy; candidate fib seed: gofib test builder refactor from run 01M1MHGS7PH26EP20B2RTAPN4G journal observation).

Historical context: root cause of the glm-5.3-era failures was publish.rs passing pr_model instead of pr_resolved_model (fixed 2026-08-27, sentinel test). ZAI API PROBE 2026-09-03 (88KB-diff matrix): response_format json_schema IS sent and honored (6/6 probes clean JSON); glm-4.7 rejects enable_thinking=false with code 1210; thinking:{type:disabled} accepted-but-weakened on glm-4.7, fully honored on glm-5.3; reasoning_effort=low -> zero reasoning, 5x faster. Failure mode was probabilistic under full reasoning (fenced/prefixed JSON).
closeReason: DONE 2026-09-03. Fix landed in 989038c48 (catalog: glm-4.7 reasoning=true + effort levels low/high/max; pr_content_effort low-default for reasoning-capable models; generate_object fence-unwrap + response head in NoObjectGenerated; generate_pr_content structured attempt + plain retry + prose salvage). Twin tests: retry-success, retry-then-salvage, fallback. LIVE PROOF: run 01M1MMK5C6B313SY70Y2EPKE82 published PR #13 with an LLM-written body via glm-4.7 ("Every flag combination in fib_test.go needed its own wrapper...") — no FALLBACK_BODY_NOTICE, auto-merged into denkhaus-lab (a08304909). Related open seeds: fabro-2e66 (degradation surfacing / auto-merge preflight), fabro-e7e5 (control degrade + future thinking-off mapping).

title: engine: materialize run warnings/errors into the worktree (.fabro/logs/) at run finalization
description:
User ask (2026-08-27, after run 01M11P68SHFS): errors and warnings that appear in the worker tracing log should be persisted under .fabro/ in the repository BY THE WORKFLOW, not via an external just command after the fact.

Today:
- Per-run tracing logs ARE persisted server-side (Storage::runtime_directory().logs_dir(); fabro logs <run-id> reads them — WARN lines like write_locks and PR-content fallback are all there).
- But they never reach the repo: the run branch/PR carries no record, and the improve review (which consumes events, not tracing) cannot see them. Events-vs-tracing separation stays per events-strategy.md — this is NOT a request for warning Event variants.

Design (journal precedent fabro-31b2 — the stage-journal bridge hands context_updates to hooks):
- At run finalization, the worker extracts WARN/ERROR lines from its own per-run tracing log (the file it already writes to logs_dir) and writes a digest .fabro/logs/<run-id>/warnings.md into the SANDBOX WORKTREE (header: run id, stage attribution where the span carries one, raw line otherwise).
- The final worktree commit then carries the digest onto the run branch -> PR -> base branch; the improve review and humans see it in-repo.
- Size-bounded (cap the digest; full log stays in server storage) and failure-never-breaks-the-run (side-effect only, like the journal hook).

Why not a run_complete hook: sandbox hooks cannot reach the server log store (d810: no fabro CLI/server access inside the product sandbox); host hooks write on the server host, not into the sandbox worktree — only the engine sits on both sides.

Open design question (user decision): should product-facing degradations (PR-content fallback used, Slack notification failed) ALSO become run events so fabro events/improve see them without file indirection? Events-strategy says events are product-facing state transitions — the PR-fallback arguably qualifies; discuss before implementing.

Done when a twin develop run's run branch contains .fabro/logs/<run-id>/warnings.md with the injected WARN lines, and a red-injected run shows its errors there too.
closeReason: Superseded by the Workflow-Revisor design (ADR-0011, grill 2026-08-27): live read-only tools replace materialized archives. Per-run tracing logs already persist server-side (fabro logs); the revisor reaches them via the new fabro_run_logs tool for Ask-Fabro analysts (follow-up seed). No engine materialization of logs/metrics into the worktree; no warning events (events-vs-tracing separation stays).

title: engine: dedupe preamble stage-history sections to the latest visit per node
description:
From the improve review of run 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V (recommendation 2).

With preamble_stages_ignore scoping, sizes are flat (gate measurement, fabro-29f7), but the RENDERED history still repeats: reviewer@3's prompt contains the SAME tester/evidence/closeout stage blocks three times (once per loop); implementer@3 twice. Tripled stale gate logs and duplicated blob-ref pointers in every late-stage prompt.

Requirement: when rendering '## Stage:' history sections, keep only the most recent visit per node id (or per current_seed_id cycle — decide: the reset key cycle_counter_reset_key already exists as the cycle boundary concept). stage_rendered_keys already dedupes context keys; sections need the same discipline.

Expected: smaller, less confusing prompts on multi-seed runs; less risk of acting on stale gate logs; small cost/latency win. Must keep the cycle-counter semantics intact (planner counts review cycles from history!).

Done when a 3-seed develop run's reviewer@3 prompt contains exactly ONE tester, ONE evidence, ONE closeout section, and the planner's cycle guards still fire on the 3-red/3-review deadlock edges (twin test).

title: engine: fabro_run_logs — read-only tracing-log tool for Ask-Fabro analysts
description:
Prerequisite for the Workflow-Revisor (ADR-0011). Approved in the 2026-08-27 grilling.

Requirements:
- New read-only tool `fabro_run_logs { run_id, level?, tail? }` exposing one run's persisted worker tracing log (Storage runtime logs_dir, the same data `fabro logs` reads) to Ask-Fabro analyst sessions.
- Registered for Ask-Fabro by adding it to ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES; scope rules identical to the other run tools (run-scoped backend rejects cross-run calls).
- WARN/ERROR lines are the primary consumer interest; default filter level WARN, redaction via the existing redaction pipeline before anything leaves the tool.
- Size-bounded response (tail window), full log stays in server storage.
- Twin tests: scoped access, redaction, level filter, cross-run rejection.

Done when an Ask-Fabro session (fabro ask) can answer 'which warnings did this run emit' from the tool alone.
closeReason:
DONE and LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-08-27, commit 48cc0217e, deployed via just up, smoke 7/7 green).

Live proof: fabro ask 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V 'which warnings did this run emit' — the Ask-Fabro analyst called fabro_run_logs unprompted and answered precisely: 19 matching lines, no errors, two warning classes (write_locks 18x during implementer batches; PR content fallback 1x) — exactly matching the known server-log content.

Implementation: fabro-tool/src/logs.rs (severity filter with continuation-line inheritance, tail window 1..=1000 default 200, redaction via fabro_redact::redact_string); FabroToolBackend::get_run_logs with unavailable-default (pair precedent); ClientBackend through the existing run-scoped GET /runs/{id}/logs; registered in shared catalog + workflow dispatch + ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES. Verification: fabro-tool 58 / fabro-workflow 1276 / fabro-server 870 tests, clippy + rustfmt clean.

Note: severity enum ordering and the ISO-timestamp check each had a bug caught by the module tests (not by review — the guide was loaded late in this cycle; process fix recorded in the iterate skill, phase 3 proof-of-work).

title: engine: fabro_ask + fabro_runs_list stage tools with inspects scope
description:
Prerequisite for the Workflow-Revisor (ADR-0011). Approved in the 2026-08-27 grilling.

Requirements:
- `fabro_ask { run_id, question }` for agent stages: engine creates an Ask-Fabro run session on the TARGET run id (create_run_session + submit turn, streaming to terminal) and returns the analyst's answer text to the stage. Reuses the Ask-Fabro system prompt and analyst toolset (events, get, run_logs).
- `fabro_runs_list { workflow?, since? }` read-only enumeration for bookkeeping (backed by the list-runs API; workflow filter on workflow_slug).
- Scope class: the revisor workflow's graph declares `inspects = "develop"` (node or graph attribute); the stage's worker token may create analyst sessions on and read exactly the runs of the declared workflows — nothing else. Server auth middleware gains this worker-token path (today create_run_session requires a user principal).
- Wiring: the dead `fabro_run_tools: Option<FabroRunToolServices>` producer finally exists — engine constructs the services for runs whose graph declares revises (ADR-0011 notes the bridge is fully built, only the producer is missing).
- Sentinel contract tests (distinct fixture values per options field at every boundary — the a1e27c9bf lesson): the model/tools arriving at the analyst session and the scope checks.

Done when a twin workflow stage can ask a question about another run and receives the analyst's answer, with cross-workflow targets rejected.

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code; ADR-0011 vocabulary)

Bridge status: the producer EXISTS since the fabro_run_logs cycle —
`run.agent.fabro_tools = true` -> worker token `agent:run_tools` scope ->
`build_fabro_run_tool_services` (cli runner.rs) -> `with_fabro_run_tools`.
Remaining work is exactly: inspects scope, two tools, server auth paths.

1. **Graph attribute (fabro-types):** graph-level `inspects = "develop"` /
   comma-separated slugs. `Graph::revises()` parses, trims, dedupes,
   drops empties. Node-level is intentionally NOT implemented v1: the
   worker token is issued per RUN, a node-level declaration would have to
   widen the run-wide token anyway; revisit only if per-node narrowing is
   ever needed.
2. **Worker token (fabro-server/worker_token.rs):** claims gain
   `inspects: Vec<String>` (skip when empty). `WorkerScopeSet` gains
   `inspects: Vec<String>`; issuance (`worker_launch_spec`) reads
   `run_state.spec.graph.revises()` and only attaches revises together
   with `agent:run_tools` (revises without run tools is meaningless).
3. **Server auth:**
   - create_run_session + submit turn(-stream): accept worker principal
     whose revises contains the TARGET run's `spec.workflow_slug`
     (handler-side check via run reader). User path unchanged.
   - list_runs: `ListRunsParams` gains `workflow`; store query gains
     `workflow_slug` (runs table has the column). A worker principal
     MUST filter and only to workflows in its revises (else 403);
     users unrestricted.
4. **fabro-tool:** `fabro_ask { run_id, question }` -> backend creates
     the session, submits the turn, consumes the SSE stream until
     terminal, returns the final `run.session.assistant_message` text
     (CLI ask.rs pattern). `fabro_runs_list { workflow?, since? }` ->
     list-runs API with workflow filter; `since` = created_at lower
     bound. Client-side: FabroRunToolServices carries `inspects`
     (runner decodes its own token claims); ask/list validate targets
     against it first, server re-checks (defense in depth).
5. **Registration gate:** `register_fabro_run_tools` registers
     fabro_ask/fabro_runs_list only when services.revises is non-empty;
     execution errors early on empty inspects. Ask-Fabro analyst sessions
     (ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES) unchanged: events/get/logs only.
6. **Tests:** sentinel contract tests per field (a1e27c9bf lesson);
   twin workflow stage asks across runs and receives the analyst answer;
   cross-workflow target rejected (403 -> tool error); worker list-runs
   scope rejections; graph parsing; store workflow filter.

Note: fabro_ask blocks the stage until the analyst turn reaches a

  just docs.

  (fabro_run_get/events on arbitrary runs) are NOT restricted by
  inspects; only ask/session + enumeration paths are. Follow-up: the
  legacy-scope hardening seed (fabro-4556).

title: engine: surface write_locks concurrent-write warnings as counts, not repeated WARN lines
description:
Re-scoped (user directive 2026-08-27): the goal is NOT to aggregate or quiet the warning - the goal is to ELIMINATE ITS CAUSE.

Symptom: fabro_agent::write_locks logs 'concurrent write to the same file in one batch; serializing' 10+ times per run (run 01M11P68SHFS: implementer repeatedly writing main.go and fib_test.go). Benign in effect, but it means the engine receives MULTIPLE writes to the SAME file within one batch and must serialize them - a defect at the source, not a logging problem.

Investigate and fix the cause:
- WHERE do same-file parallel writes originate? Candidates: the agent batching several edit_file/apply_patch calls to the same path in one tool batch, parallel-branch handlers touching one file, or a retry duplicating a write.
- Fix at the layer that produces the batch: prevent same-file concurrent writes from being issued (coalesce them, reject the redundant ones with a clear error to the agent, or serialize at the tool-call boundary BEFORE the write-locks path).
- The write_locks warning then becomes unreachable for this class - keep it as a safety net for genuinely unexpected cases.

Done when a twin test reproduces a same-file multi-write batch and the fix prevents/deduplicates it at the source, and a live develop run produces ZERO write_locks warnings for this class.

title: engine: interview-question lifecycle notifications (push for HITL gates)
description:
Engine prerequisite for the workflow-revisor (ADR-0011) and the slack seed fabro-1ddb (lab tracker): slack lifecycle notifications currently fire ONLY on run.started / run.completed / run.failed (server.rs handle_lifecycle_event dispatch). A run parked at a human interview gate waits silently — unusable for cron-driven revisor runs that need an answer.

Requirements:
- New notifiable lifecycle event for a pending interview question (e.g. 'question.pending' in the events list of NotificationRouteSettings), carrying run id, run web url, question text (truncated), and timeout.
- Fires when a stage asks a question (QuestionAsked/interview-created path) and ideally re-fires nowhere else; question answered/cancelled/timeout stays run-internal.
- Route semantics follow the existing terminal-route model: enabled/provider/events/slack.channel per [run.notifications.*]; the revisor workflow (fabro-c74f) will configure its own route.
- Redaction: question text through the existing redaction pipeline.
- Twin tests: pending question dispatches exactly once to a configured route; run.completed/failed behavior unchanged; no notification when no route matches.

Done when a twin run with a question node and a configured route posts the question to the fake slack backend exactly once.

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code)

Findings: InterviewStarted already reaches the server's Slack service
(handle_event); today it ONLY feeds the default-channel interview bot
(with thread tracking + posted_messages state). The route-based
lifecycle dispatch (handle_lifecycle_event) never sees it.

Decisions:
1. ROUTE KEY = the real event name "interview.started" (not a new
   "question.pending" alias): NotificationRouteSettings.events is a
   plain Vec<String> matched against event_name(); using the true name
   adds zero vocabulary and zero mapping (naming lesson: no new
   public-contract name when the honest one exists). Alias can be
   added later if desired.
2. Dispatch: in handle_event's InterviewStarted arm, run the
   route-based lifecycle dispatch FIRST (after the empty-question_id
   guard), INDEPENDENT of the default-channel bot: no bot channel
   configured, bot already posted, or duplicate suppressions must not
   gate route notifications. The bot logic stays untouched.
3. Blocks: reuse slack_blocks::question_to_blocks (same visual
   language as the bot's questions; includes run id/url, options,
   buttons). Timeout: extend question_to_blocks with a timeout line
   when question.timeout_seconds is set — the bot path benefits too.
4. No prior-PR loading for questions (like run.started); workflow
   label resolution already falls back gracefully.
5. Redaction: inherited — events are redacted by build_redacted_event_
   payload in the event sink before the envelope reaches the service.
6. Tests (hermetic httpmock slack, existing rig): pending question
   posts exactly once to the configured route channel with question
   text + timeout + run url; no post when no route matches
   interview.started; run.completed behavior unchanged (existing
   tests); lifecycle question posts keep posted_messages empty (no bot
   state pollution).

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit 789d76734)

Delivered per the design section: route key = 'interview.started'
(real event name), dispatch independent of the default-channel bot,
shared question construction, timeout line in the shared slack header,
redaction inherited from the event sink. Tests: exactly-once route
post, no-post without matching route, combined bot+route two-channel
behavior, timeout rendering unit matrix. Review: OK, no blockers;
should-fix (dup extraction) and low items landed. Verification: 975/975
(fabro-server + fabro-slack), clippy clean, fmt clean.

Deviation from the seed's example name ('question.pending'):
documented in the design section — the real event name adds zero
vocabulary; an alias can be layered later if desired.

title: engine: interview question channel per scope (route/workflow) instead of one global default
description:
Channel topology decision (user, 2026-08-27): #dev-fabro (product loop + HITL questions), #fabro-revisor (meta level), #fabro-ops (tests/infra). Notification routes already support per-route channels; interview questions do NOT — the server posts EVERY question to the single server-wide server.integrations.slack.default_channel (server.rs InterviewStarted handler). With multiple scopes this mixes unrelated grilling rounds in one channel.

Requirements:
- Question posting follows a scope: EITHER the run's notification route channel (new optional key on NotificationRouteSettings, e.g. questions = true) OR a per-workflow setting; the global default_channel becomes the fallback when nothing matches.
- Thread registry and answer processing stay channel-agnostic (they already are).
- Answer identity (Principal) unchanged.
- Twin tests: question posted to the route channel when configured; falls back to default channel otherwise; answer from the scope channel resolves the pending interview.

Prerequisite for the workflow-revisor's grilling rounds landing in #fabro-revisor (fabro-c74f, ADR-0011); not blocking the revisor build (questions would land in #dev-fabro until this ships).

title: world merger: develop+revisor onto the merged world, fabro as product (one-time migration)
description:
THE one-time world merger (ADR-0013): develop + revisor move onto the merged world, fabro becomes the product, denkhaus-lab and meta/denkhaus-lab retire. This seed holds the hard prerequisites so they stay visible while the revisor is built. NOT started before the revisor loop is proven (>=2 revisor cycles filing seeds that develop implements).

Prerequisites:
- Rust quality gate in the product sandbox: the runner image needs the Rust toolchain (cargo +nightly pin, clippy), and `just qualitygate` on the fabro repo must pass inside the sandbox within the tester timeout. Adjacent: fabro-199a (build-context for dockerfile builds). Cold-compile budget must be measured; the tester timeout may need raising or a warm-cache strategy.
- Tracker consolidation: lab tracker + platform tracker merge into ONE product tracker on the merged world (ADR-0012); open engine seeds move with it; sd sync across the move.
- Develop workflow adaptation: prompts/evidence.nu tuned for Rust diffs (diff size, module paths), qualitygate contract documented in the seed briefs the planner writes.
- Revisor moves with it: revises scope, run archives/bookkeeping (.fabro/revisions) survive the branch merge; cron scheduled only after the merger settles.

Done when one develop run on the merged world implements a product seed (Rust change) green through gate+review, the revisor runs against it, and the old worlds are frozen.

MERGE NOTE 2026-09-03 (upstream v0.345.0-nightly.0, merge 6530c724f): upstream PR #831 makes `fabro run`/`fabro create` create runs from immutable workflow intents and STOPS transmitting project-level `[run]`+`[environments]` settings (warning only). develop/revisor run behavior currently lives in denkhaus-lab project.toml (prepare, model, run/meta branch push, pull_request auto-merge cycle, integrations, slack notifications) — manual CLI starts on v0.345 silently lose ALL of it (falls back to server `default` environment, no prepare, no merge-back). Placement is server-authoritative now (pin_workflow_environment_authority clears provider/image from the workflow layer); the deployed server already carries `mise` and `toolchain` environments. NEW PREREQUISITE: run behavior must migrate to workflow.toml-form (see follow-up seed filed 2026-09-03) BEFORE the two revisor qualification cycles — manual starts otherwise break the merge-back cycle and pollute the loop measurement. The merger target form is unchanged: workflow-owned run behavior + server-managed environments; this merge just forces it earlier than ADR-0013 planned.

title: engine: prove fabro_ask end-to-end on the wire (twin run stage -> ClientBackend -> server SSE) + analyst session model/tools sentinel
description:
Spec-review follow-up for fabro-0c32 (2026-08-31). MUST land before the first revisor use (fabro-c74f).

Gaps from the spec review:
1. No test drives the full chain Stage -> ClientBackend (create_ask_session / submit_ask_turn) -> real server SSE stream. The ClientBackend ask path has zero coverage; only AskTurnCollector unit tests with hardcoded event-name strings (names verified against fabro-types + CLI, residual risk moderate).
2. The seed's sentinel requirement "model/tools arriving at the analyst session" is not asserted for worker-created sessions (only inferred from the shared handler code).
3. Weak sentinel: executor mock recorded created_since.is_some() (fixed in 0c32 final: records the parsed value — verify).

Done when: a twin (or scripted-LLM) workflow stage declares inspects and receives a real analyst answer through the actual HTTP path, with the analyst session's model + toolset asserted, and cross-workflow targets rejected on the wire.

---

## Rig available (2026-08-31, fabro-b5bd)

The hermetic Ask-Fabro test scaffolding needed for this seed landed
with fabro-b5bd (edbc84cfd): jwt_auth_state_with_openai_base_url
(test_support.rs), the Responses-API SSE httpmock body, the
ServerDaemon fixture record, and a terminal-run event sequence
(RunCreated -> ... -> WorkflowRunCompleted with SandboxInitialized).
Extend it: (a) prove fabro_ask returns the analyst answer through the
REAL ClientBackend on the wire, (b) assert the analyst session's
model + toolset sentinels, (c) for the sandbox-stop proof either a
Started-reporting sandbox fake (needs a reconnect injection seam) or a
Docker-provider rig asserting the container stops after the turn.

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code)

Test-level work only (no production changes expected). One server test
in tests.rs, modeled on the b5bd rig:

1. Spawn the jwt-auth router on a real socket (axum::serve on
   127.0.0.1:0 — the WorkerControlWsTestServer::spawn pattern) so the
   REAL fabro_client::Client can connect with the worker credential.
2. Worker token with inspects=["develop"] issued from TEST_SESSION_SECRET
   (issue_test_inspects_worker_token).
3. Target run: terminal, workflow_slug "develop", Local sandbox instance
   (b5bd event sequence).
4. fabro_tool::ask_run through ClientBackend::new(Arc::new(client)) with
   an httpmock Responses-SSE LLM -> assert the returned answer text.
5. Analyst session sentinels ON THE WIRE: the LLM mock asserts the
   request body carries the resolved MODEL id and the analyst toolset
   (fabro_run_events/fabro_run_get/fabro_run_logs/read_file/grep/glob)
   and NOT write_file/shell (AskFabroToolAccessPolicy + ASK_FABRO names).
6. Cross-workflow wire rejection: (a) ask_run with a nightly-slug target
   -> client-side scope error (quick re-assert), (b) DIRECT
   client.create_run_session on the nightly run with the
   develop-inspects token -> server 403 (RequiredAskFabroActor +
   ensure_worker_may_ask) — the wire-level authz proof.
7. Item 3 (created_since value sentinel): already fixed in 0c32 final —
   verify the api.rs test asserts the parsed timestamp (no new work).
8. Sandbox-stop wire proof: OUT OF SCOPE here — Local always reports
   AlreadyActive and reconnect_for_run has no fake seam; the decision
   fn is unit-tested and the stop call sites are guarded. Residual
   documented; a Docker-provider rig can cover it later if the revisor
   ever runs Daytona/Docker targets through fabro_ask.

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit 7157f991b)

Done-when satisfied at the strongest level available hermetically: a
spawned axum router + real worker-credentialed fabro_client::Client +
ClientBackend + ask_run returns the scripted analyst answer; the strict
LLM mock carries model + toolset sentinels (positive AND negative:
quoted write_file/shell/spawn_agent excluded) as matchers — one hit
proves the whole sentinel set; cross-workflow rejected client-side and
server-side (403 'Access denied.').

Findings worth keeping: (1) two same-named TEST_SESSION_SECRET constants
(test_support hex vs server::tests text) — worker tokens validate
against the state's secrets, user JWTs against jwt_auth_mode()'s key;
jwt_auth_state_with_openai_base_url now takes the secret as a parameter
and documents the trap. (2) Native analyst tools serialize under the
profile's own vocabulary on the wire (read-family), not canonical
names — wire sentinels for tool names must be profile-tolerant or
quoted-canonical-negative. (3) Sandbox-stop wire proof stays open
(Local always AlreadyActive, no reconnect seam) — decision fn unit-
tested; revisited only if the revisor ever asks Daytona/Docker targets.

Review: BLOCK (missing negative sentinels) fixed + consolidation done.

title: Graph-level retry policy with backoff config and node-level override for stage retries
description:
Stage retries today (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/retry.rs) support node attributes 'retry_policy' (presets: none/standard/aggressive/linear/patient) and 'max_retries', plus a single graph attribute 'default_max_retries' that sets only the attempt count. The backoff shape is hardcoded (initial 5s, factor 2.0, cap 60s, jitter) and presets can only be selected per node.

Gap: transient provider errors (e.g. zai 429 rate limits) can hit ANY LLM node in a workflow, so the retry default belongs at workflow level. Today every LLM node repeats 'retry_policy=standard' manually (see revisor graph nodes select/analyze/file in run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319); forgetting one node silently leaves it without retries.

Demand: declare a retry policy once at graph level (preset name, and optionally explicit backoff attributes initial_delay/factor/max_delay/jitter), applying to all nodes. Node attributes override the workflow default for special cases. Precedence: node retry_policy > node max_retries > graph retry_policy/backoff > graph default_max_retries > none. Exponential backoff with jitter already exists (fabro_util::backoff) and should stay the default shape.

title: Long-window rate limits defeat count-based retries: honor provider reset times or park-and-resume
description:
Evidence: run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 burned its full stage retry budget (5 attempts, exponential backoff 5s..40s, ~2 min total) against a zai 429 whose usage window reset only hours later ('Usage limit reached for 5 hour. Your limit will reset at 2026-09-03 05:35:16'). The provider sent retry_after=null; the reset timestamp exists only inside the error message text. Three nested retry layers (agent.llm.retry x3, stage retries x5) all exhaust quickly against a multi-hour window, then the run soft-exits.

Count-based exponential backoff cannot bridge multi-hour provider windows: the delays are far too short and the attempt count exhausts within minutes while the limit stays.

Fix directions to evaluate: (1) parse provider reset/retry-after hints (header AND message text) and cap or extend retry delays accordingly; (2) a wall-clock retry budget option (retry until T) instead of/in addition to attempt counts; (3) park-and-resume semantics: on a long-window 429, park the run in a resumable state with a scheduled wake-up instead of exhausting retries and exiting. Related: fabro-18a5 (soft-exit runs cannot be resumed), fabro-83af (graph-level retry defaults).

EVIDENCE 2026-09-11 (integrate batch, recurrence confirmed same day): midday conductor passes on the second machine died on ZAI 5h-usage-limit 429s (conductor 01M269AXA and 01M26H7ZCA46 at 12:00/12:30 Berlin; merge child 01M27V6 at 11:27 — handoff fabro-91bf). None were resumable after the quota reset: recovery required manual new passes (13:20 API trigger) and a 2h salvage for merge child 01M2837. Code status at 23:5x Berlin: fabro-llm default_retry_policy = 3 attempts with backoff capped at 5s (client.rs); 429 maps to ErrorKind::RateLimit and Retry-After is parsed (gateway.rs), but retry exhaustion fails the run hard (workflow_error) — no park. Engine resume primitive exists (operations/resume.rs, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/start {"resume":true}) but has the documented re-park trap when a routing decision already committed (see fabro-7627 engine part), and nothing triggers it on provider recovery. Priority raised P2->P1 by user decision 2026-09-11 ~23:59 Berlin; user ordering: this seed first, then fabro-7627 (manual resume UI+rewind). PRIORITY NOTE: raised P1->P0 by user decision 2026-09-12 00:29 Berlin to jump the develop queue — recurring unrecoverable outage class with same-day recurrence; user ordering: this seed next, then fabro-7627 (dep edge already in place).

title: rewind/fork UX: starting a fork with checkpoints ends terminal failed(terminated) — queue forks in resume mode or auto-switch
description:
Scope NARROWED 2026-09-03 after verification on merged v0.345.0-nightly.0 (merge 6530c724f): upstream PR #838 fixed the crash-loop half — see VERIFIED below. What remains is fix direction (1): the happy path. `fabro rewind`/`fabro fork` produce a fork that CARRIES checkpoint history, but `fabro start <fork>` queues Start mode, hits the checkpoint precondition, and the fork ends terminal failed(terminated) within seconds. The rewind output already prints the correct recovery hint ("To resume: fabro resume <fork-id>"), so the remaining work is UX: queue forks in Resume mode by default (or have start auto-detect checkpoint history and switch), so users do not have to know the mode rule. Fix direction (3) (respawn backoff) is obsolete — no respawn happens anymore.

Original report: after 'fabro rewind 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 @41' (fork to 01M1JX979PTSZRZ10ZCTMJA34E), 'fabro start <new-run>' produced an infinite worker crash loop: every worker invocation died with 'Precondition failed: checkpoint already exists in the run store — did you mean to resume?' and the scheduler respawned it ~10x/second for minutes. Root cause: forked runs carry checkpoint history; queue_run_start (lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/lifecycle.rs) selects RunExecutionMode::Start for non-resume starts; operations::start refuses runs with existing checkpoints; the worker-exit failure event was rejected ('invalid status transition: runnable -> failed(terminated)') so the run stayed Runnable and spawn_scheduler retried forever. Correct recovery was 'fabro resume <fork-id>' (mode Resume), which worked.

VERIFIED 2026-09-03 on v0.345.0-nightly.0 (server built from merge 6530c724f): reproduced the exact scenario — unarchived 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319, `fabro rewind ... @41` -> fork 01M1MG3JYMZ8DJW0G09QXKEH0Z, `fabro start` -> ONE worker invocation, worker stderr shows the precondition failure, run persists as terminal failed(terminated) (~4s from start to terminal; server log shows a single worker control-stream, zero respawns; second start attempt correctly rejected 409 'status is failed(terminated), expected submitted'). Both test runs re-archived afterwards.

title: Designed loops exhaust per-node max_visits and fail as workflow_error 'stuck in a cycle'
description:
Evidence: revisor run 01M1JXPAABBQ3TM3DJ2DQ1VZDW (forked from 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 at checkpoint @41) resumed cleanly, ran select@11 successfully (selected target 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V), then terminated as failed/workflow_error: 'node "analyze" visited 10 times (node limit 10); run is stuck in a cycle'. The original run would have hit the same wall one stage later even without the zai 429 — the budget was already spent after 10 completed revision cycles.

Problems: (1) the revisor graph (digraph Revisor) is a designed loop with a natural end ('Nothing to revise' edge), but per-node max_visits (analyze=10, file=10, select=15) turns a healthy, still-productive loop into a hard workflow_error once the budget is gone and backlog remains — 'stuck in a cycle' is misleading for a loop that is making progress each visit; (2) node visit counts persist across fork/resume, so forking a long-running loop near its budget cannot continue it at all — the fork burns a cycle and dies; (3) there is no graceful 'budget exhausted, park and re-enter next pass' terminal state distinct from an error.

Fix directions: distinguish progress-making loops from true cycles (e.g. only fail as stuck-in-cycle when a node repeats without forward state change / same failure signature), or add a designed 'budget exhausted' exit kind (soft/boundary) so loops can park resumably, and/or revisit the revisor graph's per-node caps (graph max_node_visits=30 already bounds the run).

title: Per-node skills and memory scoping for agent stages
description:
Evidence: revisor run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 — every agent stage carries ~50 skill descriptions (~1.5k tokens) plus AGENTS.md memory (5.3KB) in its system prompt, regardless of need. Validation pass 01M1M568F5BZ9F17T3SFGRDCZ3 (2026-09-03) proved node attribute project_memory=false is INERT for agent nodes: AgentSession::initialize (lib/components/fabro-agent/src/session.rs ~line 625) calls discover_memory unconditionally; project_memory only gates the older prompt-handler path (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/prompt.rs line 68). select/analyze still loaded AGENTS.md (5307 bytes, budget 32768) with the attribute set.

Demand: thread per-node scoping into the AGENT session path, not just the prompt handler. Cover BOTH: (a) memory — honor project_memory=false (or a dedicated memory=false) in AgentSession::initialize/AgentConfig; (b) skills — a per-node attribute (skills=false or skills=<dir>) to disable or scope skill discovery (AgentSession config already has skill_dirs, node-level override is missing). Both analogous to fs_hide/fabro_tools. Benefits every tool-light workflow stage.

title: Enforce journal keys in the routing output schema (painpoint mandate has no teeth)
description:
Evidence: develop prompts have mandated context_updates.journal with BOTH keys (painpoints, observations; empty valid, absence an error) since 2026-08-25 (fabro-e7c4) — yet the revisor run's journal analysis found exactly ONE painpoint entry across six develop-run journals (analyze@9: reviewers did the evidence-blob detour and logged zero). The mandate is prompt-level only; the routing output validator (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/structured_output.rs, routing_validator) checks routing fields but treats context_updates as an unvalidated object, so a compliant-looking routing JSON without journal passes.

Demand: extend routing_validator (or add a graph/node opt-in like journal_required) to require context_updates.journal.painpoints (array) and .observations (array) when the node declares it; a missing journal triggers the existing output_retries re-ask. Empty arrays remain valid — the point is that silence stops passing as success. Apply to develop planner/implementer/reviewer and revisor select/analyze/file.

title: Degrade on unsupported model control instead of dead-ending
description:
Configure fallbacks in the run's model settings and/or add engine behavior to retry once with the unsupported control dropped on api_deterministic/invalid_request. Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E had max_attempts=5 but will_retry=false and fallbacks = {}, so one parameter mismatch consumed the whole goal-gated run even though the error message contained the remedy. Expected effect: model swaps or control drift degrade a single call to defaults instead of failing the run.

DESIGN INPUT 2026-09-03 (zai probe, api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4): control vocabularies differ per model - glm-4.7 rejected enable_thinking=false with code 1210 naming its real vocabulary (low, high, max), while thinking:{type:disabled} was silently accepted-but-weakened; glm-5.3 honors thinking:{type:disabled} fully. A future generic reasoning-off control should map per model family (thinking.type for glm-5.3-class, reasoning_effort=low where thinking cannot be disabled), and api_deterministic errors carrying the remedy vocabulary (like 1210) are exactly the retry-with-control-dropped trigger this seed asks for.

title: Pre-install mise toolset in runner image
description: Pre-install the .mise.toml toolset in the fabro-runner:mise Dockerfile or mount a mise cache volume in the environment config. In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E mise install took 26.6s of the 28.5s setup on the purpose-built image for a run whose useful life was 1.5s. Expected effect: ~27s saved per run, mattering most for short or failed runs where setup dominated 2:1.

Migrate develop + revisor run behavior from denkhaus-lab project.toml into each workflow's own workflow.toml, required by upstream v0.345.0-nightly.0 (merge 6530c724f): `fabro run`/`fabro create` create runs from immutable workflow intents and no longer transmit project-level `[run]`+`[environments]` settings (warning only). Start wrapper: manual starts MUST pass `--environment mise` — the intent's environment override sits above the workflow layer, so a workflow-level pin alone does not select it (run_intent.rs admission + create.rs default to DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT_ID). Verification: one manual `fabro run develop --environment mise` from a lab checkout that (a) shows the untransmitted-settings warning ONLY for remaining project keys (ideally none), (b) runs with the mise image and glm-5.3, (c) executes prepare steps, (d) opens and auto-merges its PR, (e) posts the terminal Slack notification.

title: gofib tests: replace per-flag opts() wrappers with one options-literal builder
description:
From run 01M1MHGS7PH26EP20B2RTAPN4G (implementer@3 observation): fib_test.go predates the newer flags (-step, -last); every flag combination needed its own opts wrapper (stepOpts, lastOpts, ...), and each future flag would add another. Composing flags in tests drifts toward wrapper soup.

title: engine: preamble context table breaks markdown with multi-line values
description:
The `## Current context` table (append_filtered_context_table, summary:high fidelity) inlines multi-line values raw into markdown table cells. Markdown tables cannot contain newlines, so every renderer breaks: rows after a multi-line value visually detach from the table. User report 2026-09-03, run 01M1MMK5C6B313SY70Y2EPKE82 implementer@1: current_seed_id and current_seed_title appeared "missing" because the multi-line current_seed_brief (acceptance bullet list) shattered the table around them.

Fix directions (pick one or combine):
1. Render multi-line values single-line (newlines -> " / ") in table cells; full value stays available via the context_read tool.
2. Emit long/multi-line values as a bullet list BELOW the table (compact-fidelity style) with a short first-line cell + pointer.
3. Extend the existing large-value demote path to also trigger on newline count, not just byte size, so blob-ref handling applies.

Acceptance: (1) a context value containing newlines renders as a valid single table row per key in every markdown viewer (web UI prompt view included); (2) current_seed_id/title stay visually adjacent to a multi-line brief; (3) no information loss for agents (full value still served by context_read); (4) unit test with a multi-line context value asserting one rendered row per key.

title: evidence: survive summary:high stage-renderer tail_lines cap (119 lines omitted hid the seed-work diff)
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NTS5XCXJ4V88M9MQWKD83G (analysis complete).

## Root cause (two truncation layers)

Layer 1 (OURS, working): evidence.nu self-budgets to 6.8k chars — the
output itself was complete and in-budget.

Layer 2 (ENGINE, the killer): summary:high's per-stage section renders
command output via tail_lines(...) — the reviewer's prompt received the
evidence section as '(119 lines omitted)' + tail, hiding the integrity
header and the ENTIRE main.go diff. Second cycle: 144 lines omitted,
identical rejection. The tool-less reviewer correctly refused to approve
invisible evidence twice; planner@3 correctly escalated Blocked (cycle
guard worked); seed fabro-8d26 remains open though code is verified.

## Fix (workflow side, within our control)

The evidence capture must fit the RENDERED budget, not the raw output
budget: tail_lines appears to keep ~the last N lines and drop the head —
exactly where our critical-first sections live.

1. Measure the effective rendered cap empirically (prompt #3 evidence
   section: ~119+visible lines -> derive chars).
2. Rearchitect evidence.nu: the reviewer's verdict-critical material is
   the DIFF — emit it FIRST inside command.output (tail_lines keeps the
   tail... so instead: emit ONLY a compact integrity header + diff
   tail-budgeted to the renderer's window, dropping our own nice-to-have
   sections) OR move review to a node that renders full output.
3. Engine-side (companion on denkhaus, update fabro-9467/fabro-e47c):
   per-node preamble scoping lets the reviewer see ONLY the evidence —
   no other stages, no renderer caps on the one input that matters.

## Acceptance

- a run whose seed-work diff is ~120 lines reaches the reviewer FULLY
  rendered (no 'omitted' inside the evidence section)
- reviewer approves a green-gate pass on visible evidence in one cycle
- fabro-8d26 (verified correct) closes on the next run

Update 2026-09-16 (occurrence 2, develop run 01M2MY1JY4MPAXD9KWFN675385, reviewer painpoint, beat 11): same class, sharper facet — the preamble's evidence capture compact-truncated 115 lines MID-DIFF ('(115 lines omitted)') with NO blob-ref marker at all, so the sessions.rs half of the seed-work diff was silently invisible to the reviewer (rescued by falling back to the git diff against the claim base; fabro-45bf two-site change). Cross-ref fabro-9837 (blob refs must state payload byte size): here the demote path did not even emit a marker — the truncation is unmarked, which is the worse arm. Evidence: journal on run branch fabro/run/01M2MY1JY4MPAXD9KWFN675385 (PR pending gate at time of writing).

Update 2026-09-16 (occurrence 4, develop run 01M2N4XEB1XQW4466CXB57YJ4K / PR #181, beat 20): stage-preamble capture truncated at the HEAD of the tester/evidence block (60 lines omitted) — hid most of the workflow.fabro and planner.md diff hunks; reviewer re-verified via shell. Fourth occurrence today; the class is now the single most frequent reviewer painpoint of the day.

title: planner painpoint claims must be verified — deliver via context relay, not stated files
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NTS5XCXJ4V88M9MQWKD83G.

## Failure

Planner@3's response claimed 'both painpoints are recorded in
/workspace/fabro/.fabro/run-painpoints.jsonl and mirrored below' — the
tool history shows only two `cat` reads (second: file missing), ZERO
write calls. The staged file never existed; the refiner correctly
delivered nothing; the two genuinely valuable painpoints (evidence
truncation, deadlock diagnosis) were lost with only prose remnants in
the run log.

## Fix (workflow side)

The prompt contract says 'append one JSON line to the staged file' —
the model claims the action without performing it (classic unverified
claim). Options:

1. planner.md: mandate an explicit verify step — after writing, `cat`
   the staged file and quote its line count in the response; the
   reviewer-side check: response claims must cite file line counts.
2. Stronger (engine, fabro-176b already filed): post-stage hook appends
   declared painpoints deterministically — no LLM relay to trust.
3. Short-term deterministic: a tiny pre-refiner command node that
   extracts painpoints from context.workflow_painpoints into the staged
   file (context is engine-verified, unlike claimed file writes).

Option 3 removes the trust gap without engine changes: implement as
`stage-painpoints.nu` between planner and refiner? Evaluate during
implementation; option 1 is the 5-minute stopgap.

## Acceptance

- a run ending with painpoint claims delivers matching rows to the
  mailbox (verifiable in painpoints.jsonl)
- planner responses that claim file writes without performing them are
  caught (verify-step or deterministic relay)

## LINK (2026-08-23): message-bus seed fabro-meta-8652

The trust failure documented here (planner claiming unwritten painpoint
files) is failure class 1 of three relay failures; the message-bus
concept replaces the LLM relay entirely (message_send tool with
engine-added sender provenance).

title: develop: stale-base awareness after publish_blocked runs (unmerged run-branch remediation)
description:
## Context

fabro-67e5 landed on the platform (denkhaus 7d4176995): a green graph whose
publish failed now terminates as succeeded(publish_blocked) with a
PublishFailed failure detail and remediation text; Slack sees run.completed
(not run.failed). The workflow side (graph, prompts, notifications config)
needed no structural change — verified 2026-08-25 against meta/denkhaus-lab.

## Problem

With auto_merge enabled, a publish_blocked run means NO PR was created (or
push failed entirely), so the run branch fabro/run/<id> holds work that will
never merge back. The NEXT run clones the stale base:

- the planner may re-implement work that already sits on an unmerged run
  branch (its verification-only path only fires when acceptance criteria
  happen to look satisfied in the stale worktree)
- nothing in the loop (prepare, evidence, closeout) surfaces that the base
  is behind unmerged run branches
- the Slack remediation is the only signal; nobody acts on it autonomously

## Candidate directions (decide together)

1. prepare step: detect unmerged fabro/run/* branches ahead of base and
   fail fast / annotate context (cheap git, deterministic)
2. closeout: when tracker_empty routes to exit, check for unmerged run
   branches and surface them in the terminal context
3. evidence: include 'branches ahead of base' in the capture so the
   reviewer/planner can see them
4. accept as-is: Slack is the human signal; document the manual remediation
   (open PR from fabro/run/<id>) as the run branch being the durability path

## Acceptance

- decision recorded (ADR or seed note) on which direction(s) ship
- if 1-3 ship: deterministic, no LLM, tested against a run branch ahead
  of base

title: Fix invalid reasoning_effort pin on planner node

Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E died 1.5s into the planner stage with invalid_request: model 'glm-5.3' does not support reasoning_effort 'medium' (0 tokens, will_retry=false), failing the run with 0 of 4 seeds touched. Expected effect: the planner's first LLM call succeeds and this exact failure class becomes impossible.

title: Validate node-level model controls at submit time

In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E the error was purely static (graph pins medium, provider allows low/high/max) but was only discovered after 33.4s of sandbox + setup. Expected effect: config-class errors fail in under 1s with the provider's exact message instead of a ~51s run costing a sandbox and a pushed branch.

title: Surface root-cause error in terminal run status

In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E the visible status masked the actual model-control rejection, which lived only in stage detail. Expected effect: run lists show an actionable root cause in seconds.

title: Scope skill discovery to workflow skills dir

Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E's agent.skills.discovered event pulled 36 skills (personal ones like ask-matt, scaffold-exercises) into a planner that only needs sd, adding discovery time and prompt bloat against a tight preamble_budget_kb=12. Expected effect: smaller preambles, less role-prompt distraction, and removal of the skill-token crash class the prompts defensively work around.

title: Skip empty checkpoint commits on failed runs
description: In the engine checkpoint path, skip commit/push when the stage diff is empty and the run has no retry target. After the planner failed (0 tokens, 0 files changed), run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E still spent ~14s on two meta snapshots, two empty commits (dfb266e, d99a357) and two remote pushes — over half the workflow wall time, producing only branch pollution. Expected effect: failed runs terminate within ~2s of their terminal stage with no empty commits to clean up.

title: Raise reviewer preamble budget from 12KB to 20-24KB

In this run two ~6.4KB evidence captures exceeded the 12KB budget and spilled to ~400-char previews, so reviewer@2 approved without ever seeing the diff; the resulting no-op rework cycle cost $0.209 and ~5 min (32% of the run).

title: Add planner->refiner Blocked edge and output variant

In this run planner@4 routed preferred_next_label="Blocked", the missing edge tripped the goal gate, and the run concluded workflow_error despite seed fabro-8d26 being implemented, gated green, and approved.

title: Mark seed fabro-d810 blocked-external with infeasibility facts
description: In the seed tracker, fix seed fabro-d810 (in .seeds/issues.jsonl via sd): add the dependency on the denkhaus fabro-29f7 rebuild sequence or drop its priority below implementable seeds and label it blocked-external, and paste the infeasibility facts (which fabro not found, no run-event store under .fabro/, no meta world) into the seed description. In this run ~2.8KB was mirrored into three prompts per pass and the reviewer received the list truncated — accumulation lossy at exactly the node told to restate it; also frees preamble budget to compound with the budget raise.

title: Projectize prime boilerplate with the real gate in AGENTS.md
description: In run 01M0QTNF6GWHGPKHSQ2Y2PB8CQ, planner@1 and implementer@1 each ran sd prime/ml prime and ingested ~5 KB of generic template including a close-protocol demanding bun test && bun run lint && bun run typecheck — commands that do not exist in this Go repo, whose gate is just qualitygate. Add a project-override note in AGENTS.md outside the tool-generated seeds-onboard markers: this repo's close protocol is just qualitygate, and bun-based prime instructions do not apply. Expected effect: removes wrong-stack misexecution risk and stops contradictory context in every agent stage.

title: Skip PR creation when the run diff is journal-only
description: Skip PR creation when the run diff is journal-only. Run 01M0SFEYVC9TD6MP816RHEBFQY verified its goal (6 of 6 seeds closed, 'Tracker empty' exit) with an 18-line journal-only diff, yet attempted a PR with auto_merge = true, hit a deterministic 403, and flipped to failed(publish_failed) — same 403 noted in the 01M0T9B7T6 review. Effect: no-op runs report success instead of failed, and no squash-merged journal churn into the base branch. CORRECTION (planner, run 01M2QBA0BYJK4B241YG5RPCZHG, stale-path fix): the seed originally named .fabro/project.toml [run.pull_request] — that section no longer exists there; pull-request config now lives per-workflow in .fabro/workflows/<slug>/workflow.toml [run.pull_request], and the actual skip decision is engine-side in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/pipeline/publish.rs around line 153, where only a fully-empty diff skips PR creation (journal-only diffs still push the branch and open a PR). The fix belongs in the engine publish path: treat a diff whose changed paths are all under .fabro/journal/ as empty for the PR-creation decision.

title: Stop re-rendering every past cycle in preambles
description: In the develop workflow preambles, render only the latest visit of command stages in reviewer/implementer preambles and clear consumed context keys (review_feedback, review_verdict, stale implementation_summary) after the planner handles them. Run 01M0SS23MJM8972CBJD0SP7T4Q preambles grew 12.4KB to 21.9KB across cycles, blowing the 12KB budget; with max_visits=20 cycle 5+ would be unreadable. CORRECTION (planner run 01M2NF7QDW, stale-basis intermediate case): the capability does NOT exist engine-side, so a pure .fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro edit cannot deliver it — lib/components/fabro-workflow (stage-history preamble builder around handler/llm/preamble.rs plus context store) has no latest-visit-only attribute and no consumed-key clearing. Implementation: (a) add engine support for rendering only the latest visit of a stage's history section (e.g. a node-level attribute alongside preamble_stages_ignore) and/or a mechanism to clear consumed context keys after a consuming stage reads them; (b) wire it into .fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro for the reviewer and implementer nodes so repeated tester/evidence sections across gate-bounce cycles no longer accumulate; (c) unit tests in the engine crate covering multi-visit history rendering and key clearing; (d) graph budget context: develop now sets preamble_budget_kb=48 and already ignores planner/implementer/reviewer sections on the reviewer, so the residual accumulation is repeated tester+evidence visits plus unconsumed review_verdict/review_feedback keys. Note: .fabro/ is fs_hide-bound for file tools — read/write via shell.

Also fix the PR-body JSON contract for glm-5.3 that the deterministic fallback masked. Effect: run status reflects loop outcome — that run closed seed fabro-e6df and pushed 13 commits yet reads as failed. closure note: satisfied via upstream merge 0cac5a8 (verified by run 01M2NA1Z3 / PR #187, revisor pass PR #188) — closed 2026-09-16 /integrate after the verification-only run left the claim dangling in_progress.
closeReason: satisfied via upstream: all five criteria landed through upstream merge 0cac5a8 (fabro-67e5 line), not this seed's own commit path — verified by run 01M2NA1Z3HS7QPQR8AEWZR3GDB (PR #187, verification-only), revisor-confirmed in PR #188. In run 01M0SS23MJM8972CBJD0SP7T4Q the stage-journal hook wrote 13 identical {"data": {}} files into every checkpoint diff, inflating the loop churn the evidence script reports (10 files +82/-1).

title: Skip metadata snapshots on non-agent stages

In run 01M0SS23MJM8972CBJD0SP7T4Q snapshots ran ~1.8-2.3s at all 13 checkpoints (~25s total) — free wall-time trim with no evidence loss on those stages.

title: Prioritize source files and enlarge diff budget in evidence capture
description:
In .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/evidence.nu, sort seed files code-first (source before docs) before the whole-file diff walk — line 229 currently sorts alphabetically so README.md (~1.3 KB) consumed the ~2 KB allowance — and raise OUTPUT_BUDGET from 6800 to ~7600 by trimming SPEC_CAP (2200). Update 2026-09-16 (line-watch close, beat 15): CLOSED as satisfied-by-verification. Run 01M2N1G834RTCSZNX7EK40G3SE (PR #177) claimed this seed verification-only and verified all three acceptance criteria against the current tree: diff-sort-key z:/a: prefixes in all three diff walks, OUTPUT_BUDGET replaced by HARD_CAP=128000 + EMIT_BUDGET=30000 chunked emission, per-seed full diffs with omitted-files disclosure (criteria met by the superseding design landed via sync commit 54b6fcf). The run's closeout did not record the close (tracker-hygiene gap, journal of revisor run 01M2N1RRTKXE) — this close completes it with the reason the tracker must carry (fabro-02c4).

title: Lint develop seeds for spec contradictions before tracker entry
description: Add a contradiction check at seed creation (where fabro-4f3e-style seeds are authored) comparing the spec's examples against pinned behavior in README/CONTEXT.md. Evidence: seed text said -start 'Default 0' while gofib's 1-based indexing is pinned by README/CONTEXT/tests; planner@1 burned 102.5 s inference and /bin/bash.067 deliberating it (~40% of planner time). Effect: ~1.5 min and ~/bin/bash.05 saved per ambiguous seed, one less source of reviewer ping-pong.

title: Compute pipeline progress from unique completed nodes
description: In the engine's progress projection, compute progress as unique completed non-meta nodes / total instead of cumulative stage completions against a fixed node denominator. Evidence: run 01M0T2GW0PTNF3CHNQKHER1271 implementer prompt read '0 of 5 stages completed' after the planner had completed; final projection said '6 of 5' because planner ran twice. Effect: honest, interpretable mid-loop progress numbers. SCOPE UPDATE 2026-09-09 (cycle dedupe): covers BOTH surfaces of the cumulative-vs-unique counting bug — the run-level progress projection AND the stage-preamble header ('Pipeline progress: 0 of N stages completed' with earlier nodes done; runs 01M1RF53Q, 01M219SFJ seq 73/150, 01M22PCGN4). fabro-a0e3 closed into this seed; implement once, close both surfaces.

title: Cap reviewer re-verification to capture-only judging
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/reviewer.md add a verification-economy clause: judge from the evidence capture; use tools only for claims the capture cannot show; never re-run a check whose exact assertion already appears in the diff. In the analyzed run reviewer@1 spent 61.0s of 62.2s active time re-running build, go test, go vet and README reproduction already pinned by exact-string test assertions and a green tester stage, finding zero discrepancies. Expected effect: review cycle ~62s down to ~35-40s, ~$0.02 saved per seed.

title: Whitelist implementer smoke checks and make spec re-fetch conditional
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md (a) replace 'a quick smoke check is fine' with a hard whitelist (build + affected test package only; never just qualitygate) and (b) make the step-1 sd show fetch conditional on a thin or ambiguous brief. In the analyzed run implementer@1 was 48% of run cost, ran the full gate plus live CLI checks later re-verified by tester@1, and its first tool call re-fetched the spec the planner had just distilled because step 1 mandates it while the Input section declares the brief authoritative. Expected effect: ~25-40% off implementer inference (~30-45s, ~bash.03 per seed) and the brief-versus-spec authority ambiguity disappears. FRESH EVIDENCE 2026-09-09 (review 01M22YZBNJ0): the step-1 re-fetch mandate is dead letter in practice - the implementer re-fetched a brief-verbatim seed again; the conditional must REWORD step 1 itself, not rely on the Input section's brief-authoritative note. CORRECTION (planner, run 01M2MTN5MJ17SA67M8N82HZMSE, against current tree): part (a) is largely satisfied — step 4 already fixes the ONE mechanical verification call to `just verify implementer` (scripts/verify.nu, fabro-6e7f) with a hard gate ban and crate-scoped policy; the phrase 'a quick smoke check is fine' no longer exists. REMAINING WORK: (1) step 1 of 'Your job this pass' still opens with an unconditional 'Re-read the seed requirements from `sd show <current_seed_id>`' — reword step 1 itself so the fetch fires only when the brief is thin/ambiguous (carry the Input-section conditional into step 1; do not rely on the Input note alone); (2) the verification-only line (~line 135) still says 'run a quick smoke check where cheap' — align it with the cost-tiered whitelist language.

title: Give the evidence node its own output context key

In the analyzed run tester wrote the gate log (checkpoint seq 199) and evidence silently overwrote it (seq 209) because both nodes share one key; the reviewer prompt already papers over the clobber, so it only failed to bite because everything was green. Expected effect: no last-writer-wins overwrite; on a red-gate bounce the gate result stays readable from context.

title: Add a review_notes channel for non-blocking findings
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/reviewer.md and planner.md: Approved JSON gains optional context_updates.review_notes; the planner folds them into a future brief or parks them as a low-priority polish seed. In the analyzed run the reviewer's only substantive observation (pretty branch calls Fib(seed) twice; a local var would suffice) was lost at approval because it was explicitly not a deviation and the painpoint channel covers loop friction only. title: Forbid brief duplication and empty-tracker double checks in planner
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/planner.md make the closing rule absolute (prose must not repeat the brief; routing rationale only) and move the sd-list restriction into the decision order (sd ready empty with nothing in progress means route Tracker empty; do not run sd list). Expected effect: about 1.5KB less carried context per cycle and one turn (~5s) off every terminal planner pass.

title: Render verification report only in implementer JSON summary
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md, state the per-criterion PASS/FAIL report lives only in the JSON implementation_summary and pre-JSON text stays one short paragraph. In run 01M0T9B7T6XNM1D7JNY35Y6H8K the implementer duplicated the report as markdown prose plus verbatim JSON (8,024 of 10,693 output tokens; implementer was 60% of run cost at $0.213 of $0.353), and both copies were re-read as preamble by reviewer and planner. title: Add deterministic post-approval seed-close node
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro, insert a command node on the reviewer Approved edge that closes the seed, checks sd ready, and routes empty-tracker to exit vs seeds-remaining to planner (Changes requested still routes straight to planner). In run 01M0T9B7T6XNM1D7JNY35Y6H8K planner@2 only mechanically closed fabro-8208 and listed an empty tracker (14.8s, $0.016 of LLM work). title: Include gate stdout tail in evidence capture
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/evidence.nu, append the quality gate's small stdout tail to the evidence integrity header. In run 01M0T9B7T6XNM1D7JNY35Y6H8K tester@1 output was 288 bytes yet reached the reviewer only as a blob ref, and the reviewer prompt explicitly excludes gate output, so reviewer@1 re-verified live (six re-runs, 97.5s, 25% of run cost).
