title: Auto-approve parent-spawned develop runs for trusted worker subjects
description: Extend the server auto-approve policy to trusted worker subjects on parent-spawned develop runs, closing the idle approval window. Basis: run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN sat pending(approval_required) from 16:36:39 to 16:38:58 — 2m19s, ~13% of run wall, doing nothing — even though conductor auto-approve landed same-day in commit 7fda512 (16:18 UTC); verify whether that commit's subject set covers this spawn path and extend it if not. Expected effect: ~2 min saved per run and no zombie-pending risk; the approval-TTL backstop is already filed as fabro-54f0, so this seed covers only the auto-approve mechanism. Basis: run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN, workflow version af625ca581c5947f51dfa5597eb67892e0bee5d71ae041130412d1a54873ce8e, commit ecbd4d47c4c6d3272035e535731bc14f61a20662
closeReason: VERIFIED COVERED by fabro-2e3c (aa5c598a9, landed same day after this seed was filed) — no extension needed. Evidence: (1) gate predicate in lifecycle.rs skips the parent-worker approval gate when ApprovalMode::Auto; (2) both spawn paths plumb auto_approve end to end: fabro_run_create tool spec -> manifest builder (manifest.rs auto_approve passthrough) -> server args mapping; (3) LIVE proof: conductor pass 01M1SQYDJMHS's merge child 01M1SR27KEJG (post-2e3c) ran run.created -> run.submitted -> run.start_requested -> run.runnable with NO approval_required window. The seed's observed 2m19s idle window (01M1S6VRWQMD) predates 2e3c. Conductor prompts already pass auto_approve:true on all three legs. Backstop remains fabro-54f0 (approval TTL).

title: engine: auto_approve not effective through the git-source intent path (children still wait approval_required)
description: Conductor pass 01M1S6MSV4 passed auto_approve:true on fabro_run_create (visible in the tool-call args); git_source::intent_from_spec maps it into RunIntentArgs.auto_approve, but BOTH children (develop 01M1S6VRWQ, revisor 01M1S9C1H8) still landed in pending/approval_required and needed manual approval (2026-09-05). The intent admission path apparently does not apply args.auto_approve as the pre-execution approval (the legacy manifest path filtered/honored it). Fix: create_run_from_intent admission must honor RunIntentArgs.auto_approve (set approval to Auto or record the approval event at admission). Blocks fully autonomous conductor children. Basis: runs 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN + 01M1S9C1H8XVVEEB62JQKPXKY3, commits 5f413bbc7/7fda51235.
closeReason: Fixed and production-proven (commit aa5c598a9): the start handler's parent-worker approval gate now honors the resolved approval mode — args.auto_approve=true (-> ApprovalMode::Auto) starts orchestration children directly; every other parent-worker spawn keeps the anti-runaway guard. Proof: conductor pass 01M1SQYDJMHSVJYMZB3C643K7J created merge-upstream child 01M1SR27KEJGNQ which went straight to running with NO pending/approval_required. 920/920 fabro-server tests green incl. new companion tests (auto_approve starts runnable; without the flag the gate still parks).

title: ci: prebuilt cargo-chef gate image on GHCR — cut dogfood-gate Rust time from 10-15min to ~5min
description: GitHub-hosted runners start empty: rust-cache covers deps only on cache hits (misses/evictions recompile everything) and never covers toolchain+nextest setup or the workspace itself, so dogfood-gate Rust runs take 10-15 min — and the conductor waits for that merge (direct line latency, observed PRs #28/#30). Wanted: cargo-chef recipe layer baked into a gate image pushed to GHCR; dogfood-gate runs in that container so dependency compilation and toolchain come from image layers. Rebuild the image post-merge on denkhaus (incremental via GHCR build cache) plus nightly for Cargo.lock drift. Expected: ~4-7 min per code PR. Basis: PRs #28/#30 gate timings, conductor passes 01M1S6MSV4/01M1SQYDJM.

title: web: automation pause button is a no-op stub — wire pause/resume to replaceAutomation
description: The Pause-schedule button on automation cards (apps/fabro-web/app/routes/automations.tsx, AutomationCard ~lines 169-176) has NO onClick handler: clicking does nothing, no request is sent, no state changes. The card is also blind to the schedule trigger's enabled flag: AutomationRow.schedule only carries the expression (findScheduleTrigger(a)?.expression), so the list shows the Pause button even when the schedule is already disabled and offers no resume path. Fix: extend AutomationRow with scheduleEnabled (findScheduleTrigger(a)?.enabled === true) and keep the raw Automation for the request body; make the button a toggle that calls automationsApi.replaceAutomation(id, revision, body) with the schedule trigger's enabled flipped (pattern: automations-edit.tsx:107 — If-Match via automation.revision, then mutate(queryKeys.automations.list()), toast on success/error, busy spinner like the Run button); Pause icon + 'Pause schedule' when enabled, Play icon + 'Resume schedule' when disabled; mark the paused schedule badge (amber 'paused') so the state is visible. Tests: pause sends PUT with schedule enabled:false, resume sends enabled:true, If-Match equals current revision. Observed live 2026-09-06: user clicked Pause for the conductor automation in the web UI, nothing happened; the schedule had been paused out-of-band via API (revision 32ea7dfb).
closeReason: Landed: AutomationCard pause/resume toggle wired to automationsApi.replaceAutomation (If-Match revision, schedule trigger enabled flipped), amber paused badge, busy spinner, toast on success/error; AutomationRow carries scheduleEnabled + raw; tests: pause PUT enabled:false, resume PUT enabled:true, If-Match revision, paused badge (3 tests, full web suite 719/719, typecheck clean).

title: Develop prompts: purge retired two-worlds framing, make project-agnostic for cross-project reuse
description: URGENT (user directive 2026-09-06). The develop workflow prompts still carry the retired two-worlds model that ADR-0013 (world merger d9138572c) removed: implementer.md says 'You build the PRODUCT — on this world that is the Rust workspace under lib/' and builds a whole 'Platform scope is off-limits' section on the product/platform split; planner.md and reviewer.md repeat platform/product carve-out language, fs_hide world bindings, and repo-specific path lists (.fabro/, .seeds/, .mulch/, .agents/, scripts/, justfile). Goal: ALL develop workflow prompts (planner.md, implementer.md, reviewer.md, plus workflow.fabro/workflow.toml attributes and scripts/*.nu that carry world language) reformulated GENERALLY and PROJECT-AGNOSTICALLY, so the workflow is reusable in another project with minimal effort (user directive: 'möglichst generell und projekt-agnostisch, sodass ein workflow mit nur geringen aufwand in anderen Projekten wiederverwendet werden kann'). Approach directions: (1) replace world-scoped scope rules with a single capability-based scope description driven by the per-node fs/tool envelope (ADR-0009 family), not product/platform prose; (2) externalize every repo-specific fact (path lists, tracker commands, gate commands, pinned toolchains) into workflow settings/context values or one PROJECT_FACTS block so prompts stay generic; (3) keep the stage contract (journal keys, PASS/FAIL reporting, seed workflow) unchanged — this is a framing/portability rework, not a behavior change; (4) sweep for 'world', 'platform', 'product', 'denkhaus', 'lab' phrasing and rewrite each hit. Verification: grep shows zero two-worlds phrasing; a develop qualification cycle still passes end to end. Basis: .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/{planner,implementer,reviewer}.md, ADR-0013 (repo docs/lab/adr/0013*), ADR-0009 stage-envelope family.

title: web: typecheck must cover test files — tsconfig exclude hides test-file type errors from CI
description: apps/fabro-web/tsconfig.json excludes **/*.test.ts and **/*.test.tsx, so 'bun run typecheck' (tsc) never checks test files while editors (VS Code TS server) DO surface their errors — observed 2026-09-06 with automations.test.tsx (teardown misuse + unknown-typed mock body): bun tests passed, typecheck green, user saw type errors in the editor. SECOND INSTANCE same day (PR #32 gate): the editor's NEWER TypeScript service offered a quick-fix 'ignoreDeprecations: 6.0' for a deprecation only TS 6.x knows; the value breaks CI's tsc 5.9 (TS5103) — editor and project TypeScript versions diverge. Fix: (a) typecheck-tests script/config (tsconfig without the exclude, bun-types for bun:test) wired into CI/typecheck so editor and CI agree; (b) pin the editor to the workspace TypeScript via .vscode/settings.json 'typescript.tsdk': 'node_modules/typescript/lib' so quick-fixes match CI; (c) then fix any pre-existing test-file type errors the widened check uncovers.

title: workflow: for_each item-limit test is timeout-marginal under parallel nextest load
description: fabro-workflow handler::parallel::tests::for_each_accepts_an_array_at_the_item_limit takes 3.6s solo but exceeds nextest's 6s default under full-suite parallel load (observed 2026-09-06: 1 TIMEOUT in a 1642-test run, passes solo). Trim the test's work or mark slow; not diff-related flake.

title: Decouple merge-upstream workflow prompt from the local /merge-upstream skill — workflow must run autarkic
description: The AUTONOMOUS merge-upstream workflow references the LOCAL user skill: .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/prompts/merge.md line 6 instructs the run agent to read .agents/skills/merge-upstream/references/conflict-policy.md FIRST and check references/touchpoints.md (line 9 repeats it per conflict class); line 20 names the manual skill as failure routing. Both sources have DIFFERENT meanings despite overlapping content: the workflow is the autonomous merge executor (conductor line, runs unattended in the sandbox); the skill (.agents/skills/merge-upstream/SKILL.md) is the USER's local entry point for manual merges (upstream report, workflow-change assessment, self-reflection — user directive 2026-09-05: `/iterate` and `/merge-upstream` are user entry points). Problems: (1) autonomy breakage — reworking the local skill silently changes autonomous behavior; (2) semantic coupling — platform/local surface owns content the product line depends on; (3) no ownership boundary for future edits. Wanted: workflow prompt fully self-contained — move/conflict-policy and touchpoints content INTO workflow assets (e.g. .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/references/*.md or inline prompt sections), zero reads of .agents/** from any workflow prompt; the local skill stays exclusively local with zero references to workflow prompt files; where content must exist in both, each copy carries a provenance note naming the other ('deliberate duplication — update both, ADR-0008 one-unit rule per source'). Line 20 may keep NAMING the manual skill as the human fallback (routing semantics), but must not depend on its files. Verification: grep -r '.agents' .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/ returns nothing; grep -r 'prompts/merge' .agents/skills/merge-upstream/ returns nothing; a merge-upstream qualification pass completes without touching .agents. Basis: .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/prompts/merge.md lines 6/9/20, .agents/skills/merge-upstream/SKILL.md, conductor merge-leg routing (ADR-0015).

title: Lint workflow-prompt tool-call JSON examples against the live tool schemas
description: Two consecutive conductor passes (01M1V7Q00XGJ 11:30, 01M1V9DXW8 12:00, 2026-09-06) burned 6+9 failed fabro_run_create calls because the leg-prompt JSON examples drifted from the tool schema: first the missing runs wrapper, then the missing REQUIRED CreateRunSpec.workflow slug next to workflow_source. Prompt examples are data; validate them mechanically. Wanted: a lint (revisor intake or qualitygate) that extracts fenced/inline JSON tool-call examples from .fabro/workflows/**/prompts/*.md, matches them to the named fabro tool, and validates them against fabro_tool::tool_definitions() schemas (or a unit test in fabro-tool doing the same for known example files). Non-JSON or shell examples are skipped. Verification: the lint catches both historical defects when run against the pre-fix prompt versions.

title: fabro_run_create: accept workflow_source-only specs (derive the slug) and reject slug/source mismatch verbosely
description: User design review 2026-09-06 after two consecutive conductor passes burned 6+9 fabro_run_create calls on payload validation: when callers systematically drop required fields, that is a boundary problem (payload validation + verbose errors + contract ergonomics), not a prompt problem. The prompt fixes (56a982d34, 462d033b3) were stopgaps; this seed is the durable fix. Wanted: (1) CreateRunSpec accepts workflow_source-ONLY payloads — the server derives the workflow slug from workflow_source.workflow (it already resolves the source server-side; mx-e21031); (2) when BOTH workflow and workflow_source are present and disagree, reject with an error naming both values (kills the drift class); (3) validation errors name the exact property path and expected shape (overlaps fabro-e4ac — implement together); (4) conductor leg prompts simplify back to the workflow_source-only form once accepted. Rationale: the natural caller payload is valid; redundancy invites drift; every future orchestration agent benefits. Basis: passes 01M1V7Q00XGJ merge@1 (11:30, 6 attempts), 01M1V9DXW8 merge@1 (12:00, 9 attempts), CreateRunSpec.workflow required vs workflow_source optional (create.rs:191-194).

title: engine: routing output_schema must constrain preferred_label to the node's outgoing edge labels
description: INCIDENT 2026-09-06, merge-upstream run 01M1V7XSV75BE92JZ0135SHQXK: the reviewer APPROVED (verdict text, merge commit 401e3ceb7 verified) but emitted preferred_label='deploy' — a value no outgoing edge knows. All conditional edges missed, the unconditional soft fallback 'Unrouted review outcome' fired, and the run parked failed(soft_stop) with ~50 min of reviewed merge work stranded on the run branch. output_schema='routing' accepts free-form preferred_label. Wanted: the routing schema validates preferred_label (and any label fields) against the node's outgoing edge labels; on an unknown label, fail the OUTPUT (not the run) with output_retries, error naming the offending value AND the allowed labels — the boundary-first principle (fabro-e4ac class): systematic agent misuse = validation gap, not prompt material. The prompt stopgap (review.md strict routing) landed same day; this seed is the durable fix. Also consider: an unconditional edge without kind should be a graph-validation warning when it is the only unrouted-label catcher (a silent soft park is the most expensive routing failure).

title: web: run status header should render soft_stop (and deadlock/cancelled) distinctly, not plain 'failed'
description: User observation 2026-09-06 on run 01M1V7XSV75BE92JZ0135SHQXK: the status header shows 'failed' although the run parked at a kind=soft exit (reason=soft_stop, work preserved, next pass re-enters autonomously) — indistinguishable at a glance from a hard failure. Wanted: status chip/title renders soft_stop as amber 'soft-stopped' (and deadlock as 'parked — needs human', cancelled distinct from failed), with the failure reason visible without opening the log. ALSO (spec review of fabro-54f0): make failed(approval_timeout) runs visible in the pending/failed list surface — the 54f0 seed's 'surfaced in the UI pending list' requirement was API-side only; this seed owns the web rendering including approval_timeout.

title: engine: automation circuit breaker — pause the schedule after N consecutive identical failure signatures
description: Autonomous-operation gap observed 2026-09-06: three conductor passes parked soft_stop in a row (12:00, 12:30, 13:00 — first a merge routing park, then 2x zai 429 quota exhaustion) and nothing stopped the 30-min cadence. Nothing counts repeated parks; the line happily repeats work or burns sandbox spin-ups all night. Wanted: per-automation consecutive-failure tracking keyed on failure.signature (e.g. api_transient|zai|rate_limited) or (workflow, park-reason); when the SAME signature parks N consecutive automation runs (default e.g. 3), the scheduler pauses the schedule (visible state, like the pause button) and emits ONE aggregated notification (Slack lifecycle exists) naming signature, count, and last run — instead of N single failed-run notifications. A human resumes deliberately; resuming resets the counter. This is the autonomous line's blast-radius limiter for every unknown park cause (routing defects, provider outages, sandbox issues).
closeReason: LANDED via PR #32 (96d88e536, squash) — manual finish of parked run 01M1VZTJSZ551NFPHPD429MG0: per-trigger breaker state (signature, consecutive count, high-water run id, paused_at) persisted on automation_triggers with configurable threshold (NULL = engine default 3) + migration 2026090601; scheduler pauses a trigger after N same-signature terminal failures, resets on success, one aggregated notification (Slack blocks) instead of per-run spam; OpenAPI + TS model for breaker_threshold. Implementation by the develop workflow (planner/implementer/tester green); manual completion: verification (921/921 server, 551/551 automation/store/api, clippy incl. --features test-support), rust-style-guide review (state machine = persisted runtime state; 3 lint findings in test_support fixed), evidence-cause fix (fabro-ad23 emit helper) included in the same PR. Note: the orphan run originally died in the evidence stage BEFORE its reviewer — the manual review in the PR body substitutes.

title: engine: automation honors provider rate-limit reset windows (skip fires until quota reset)
description:
Observed 2026-09-06: zai 429 code 1308 'Usage limit reached for 5 hour. Your limit will reset at 2026-09-06 21:11:07' — the reset timestamp rides the raw error body, yet the conductor automation kept firing every 30 min and parking in survey until reset. Cheap (429 fails at open, zero LLM tokens) but pure noise: failed runs, sandbox spin-ups, alert spam. Wanted: when a run parks with a provider rate_limit signature carrying a reset timestamp (parse from detail.raw), the automation scheduler suppresses fires until reset+grace (state visible in the automation); first fire after the window resumes normally. Complements the circuit-breaker seed (this is the KNOWN-cause fast path with an exact ETA). FRESH EVIDENCE 2026-09-10 (line-watch): real 5-hour zai window exhausted at ~12:00 local; three conductor passes soft-parked on the survey LLM call ('Usage limit reached for 5 hour... reset at 2026-09-10 18:12:25 UTC'), the breaker paused the schedule (consecutive_count 3, paused_at 10:02:30Z) and NOTHING re-enables it at quota reset - the line stays down ~8h unless a human re-enables the trigger. This is the concrete resume gap.

DESIGN DECISION 2026-09-12 ~01:05 Berlin (user): DROP reset-timestamp parsing as the primary mechanism. Provider reset timestamps are timezone-untrustworthy — observed 2026-09-11 (handoff fabro-91bf): ZAI reported 'reset at 13:14:50' which was Beijing time, read as Berlin time = 6h off; a general solution must work across providers of any timezone and labeling discipline. PRIMARY MECHANISM: exponential backoff on the rate-limit failure signature at the automation-scheduler level — each consecutive rate-limit park doubles the fire-suppression window (e.g. base 30m -> 1h -> 2h -> 4h, cap ~6h), auto-resume fires after the window, first success resets the backoff. Builds on the landed per-trigger breaker state (fabro-3d97). Timestamp parsing stays OPTIONAL as a cross-check hint only when the provider includes an explicit UTC offset/label. Acceptance: repeated provider outages of unknown ETA converge to skipped fires without timezone assumptions; deterministic no-LLM runs are unaffected (suppression keys on the rate-limit signature, not generic failure).

DESIGN REFINEMENT 2 2026-09-12 ~01:1x Berlin (user): backoff growth is capped at ONE fire interval (30 min) — never suppress probes longer than the cron cadence. Waiting hours past the real reset wastes productive time and the true ETA is unknowable (timezone-untrustworthy timestamps). The waste to eliminate is NOT the 429 probe (fails at open, zero LLM tokens) but the per-probe collateral: run records, sandbox spin-ups, alert noise. REVISED MECHANISM: cheap pre-fire availability gate — when the last run parked with a rate-limit signature, the scheduler skips run creation + sandbox provisioning QUIETLY (no failed-run record, no notification spam) while marking the trigger state rate-limited (visible in automation status); every fire (>= every 30 min) still probes by attempting/allowing the cheap path, and the first success resets to normal firing. Optional timestamp hint only with explicit UTC offset. Acceptance update: during a 5h provider window, zero sandbox spin-ups and zero alert spam, at most one cheap probe attempt per 30 min, and normal operation resumes within <=30 min of the provider actually being available.

title: merge-upstream: reuse a parked reviewed merge branch instead of re-merging from scratch
description: Observed 2026-09-06 (run 01M1V7XSV75B): ~50 min of merge+gate+review work (commit 401e3ceb7, reviewer approved all 13 touchpoints) parked on the run branch because the routing label missed (fabro-de4d). The next pass would REDO the entire merge — repeated nightly, each redo burns 40-60 min LLM for identical, already-reviewed output. Wanted (defense in depth beyond de4d): (a) the merge-upstream graph opens the run PR as PART of the approved exit path (before/independent of the final routing), so an approved merge always reaches auto-merge even if later routing parks; and/or (b) the merge stage's prompt starts by checking for an existing parked run branch of the same workflow whose reviewer approved (checkpoint/event evidence) and reuses/promotes that branch (PR) instead of re-merging. Either way: approved work never silently repeats.

title: engine: automation-spawned conductor runs carry no automation_id — overlap guard is blind, scheduler stacks parallel passes
description: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (2026-09-06, investigation): the automation tag IS persisted — scheduler-spawned conductor runs carry automation {id: conductor, trigger_id: schedule} in RunCreated (verified on 01M1VZR3AAWY and stacked pass 01M1W1EZ5WZ; second stacked pass 01M1W1HHCE showed None — CHECK why, possibly different creation path). The real gap: the conductor automation had on_overlap: None (= default Fire), so the existing fabro-09ea skip-guard was never consulted — three passes stacked while one ran. IMMEDIATE OPS FIX APPLIED: PUT replaceAutomation set on_overlap=skip (revision c9b0258770025888) — the guard now suppresses fires while a pass is non-terminal. REMAINING WORK for the line: (1) verify the next fire slot logs 'Scheduled fire skipped: overlapping run still non-terminal' while a pass runs; (2) investigate why pass 01M1W1HHCE lacks the automation tag (creation path audit); (3) consider making Skip the DEFAULT for scheduled automations (or at least require an explicit choice at creation) so unattended lines cannot stack by configuration oversight — small engine change + test; (4) surface on_overlap in the automations web UI.
closeReason: Primary defect was configuration, not code: 09ea's skip-guard exists and runs are tagged; the conductor automation just never had on_overlap=skip set. Fixed live via API (revision c9b0258770025888). The remaining engineering follow-ups ((2) untagged 01M1W1HHCE creation-path audit, (3) Skip-as-default + test, (4) UI surfacing) are re-filed as the updated description for a fresh seed by the revisor/line — see description.

title: develop: implementer (and reviewer) must load and validate against the rust-style-guide skill
description: User review 2026-09-06: does the develop implementer use the rust-style-guide? Facts: (1) ACCESS EXISTS — run sandboxes discover the skill (agent.skills.discovered lists rust-style-guide from /workspace/fabro/.fabro/skills); (2) the implementer prompt NEVER mentions it (no occurrence of style.guide in .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md); neither does the reviewer prompt — the binding Rust policy is invisible to the whole develop pipeline. The 2026-08-27 fabro_run_logs lesson (agent-side): a skipped guide load shipped two logic bugs that a guide-first pass would have caught at design time; the local iterate skill got a mechanical gate for exactly this — the develop workflow needs the same. Wanted: (a) implementer prompt: BEFORE the first Rust edit, read the skill's guidelines.md index and the pages covering the diff (name the pages in the summary as proof-of-work); validate the implementation against them; deviations are findings, not accidents; (b) reviewer prompt: the standards axis IS the rust-style-guide — load workflows/code-review-refactor.md plus the pages covering the diff under review; (c) keep it cheap: pages-on-demand only, no full-guide reads. Basis: implementer.md/reviewer.md grep (zero mentions), sandbox skill discovery events (e.g. merge run 01M1V7XSV75B seq 25), iterate-skill mechanical-gate precedent, fabro_run_logs postmortem.

title: engine: fabro_run_wait until=merged needs a gate-failure signal — OPEN PR with failed checks must not loop timeouts forever
description: Incident 2026-09-07 (conductor pass 01M1XCC9SP1YH38326ZCVJZT3J, develop child 01M1XCHJTDBJKZ31VFMY1KD61Q, PR #33): the develop child merged its work and enabled auto-merge, but the dogfood gate FAILED and a later base push made the PR DIRTY. The conductor leg waits with fabro_run_wait until=merged; ADR-0016 wait results are terminal|merged|closed_unmerged|timeout — a PR that is OPEN with failed checks (or DIRTY) matches NONE of them, so every wait returns timeout and the agent re-waits: 5 chained fabro_run_wait calls over 2+ hours with zero routing until manual repair (debug!-level fix + base merge pushed to the run branch, 09:3x UTC). Wanted: (a) the wait result gains a distinct reached value (e.g. 'blocked' or 'checks_failed') when the linked PR is open but its required checks concluded FAILURE, or its merge state is DIRTY/BLOCKED for a sustained window; (b) conductor prompts route that value to a repair child or park with a clear reason instead of re-waiting; (c) regression test: open PR + failed checks + until=merged returns the new value, not timeout. Related: fabro-94e8 (auto-rebase for stale bases), fabro-6a77 (branch-pushed-PR-failed completion semantics), ADR-0016.

title: Develop planner: pick only seeds assigned to fabro (sd ready --assignee fabro) — deterministic line/user ownership split
description:
GRILL SETTLED 2026-09-07 (user decisions in session):

DECIDED: (D1) The assignee filter for the develop workflow is APPROVED — 'sd ready --assignee fabro' becomes the planner's candidate source. (D2) The REVISOR ASSIGNS NOBODY: filing seeds is its job, ownership is NOT — revisor-filed seeds land UNASSIGNED in the backlog. (D3) Who executes a seed is decided JOINTLY by user + agent (cycle report / grill / chat is the forum; the agent's @fabro assignment is a proposal the user can veto by reassigning anytime). (D4) Fail-closed default (Opt-in): nothing belongs to the line until @fabro is explicitly set. (D5) Emergency channel stays as the standing user directive: when the line/engine is DOWN the agent repairs directly with the user's knowledge (no seed picker involved); the seed is filed retroactively for documentation. No emergency self-service class exists for the revisor or the line.

MECHANISM (line implements, from D1): (1) develop planner prompt candidate source: 'sd ready --assignee fabro --limit 200' (CLI pre-filters — the LLM never sees unassigned/user-owned seeds); (2) goal fast-path honors a named seed id ONLY when assignee is fabro; (3) claim: 'sd update <id> --status in_progress --assignee fabro'; (4) Tracker-empty on the filtered view = legitimate end of work (park) — while the backlog is unassigned the line does NOTHING rather than something; (5) docs/agents/issue-tracker.md documents: assignee is the ownership switch; filers (agent, revisor) file UNASSIGNED; assignment is a joint user+agent decision recorded in the cycle report; (6) revisor seed-intake prompt: remove any language implying the revisor decides execution — it only files.

OWNERSHIP (user decides, NOT the implementer): the existing backlog assignment list is a user+agent joint decision (category proposal from the agent, approval by the user); NO bulk-assign by the develop run. Sentinels (fabro-919b/fabro-80cc) stay until mechanism landed AND backlog curated.

Acceptance: planner prompt ships the filtered command; an unassigned or user-assigned open seed never appears in develop candidates; empty filtered view parks; revisor files unassigned; docs updated; ownership list untouched by the implementer.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) develop-leg routing must treat reached=blocked as 'merge pending', not failure: re-wait until=merged with a bounded deadline (e.g. 2-3 chained waits), and only route Failed on terminal-failed children (child status, not PR state); (b) after merged OR after child-terminal+parked-for-gate, ALWAYS run the revise leg; (c) backfill: the survey leg should detect completed develop runs without a revisor pass (no revisor journal/review artifact for the run id) and trigger a catch-up revise; (d) regression test: conductor graph routing on wait results terminal|merged|closed_unmerged|blocked|timeout maps blocked to wait-again/revise, never to the failed exit.

title: agent: edit-tool file writes land with mtime 1970-01-01 — cargo skips recompiles, edits silently lag until manual touch
description: From unreviewed run 01M1Y2SMEVDHAFB59GZV9B84CQ (PR #41 implementer; recovered via journal sweep 2026-09-07 after the run aged out of revisor freshness): edit-tool file writes landed with mtime 1970-01-01 (e.g. lib/components/fabro-validate/src/file_refs.rs), so cargo considered the sources older than cached rlibs and silently skipped recompiles — a just-added pub fn was reported missing and behavior lagged the edits until a manual touch. This is silent cache poisoning of the build loop: any agent edit can produce a stale-binary diagnosis that costs implementer revisits. Fix direction: the platform's file-write path (edit tool / sandbox write transport) must set a real mtime — utimensat/write-with-times after creating or replacing the file so downstream build systems see fresh sources. Acceptance: an edit-tool write produces mtime == wall clock (unit test on the write path); a before/after cargo check in a scratch crate recompiles after an agent edit without manual touch.

title: develop: verification-only briefs must not assert 'criteria satisfied' — derive per-criterion checks instead

The pass only converged because the implementer re-checked; a lazier one would have closed the seed on the brief's word. Fix direction: the planner's verification-only brief generation must not carry satisfaction assertions — instead list each acceptance criterion with an instruction to verify it against the CURRENT worktree and report per-criterion status in the summary. title: conductor survey: reword misleading 'burns the backlog down' claim — backlog journal is visibility-only, drain needs the revisor's newest-first rule to change
description: PR #45's survey prompt says 'the revisor revises the newest revisable run, so each subsequent pass burns the backlog down one run at a time' — but the revise leg creates the revisor without a goal and the revisor's select rule picks the NEWEST unrevised fresh run (which is always the current pass's own child), so the backlog NEVER drains; additionally the freshness rule (ADR-0015) makes older runs stale-evidence the moment the workflow version drifts, permanently disqualifying them. The journal line is dead-letter optimism (user + agent analysis 2026-09-07). Fix: reword survey.md to state the truth — the backlog entry is VISIBILITY-only (unreviewed run ids stay observable), runs are only revisable while fresh, and a real drain would need the revise leg to pass an explicit backlog run id in the goal (a decision not made). Do not promise behavior the graph cannot deliver.

title: Bake gh into the develop toolchain image (or check open PRs engine-side) so the in-flight-PR guard functions
description:
CORRECTED 2026-09-08 (user decision, ADR-0019): the gh-baking approach implemented via PR #53 was REVERTED (commit f00fdb102). WHY GH IS FORBIDDEN IN AGENT SANDBOXES: the engine injects a freshly minted GITHUB_TOKEN into every agent shell call (fabro-workflow services.rs resolve_workflow_env) plus a git credential bridge (git_bridge.rs) - combined with the gh binary this was a fully WRITE-CAPABLE forge client in every agent shell (merge, close, force-push, branch delete), bypassing every engine governance control (gate, revisor, auto-merge; fabro-github is the only sanctioned write path, engine-side). Baking a raw forge client into the agent image was a capability addition without a user decision - exactly what ADR-0019 now forbids: direct agent tools are read-only at most, extend existing tools over new ones, capability changes are needs-user. The guard's legitimate need (open-PR visibility) is solved credential-less via fabro_runs_list (fabro-06e0, Weg A). This seed stays CLOSED; the correction documents the revert and the prohibition rationale for the tracker record.

(original request: bake gh into the develop toolchain image so the in-flight-PR guard works; implemented as PR #53, reverted 2026-09-08)

title: Point reviewer phrase checks at read_file offset/limit when diff line numbers are known
description:
In .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/reviewer.md (tool-guidance/verification section), instruct the reviewer to verify phrase-presence claims with read_file offset/limit on the exact lines the diff already names — or pass an explicit max_results to grep — instead of multi-pattern grep alternations. title: develop planner: in-flight PR guard is credential-less and must STAY that way — use fabro_runs_list, remove gh from the toolchain image
description:
USER DECISIONS 2026-09-08: (D1) Weg A ONLY - extend existing surfaces, NO new tools; (D2) gh REMOVED from the toolchain image by direct revert (commit f00fdb102, capability change without user decision gets reverted per ADR-0019) - image rebuilt and verified (gh absent, sd/rg/just/nu + mise trust intact). SECURITY CONTEXT: the engine injects GITHUB_TOKEN + a git credential bridge into agent shell calls - so the brief gh presence was a write-capable forge client in agent shells, NOT a harmless unauthenticated binary as first assumed; the prohibition rationale is documented on fabro-05d0 and ADR-0019.

REMAINING WORK (this seed): (1) extend the fabro_runs_list AGENT TOOL projection with pull_request {number, state} - the projection is RunSummaryResult/run_summary_result in lib/components/fabro-tool/src/common.rs, which currently has NO pull_request field at all (planner-verified 2026-09-08; the OpenAPI HTTP Run schema already carries pull_request link and is NOT the surface to change). Live PR open/closed/merged state must be enriched engine-side, read-only, via the existing server GitHub client (same path as GET /runs/{id}/pull_request live details) - stored PullRequestLink (lib/foundation/fabro-types/src/pull_request.rs) holds only owner/repo/number. (2) The develop graph (.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro) declares no inspects, and fabro_runs_list refuses callers without it - add inspects covering the develop workflow (conductor precedent: inspects="develop,merge-upstream,revisor") and confirm the planner agent stage actually gets the runs_list tool. (3) Planner guard (.fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/planner.md step 4 IN-FLIGHT PR CHECK): replace the gh command with fabro_runs_list -> filter runs with open/non-terminal linked PR -> extract seed ids from run goals -> skip matching candidates, journal 'skipped: in-flight PR <n>', continue down sd ready --assignee fabro; remove the gh fail-open clause (no gh exists anymore - the guard must not reference it). Acceptance: a develop pass with a seed whose PR sits open in the gate journals 'skipped: in-flight PR <n>' and claims a DIFFERENT seed - verified live; planner prompt no longer mentions gh; no credential added; no new agent tool exists.

title: revisor + reviewer must become security-affine (ADR-0019): capability-affecting ideas get shot down at filing and review time
description:
USER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-08: 'der revisor und der reviewer muessen unbedingt sicherheits-affiner werden, sodass solche ideen von vornherein abgeschmettert werden' - the gh incident (PR #53 baked a forge client into the toolchain image; a follow-up seed proposed GH_TOKEN provisioning) only stayed harmless because credentials happen to be absent from sandboxes - luck, not design. The two autonomous gates must enforce ADR-0019 themselves.

FIX (1) REVISOR file stage (.fabro/workflows/revisor/prompts/file.md): add to the seed-intake rules - when a finding or proposed fix direction would ADD/CHANGE/REMOVE a tool, credential, or permission in an agent-reachable surface (Dockerfiles, environment env, tool allowlists, hook configs, new binaries): (a) the seed MUST carry labels needs-user (in addition to revision) and stay for user assignment per ADR-0018 D3; (b) the seed body must cite ADR-0019 and state 'implementation awaits explicit user approval'; (c) the revisor NEVER proposes raw authenticated clients or token provisioning as fix directions - engine-mediated, read-only, extend-existing-tools is the only vocabulary (ADR-0019.2/.3).
FIX (2) DEVELOP reviewer (.fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/reviewer.md): add a review axis to the checklist - CAPABILITY DELTA: if the diff touches .fabro/Dockerfile*, env/credential provisioning, tool allowlists, hook configs, or adds binaries/secrets to agent surfaces, verify the seed records an explicit user decision (ADR-0019 citation + approval note); without it, that is a BLOCKING finding -> route Changes requested naming ADR-0019 (a merged capability change without user decision gets reverted). Capability REDUCTIONS (removing tools/credentials, least-privilege narrowing) are fine and welcome - do not block those, just verify they cite their basis.
Acceptance: revisor files a capability-affecting seed with needs-user + ADR-0019 citation (verifiable on the next such finding); reviewer prompt carries the capability axis; one gate run demonstrates a blocking Changes-requested on a capability delta without recorded approval (test or staged verification).

ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE (2026-09-08): the gh incident was WORSE than first diagnosed - the engine injects GITHUB_TOKEN into every agent shell call (resolve_workflow_env) plus a git credential bridge (git_bridge.rs), so the baked gh was fully WRITE-CAPABLE (merge/close/force-push/branch-delete), not a harmless unauthenticated binary. The reviewers approved PR #53 partly because the per-tool-call env injection was invisible from a container-env perspective. The capability axis must teach reviewers to check what the ENGINE hands to agent shells (env injection, credential bridges), not just what the diff itself adds.

title: Drop current_seed_brief from the develop reviewer node's preamble_allow_keys
description: In `.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro` (reviewer node), remove `current_seed_brief` from `preamble_allow_keys`. Evidence from run 01M1YY8JJCE31XHSDCZ816634G: the reviewer preamble carried both the ~2.3 KB `current_seed_brief` and the 8.9 KB evidence capture whose own '== in-progress seed spec ==' section delivered the same spec twice; the duplicated payload blew the 24 KB aggregate inline budget, so the capture rendered as a `blob-ref` and forced a `read_file` detour (reviewer@1). title: engine: scrub clone token from sandbox remote URL — engine git ops switch to transient per-exec credentials (user decision 2026-09-08)
description:
MERGE NOTE 2026-09-12 (409a3e9dd) — PREMISE FUNDAMENTALLY CHANGED, needs a user re-decision:
Upstream #849's new clone model (fabro-sandbox/src/clone.rs) already implements the scrub half: the token travels with the clone PER CALL (-c url.<clean>.insteadOf=<token-url>) and the remote URL is never rewritten (tests assert no set-url, no persistent token in config). embed_token_in_url and push_credentials.rs no longer exist.
BUT the new model deliberately installs the minted token as the checkout's AMBIENT credential helper after cloning, so the AGENT's own git commands can push — the exact opposite of ADR-0019.6's 'credential-free sandbox' posture this seed decided.
Remaining decision: keep the strict posture ON TOP of upstream (do not install / scope the ambient credential helper; engine-side git goes through the driver's Git facet with per-exec credentials — the facet already tracks credential age for retry), or adopt upstream's ambient model and close this seed as superseded. Effort either way is now small compared to the original scrub+transient rework.
closeReason: RESOLVED 2026-09-12 (user decision, recorded as ADR-0019 item 8): the upstream ambient checkout credential is ACCEPTED as the sandbox's forge capability. Verified facts: token minted per-repository with contents:write ONLY (no PR creation possible from a sandbox); PR path uses a separate server-side token (contents+pull_requests); installation tokens are GitHub-fixed at 60min, engine refresh margin 10min; remote URL never carries the token (per-call insteadOf rewrite); store file umask 077 dies with the sandbox. Token revocation on teardown explicitly DECLINED; strict ADR-0019.6 posture superseded for clone/push. No per-agent credential scoping exists or is planned — the per-checkout store is the boundary.

title: revisor: scope seed WRITES to its own set — supersession closes and label changes never touch user-owned seeds (ADR-0018)
description:
USER FINDING 2026-09-08 (revisor prompt review): the revisor's seed WRITE operations are unscoped - the supersession rule (prompts/file.md) says 'a finding SUPERSEDES an existing open seed... file the new seed, then immediately sd close <old-id>' with NO ownership boundary, so the revisor could close USER-owned seeds (design forks like fabro-3b1b, grill topics like fabro-b11a, upstream-posture seeds) and thereby remove items from the user's decision space - an ADR-0018 violation (the revisor owns nothing; reviewing is not owning). READS stay GLOBAL (sd search against the full inventory is correct - duplication is assignment-orthogonal; scoping the search would CREATE duplicates against user-owned work).

FIX (prompts/file.md, sequence AFTER PR #59 which touches the same file): (1) supersession closes ONLY seeds labeled revision (revisor-originated set) or assigned @fabro; user-owned/unassigned seeds are NEVER closed by the revisor - when a finding supersedes one, cross-reference it in the new seed's description and journal 'supersession candidate (user-owned, not closed): <id>' for the human gate; (2) label backfill (--set-labels revision) only on seeds already labeled revision or provably revisor-originated (Basis cites a revisor run); (3) add one sentence to the tracker command reference table: 'ownership rule: close/relabel only your own or @fabro seeds - ADR-0018 D2'. Acceptance: prompt states the ownership boundary; a staged test or journal evidence shows a user-owned supersession candidate is cross-referenced, not closed.

title: fabro_run_wait until=merged returns blocked immediately — conductor misroutes slow-gate PRs in BOTH legs (merge: 'Merge child failed', develop: 'Gate stuck — revise anyway')
description:
ROOT CAUSE: `fabro_run_wait {"until": "merged"}` returns `blocked` within seconds while the PR gate is merely young (checks running, PR open). A blocked return therefore consumes no wall time, and any bounded re-wait chain over it degenerates: N waits burn in <60s against a gate that needs ~15 min. FLAVOR A (merge leg, original filing): the conductor misjudges a successful merge pass as 'Merge child failed'. FLAVOR B (develop leg, new evidence 2026-09-10 13:0x): the develop leg's fabro-1dc9 chain (3 waits, '~60 min ceiling') is ineffective for the same reason — conductor 01M25K0SNNZABSBAE4XJ5S0R4Y routed 'Gate stuck — revise anyway' at 12:58:13, 56 seconds after PR #121 was created (12:57:16, dogfood-gate pending, healthy). The pass soft-parked a young gate and started the revisor in parallel with the running gate. The 08:24/08:30 passes only looked correct because their gates merged within ~80s. Expected effect of fix: `blocked` must distinguish young vs persistently stuck — e.g. the wait keeps polling inside its timeout_ms while checks run (blocked only returns when the gate has actually failed or the wait budget is exhausted), or blocked returns carry gate-age/failed-checks signal the conductor can route on. Engine-side fix in fabro_run_wait semantics (fabro-workflow run-wait tool), not another conductor prompt patch: the 1dc9 re-wait chain cannot work while blocked returns are instant. Basis: runs 01M25K0SNNZABSBAE4XJ5S0R4Y (develop leg, PR #121, dogfood-gate pending at misroute time) and the original merge-leg report; 2026-09-10

FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-10 15:2x (line paused, direct agent repair, pending PR): lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/wait.rs gate_verdict() + fabro_github::list_check_runs_for_ref — blocked state counts as stuck ONLY with a failing check conclusion (failure/timed_out/action_required/cancelled) or a structural dirty conflict; young/pending gates and failed check-fetches keep polling until the deadline. 5 unit tests for the verdict table. Basis addition: commit pending on denkhaus.

WHY IT MATTERS: the ADR is the durable decision record; prompts get rewritten by every revision pass and are agent-reachable surface themselves. Reviewers, revisors, and future grill sessions cite ADR-0019 - if the record omits the engine-provided-credential class, the gate doctrine silently narrows back to container-env-visible capability on the next prompt rewrite (exactly the PR #53 blind spot the extension closed).

FIX: add one paragraph to ADR-0019 Decision section (or a numbered extension like .7) stating: engine-provided credentials and bridges (GITHUB_TOKEN injection, git credential bridge) ARE agent-reachable capability; diffs that use them on new code paths are capability deltas requiring recorded user approval; cite PR #68, run 01M20RK7XFNPJRZ2T437XGDEP8, and the fabro-16ff user directive (2026-09-08). Commit a4850e681 fixed this for the CONDUCTOR survey only ([run.clone] depth = 0 in .fabro/workflows/conductor/workflow.toml) - the merge children are their own workflow and .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/workflow.toml has NO [run.clone] section, so every merge child still rediscovers the trap. Each child run clones origin/denkhaus fresh at creation (conductor workflow.toml comment).

FIX: add [run.clone] depth = 0 to .fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/workflow.toml, mirroring the conductor commit a4850e681 (volume is ~neutral - the survey's unbounded git fetch upstream already pulls the full shared history into the shallow clone each pass, ~150 MB either way, measured). ADR-0019: this finding adds a binary to the agent-reachable toolchain image surface, so it is capability-affecting — implementation awaits explicit user approval. Fix direction stays engine-mediated (image build content / engine-managed cache mount; the prebuilt binary is the repo's own read-write CLI, no new credentials or external clients). Basis: run 01M2183254XQ3HJ45SR4P1Y2X6, workflow version 84429d0a3253eaa52e2406a04a3b97b4365d0ff68b0cdc2f46c296e8c05ec7a6, commit 0dc16012c16ee2f6b2e61ecc73afcf0bd5f26b3d

USER DECISION 2026-09-16 (release session, ~21:20 Berlin): approved — bake the fabro CLI into the toolchain image AND do it in ONE GO with the pending image release. RULE (user, same message): new images are built and pushed ONLY via `just image-release` — one unified path (it already chains scripts/image-release.nu + scripts/run-images.nu --push). IMPLEMENTATION: extend scripts/run-images.nu to stage the full `fabro` CLI binary from the same checkout (debug profile per the original demand) into .fabro/bin/, Dockerfile.toolchain COPYs it next to fabro-validate, and the existing content+binary hash gate decides rebuilds — no manual docker build, no separate push path. CAPABILITY NOTE (ADR-0019 transparency): unlike validate-only fabro-validate, the full CLI carries an HTTP client; run sandboxes hold no server token/auth.json, and the user has explicitly accepted this scope (decision above). Replaces the 'or shared cargo cache' alternative — the prebuilt binary is the chosen route. Priority raised: rides the CURRENT release window.

title: engine: conductor passes overlapped despite on_overlap=skip — double develop claim on fabro-8bf4 (PR #84 vs #86)
description:
Incident 2026-09-09 11:00-11:20Z (caught by line-watch): two conductor passes ran in PARALLEL although the conductor automation has on_overlap=skip — pass X 01M22X67GYXC (started ~10:53Z, still running at 11:20Z) and pass Y 01M22VF9PWJH (11:14-11:39Z). Their develop legs both claimed fabro-8bf4: X's child 01M22X87J1R planner at 11:02:37Z journaled the in-flight guard saw only PR #78 ('no skip needed'); its PR #86 opened 11:16:45Z (run end). Y's child 01M22VHABGCN claimed the same seed ~11:15Z - in the mid-flight window where the seed has NO open PR yet - and PR #84 merged first (396f5ca3e). Result: two green but overlapping implementations of one lint (envelope.rs/context.rs); PR #86 closed as duplicate. Cost: one wasted develop run (~15 min + LLM spend) + duplicate PR handling.

Two coupled gaps:
(a) OVERLAP SEMANTICS: investigate why on_overlap=skip admitted pass Y while pass X was active. Hypotheses: overlap check considers only actively-executing (not waiting/parked-on-child) runs; or the run_wait blocked-instantly misjudgment (open fabro-ee5d) made X look terminal to the scheduler. Reproduce from run states + automation trigger log.
(b) MID-FLIGHT BLIND SPOT: the planner in-flight guard (fabro_runs_list -> open run-linked PRs, fabro-06e0/c419) cannot see a seed claimed by a RUNNING develop run whose PR does not exist yet (~15 min window per pass). Fix direction: the guard must also exclude seeds claimed by running develop runs - fabro_runs_list already returns run status/workflow/parent - or the conductor must serialize develop legs engine-side so parallel claims are impossible.

Expected effect: the double-implement class (fabro-22e4 lineage) stays closed even under overlapping passes; no wasted runs/PRs. Evidence: journals of 01M22X87J1R (planner observation) and 01M22VHABGCN, PRs #84/#86, fabro ps -a timeline. THIRD SURFACE (line-watch 2026-09-09): the revisor reviewing the duplicate run at 11:21Z also missed it - its review (PR #87) never mentions #84/#86 because the run's basis predates #84's merge. Add to the revisor/analyst checklist: before distilling a develop run, check whether the run's seed is already closed on the base branch (duplicate-run detection), so a duplicate run cannot pass review as healthy.

title: PR staleness supervisor: HTTP 409 must not count as an update-branch strike (only 422 is a real conflict)
description: PR #99 (commit 10c77c927) maps BOTH 409 and 422 from the GitHub update-branch endpoint to PullRequestApiError::Conflict, and the supervisor counts every Conflict against MAX_UPDATE_BRANCH_ATTEMPTS=3 (pull_request_supervisor.rs). GitHub can answer 409 also while a previously requested update is still in progress ('merge conflict'-adjacent queue states), not only for genuinely unresolvable head/base conflicts. A slow gate (>5 min per 5-min poll) can therefore accumulate 3 strikes in ~15 min and retire a still-converging run PR as stale_base. Wanted: only HTTP 422 counts as a strike; 409 is journaled (warn) but tolerated, or the supervisor verifies queued-update completion before counting. Acceptance: wire test with 409-response asserting no strike increment + 422 asserting increment; existing cap/age tests stay green; clippy+fmt clean. Basis: commit-review grill session 2026-09-09, fabro-94e8 implementation review, PR #99. FRESH EVIDENCE (2026-09-09, PR #110): the revisor PR opened CONFLICTING at 19:29:23Z with auto-merge armed; GitHub-side update-branch cannot resolve .seeds JSONL conflicts at all, so the supervisor's conflict path would have retired the PR as stale_base after 3x5min (~19:44Z) while the correct manual repair (local merge + JSONL union) took ~2 minutes (branch updated 19:33Z, gate 19s, merged 19:35:20Z). Strengthens: 409/422 strikes need a notify-first/manual-repair-window policy for repos with append-heavy JSONL trackers, not just the 409-vs-422 split.

title: Closeout closure discipline: sd close only when the seed demand is visible in the run diff, else a documented reason is mandatory
description: fabro-9967 was closed 2026-09-09 15:42 (in a seeds:sync) although planner.md never implemented its demand (sd ready cap + created_since) — the revisor caught it only by accident while deduping (run 01M23J61HH8Z, regression finding). Separately, non-implementation closures (superseded/absorbed/duplicate, e.g. fabro-a0e3 absorbed into fabro-45bf by run 01M2368YQ) record their reason ONLY in the revisor journal, never in the seed record — a closed seed looks like lost work until someone greps journals. Wanted: (a) closeout closure discipline: before sd close, verify the seed's named demand is literally visible in the run diff; if not, DO NOT close from the run — park the seed with a journal note instead. CORRECTED TARGET (planner, 2026-09-16): there is NO closeout prompt file — the closeout step is deterministic via .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/closeout.nu (ADR-0010, 'Never an LLM'). So rule (a) lands as a pre-close check inside closeout.nu itself (a diff-visibility gate around the sd close call), or — if scripting it is disproportionate — as a documented decision in the script comments plus the rule surfaced in the planner prompt; implementer's call, journal the choice. (b) Any sd close the loop performs without its own implementing diff (superseded/absorbed/duplicate/stale-basis) must append the reason + evidence (run id / absorbing seed id) to the seed description BEFORE closing, so the closure is self-explaining in the tracker — this rule lands in the prompts that perform such closes: the develop planner prompt (.fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/planner.md, superseded-close exception fabro-d183) and the revisor prompt (.fabro/workflows/revisor/prompts/file.md supersession rule). Acceptance: closeout.nu carries the diff-visibility pre-close check (or the documented no-script choice journaled) with the 9967 incident cited; planner.md and revisor file.md prompts carry the reason-before-close rule with the fabro-a0e3 absorption (run 01M2368YQ) cited. Basis: commit-review grill session 2026-09-09; fabro-9967 closure regression (run 01M23J61HH8Z); fabro-a0e3 absorption opacity (run 01M2368YQ); commit f9d5e53a1/533b3c4dc sync closures; path correction run 01M2MJ0XJ0RH0RGMDARDD2K37X.

title: seeds-cli upstream: persist sd close --reason in the issue record

title: Engine: own the run-lifecycle event protocol — one module + one shared Event-to-Status transition table
description:
Architecture review 2026-09-10 (improve-codebase-architecture, user + agent; walkers: fabro-server, fabro-store/fabro-workflow). Top recommendation, filed unassigned per ADR-0018.

PROBLEM: The run-lifecycle event protocol (RunStartRequested -> RunRunnable -> RunStarting -> Running, terminal fails) has no owner. Emitters are spread over operations/start.rs:137-227, operations/resume.rs:36-46, server.rs:3405-3488 (writes terminal events directly), and test_support.rs mark_run_running:112-130 (a second protocol adapter inside tests). The same event stream is folded by TWO reducers with no shared table: server.rs update_live_run_from_event:3576-3740 (no transition validation, RunRunnable suppression, publish-blocked error field) vs fabro-store run_state.rs RunProjectionReducer (try_apply_status + InvalidTransition). The Paused{prior_block}/RunUnblocked arms already drift (server.rs:3610-3616 vs run_state.rs:197-205), and run_state.rs:84-112 patches historic Submitted->Starting / RunFailed fast-forward forms because the protocol was never an interface.

WANTED: (1) New fork-owned module fabro-workflow/src/operations/lifecycle_events.rs exposing the sequence as an interface (request_start / runnable / starting / running / resubmit / terminal_failure); server.rs and test_support become adapters. (2) One pure transition table (RunStatus x EventBody) -> Result<RunStatus, InvalidTransition> in fabro-types; BOTH reducers consume it, the live reducer adds only its side effects (map cleanup, bus cleanup).

DRIFT RULES (fork of fabro-sh/fabro, upstream merged regularly — conductor pass): the module and table are additive/fork-owned; edits concentrate in already-fork-modified files (server.rs +279, start.rs +107, run_state.rs +34 fork lines); resume.rs is upstream-identical (churn 5/12w) and gets a minimal adapter edit only. No wire-contract change; no new pub items on AppState. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the RunSupervisor full build-out (27 lock sites, ManagedRun) — that is phase 2 behind this seed.

ACCEPTANCE: equivalence test proving both reducers yield the same status for every event sequence (property test over the table); unit tests per transition incl. cancel-before-starting and failure-before-running; historic shims in run_state.rs carry a documented reason; lifecycle tests run without AppState lock surgery.

BASIS: commit bfbe3a6c8 (2026-09-09); walk reports /tmp/arch-walk-server.md (F1/F2), /tmp/arch-walk-store-workflow.md (F2/F8); upstream churn 12w: server.rs 49, start.rs 47, run_state.rs 53, resume.rs 5.

REOPEN CONTEXT (integrate, 2026-09-10 13:2x UTC): first implementation attempt (run 01M25K41V4NE, PR #121, 55 min) FAILED the dogfood-gate: fabro-cli::it::cmd::rm::rm_deletes_completed_run and rm_partial_failure_json_includes_removed_and_errors (lib/apps/fabro-cli/tests/it/cmd/rm.rs:284 — errors array expected [01M25QAG0W0V6X2CZAEZG47W8V], got []; rm did not treat the run as completed/deletable). The transition-table refactor changed which terminal states rm counts as completed. The seed stays OPEN on base (the close lives only in PR #121's unmerged branch); a re-claim must first reconcile with #121's branch (git fetch origin fabro/run/01M25K41V4NEWXSA3SVGRHKRXK — reuse or supersede its work) and the fix is likely a transition-table/`completed` predicate adjustment, not a rewrite. Repro on the #121 branch: cargo nextest run -p fabro-cli rm_deletes_completed_run rm_partial_failure_json_includes_removed_and_errors.

title: engine: conductor parks at soft exit after Work-routed survey since the 2026-09-09 22:29 deploy - develop leg never starts (line down)
description:
LINE DOWN INCIDENT 2026-09-10 07:01-09:30 (line-watch, reproduced twice): after the night deploy (server image built 2026-09-09 22:29 CEST, container started 22:35), every conductor pass parks at the soft exit immediately after a Work-routed survey; the develop leg never starts.

Evidence:
- Automation-fired pass 01M251VFNABCNMA94QDNHYZ5Q7 (07:00-07:01) and manual repair fire 01M253EWK1X299DRFTAJJHA0MV (07:28-07:29) both: survey stage completes green with correct route decision journaled ('route decision: Work'), then the exit handler completes in 0ms and run.failed fires with reason=soft_stop, kind=soft, category=deterministic ("infrastructure could not finish"). No develop-leg journal entry, no child run created.
- stage.completed context_values carry NO preferred_next_label on EITHER the broken passes or the last-known-good pass (20:08 yesterday on the OLD image) - routing reads the structured output elsewhere; do not chase the context key.
- Last known-good conductor pass on the previous image: 01M23W3067KQ 20:08-21:10 (develop child 01M23W4S7Q2G created fine, PR #113).
- The deployed image contains the 2026-09-09 engine merges: #84 (allow-keys lint), #90/fabro-91ff (overlap guard: run_summary_store + planner/analyze prompts), #96/fabro-de4d (preferred_label edge validation in fabro-validate, new rule routing_fallback_silent), #99/fabro-94e8 (update-branch), #107+#109 (PR postlude). Prime suspects: routing/output-schema handling around de4d and 91ff.
- Secondary blocker: the automation breaker (signature park|Conductor|soft_stop, consecutive_count 1, threshold appears to be 1) suppresses the */30 schedule after the first soft_stop - even a one-off park kills the line until the breaker resets.

Repro: FABRO_SERVER=http://localhost:32276 just run conductor (twice, deterministic). Also note the local repair path tripped over auth.json URL keying (127.0.0.1 vs localhost entry) - separate papercut.

Expected fix: find why the survey->develop edge (condition preferred_label="Work") is not taken on the new image though the survey emits the route; also revisit the breaker threshold (a single soft_stop should not permanently suppress the schedule without an incident signal).

Execution note: filed by line-watch during line-down; the line cannot pick this up itself (chicken-egg) - direct agent repair with user knowledge, or user-led. ROOT CAUSE FOUND (line-watch 10:2x, inspect of 01M253EWK1X): the survey agent's final answer literally set preferred_next_label="Unrouted survey outcome" (last_response in the stage context: {"preferred_next_label":"Unrouted survey outcome","outcome":"succeeded",...}) while its journal says 'route decision: Work'. The engine's Edge selected log confirms: from survey to exit label="Unrouted survey outcome" reason="preferred_label". fabro-de4d (#96, in the 22:29 image) constrains the routing output_schema enum from the node's outgoing edges - but the survey's outgoing set includes the UNCONDITIONAL safety-net edge (validator rule all_conditional_edges, label "Unrouted survey outcome"), so the fallback became a first-class valid choice and glm-5.3 picks it deterministically (2/2 passes on the new image). FIX DIRECTION: build the preferred_label enum from CONDITIONAL choice edges only (exclude unconditional safety nets and outcome=failed edges) in the de4d schema construction (lib/components/fabro-workflow, routing/output_schema area); optionally also make the model-facing schema description mark the fallback as engine-reserved. The old image worked because the enum was not edge-constrained. FIXED 2026-09-10 10:5x (line-watch direct repair, mandate: line down): lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/structured_output.rs routable_edge_labels now includes conditional edges whose condition routes on preferred_label naming the label (clause walk incl. and/or/not); regression tests cover the conductor-survey shape and composite conditions. Verification: cargo test -p fabro-workflow --lib (2 new tests green, 1326 pass; 4 pipeline failures pre-exist on clean tree - sandbox/env-dependent), clippy + fmt on touched crate green (nightly-2026-04-14). Commit 0373f5c10; deployed via just up.
closeReason: superseded: fix landed in 0373f5c10 (routable_edge_labels includes conditional preferred_label edges; regression tests for the conductor-survey shape); verified live — passes 01M256NF09VY (08:24), 01M257096GRA (08:30), 01M25H9VVJ (11:30) all route Work and reach the develop leg after the 10:18 deploy

title: Web UI run actions: add Resume that re-runs the last failed node — engine auto-rewinds to its entry checkpoint (Retry alone discards committed stages)
description: Where/what: the web run actions menu (apps/fabro-web/app/lib/run-actions.ts offers cancel/approve/deny/archive/unarchive/retry) has no Resume for terminal runs; Retry is the only recovery path and re-runs the whole workflow from scratch, discarding completed stages, stage context, and run data. Change (1) engine: a Resume of a failed run must itself determine the rewind target — the entry checkpoint of the last failed stage, dropping that stage's committed outcome/routing decision — so Resume re-runs exactly the failed node with all prior committed work intact. Plain POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/start {"resume":true} is NOT enough when the failure already committed a routing decision (soft-exit park): it replays only the exit stage and re-parks immediately. (2) web UI: expose this as a Resume action in the run actions menu for terminal runs that have checkpoints; Retry stays for explicit fresh starts and the UI copy must distinguish the two. Optional advanced form: a 'Rewind to checkpoint…' picker over the checkpoint timeline (node@visit, as fabro rewind --list shows). (3) API changes OpenAPI-first (docs/public/api-reference/fabro-api.yaml -> fabro-api build.rs -> fabro-api-client regen). Open design point: fabro rewind forks a new run id ('new run 01M25G94'); one-click Resume either keeps fork+parent link or the engine grows in-place resume-from-failure for terminal runs. Expected effect: a 429-style mid-run death costs only the failed node's re-execution instead of the whole run. Grounded: 2026-09-10 zai 429 killed Revisor 01M257B996MJ at the File stage after 'Findings ready' (~9 min agent work, checkpoint @3 analyze); UI Retry would have discarded it. Plain `fabro resume` re-ran only the exit stage and re-parked in 2s (routing 'Bookkeeping failed (nothing merged)' was already checkpointed); the actual rescue needed `rewind @3` (fork 01M25G94TMN8) + resume -> File stage succeeded on first attempt, PR #118. Basis: run 01M257B996MJNPWPY33MNDAEHP (+ fork 01M25G94TMN81J03TC153NRJXF, PR #118), 2026-09-10

title: Engine: staleness supervisor retires run PRs on .seeds JSONL update-conflicts — revisor bookkeeping lost (resumed/forked runs carry stale tracker state)
description:
PROBLEM: the PR staleness supervisor closes run PRs as stale_base after 3 update-branch attempts fail with 422. When the conflict sits in `.seeds/issues.jsonl`, the branch is unmergeable by GitHub's updater and the run's whole bookkeeping (filed seeds, review/revision artifacts, journals) is dropped from base when the PR retires. EVIDENCE (2026-09-10): revisor run 01M257B996MJ died on the zai 429 at its File stage; rescued via `fabro rewind @3` into fork 01M25G94TMN8, whose PR #118 (two seeds + review of develop run 01M25732658J) sat in the gate while base moved (#117 merge + seeds syncs). Supervisor update-branch attempts hit 422 on the tracker file at 11:16/11:21/11:26 (attempts 1-3), PR closed stale_base 11:31:34. The two revisor seeds and the review artifacts landed nowhere; manual recovery from run branch `fabro/run/01M25G94TMN81J03TC153NRJXF` during integrate (seed re-filed as fabro-8a60, second folded into fabro-52b4). ROOT CAUSE: forked/resumed runs inherit the pre-fork clone's tracker state; a normal base move then conflicts at JSONL level, which neither GitHub update-branch nor the supervisor can resolve. CHANGE (engine, fabro-server pull_request_supervisor / pipeline): (a) resolve 422 conflicts on `.seeds/issues.jsonl`/`.mulch/**` with the documented closed-wins union instead of counting a strike; or (b) rebase tracker state onto current base at fork/resume creation; or (c) at minimum, park (not close) revisor/bookkeeping PRs on retirement and surface the loss — silent drop of filed findings is the worst outcome. CLASS LINEAGE: fabro-94e8 (origin: run-branch staleness) -> fabro-17e8 (409 must not strike) -> this (422-on-JSONL real conflict must resolve, not strike). One class, one durable fix: make the supervisor conflict-aware for the loop's own JSONL formats. Basis: runs 01M257B996MJNPWPY33MNDAEHP + fork 01M25G94TMN81J03TC153NRJXF, PR #118, server log 11:16-11:31 UTC, 2026-09-10

SECOND INSTANCE (2026-09-10 ~14:1x UTC): PR #121 (fabro-3fe4 first attempt, run 01M25K41V4NE) hit the same 422-on-JSONL update-branch wall after base pushes (including the integrate batch 76ed61987) and was retired stale_base ~14:12 — this time NOT rescued by reopen; the branch survived and the fix landed via a fresh develop run (PR #123) instead. The 12:02 breaker-park + this retirement make the day's count two JSONL-driven PR losses in ~2 hours. The evidence strengthens the (a) JSONL-aware update-branch resolution as the preferred durable fix. Related same-day: fabro-8ee1 (duplicate develop child after the pass's own gate-stuck misroute) and fabro-ee5d (instant blocked returns misjudging young gates as stuck) — the three incidents form one operational cluster around conductor PR-wait semantics. Basis addition: PR #121 retirement, server logs 14:11-14:12 UTC.

title: Engine: fabro_run_create must structurally reject a duplicate develop child while a sibling of the same parent is non-terminal (conductor recreated a child after wait-timeout)
description:

Engine: oversized checkpoint event exceeds the events-endpoint body limit (413) and kills the run — two 2h merge-upstream runs destroyed mid-flight
description: WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-11, two instances): MergeUpstream runs die irrecoverably at their conflict-resolution checkpoint with `worker lost canonical run store during append run event: request failed with status 413 Payload Too Large: Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded` (event=checkpoint.completed). Instance 1: run 01M27V69K6BVS8RNEK3PAAT48Q died 09:29 after 28m (also `Git push failed` immediately before — likely the same oversized-payload class on the push path or a consequence). Instance 2: run 01M2837TP51DNK159MHVPTCVVK died 13:13:36 after 111m of healthy conflict-resolution work (tool calls seconds before death, 0 agent errors) — the accumulated checkpoint payload simply crossed the HTTP body limit. Conductor passes 01M27V3Y12QD and 01M2834T4ZWY routed 'Merge child failed' correctly; ~2.5h of merge work was destroyed. ROOT CAUSE: the worker->server event append (POST /runs/{id}/events, the canonical store) has a request body length limit with no ceiling-aware path for large checkpoint payloads; a run whose serialized state (diff summaries, context, journals of a big merge) grows past it dies at the next checkpoint with no truncation, chunking, or blob offload. KNOWN PRIOR ART: evidence capture already enforces a 16 KB inline ceiling with blob-ref detours elsewhere; the checkpoint event path lacks the equivalent. FIX DIRECTIONS (engine, fabro-server/fabro-workflow): (a) offload oversized event payloads to the blob store and inline a reference (preferred — no data loss); (b) or chunked append; (c) at minimum, fail the checkpoint with a resumable error instead of stopping the workflow run. IMPACT: every large merge (busy fork + high upstream drift) hits this — the merge leg is effectively capped by payload size, not by conflict complexity. Manual /merge-upstream remains the workaround. Basis: runs 01M27V69K6BVS8RNEK3PAAT48Q and 01M2837TP51DNK159MHVPTCVVK (+ conductors 01M27V3Y12QD, 01M2834T4ZWY), server log 13:13:36 UTC, 2026-09-11
closeReason: implemented via salvage of develop run 01M2D47MQKKSDS3P1V2JM0FYYA (implementer WIP finished+gated locally): run-store sink offloads oversized checkpoint payloads to content-addressed blobs with inline blob:// refs (lossless), bound_run_event truncation as logged fallback; 3 regression tests (413 offload class, blob-failure fallback, resumable append failure); landed as bfa4686f2/916fb0393 on denkhaus

title: checkpoint.completed event exceeds 3MB body limit: 413 kills run AFTER successful merge
description:
Observed 2026-09-11 on merge-upstream runs 01M27V69 and 01M2837: the worker appends checkpoint.completed whose JSON body exceeds MAX_RUN_EVENT_BODY_BYTES (3MB, fabro-types/src/run_event/mod.rs). Server rejects with 413 Payload Too Large, event sink loses the canonical store, workflow stops, run is marked failed(workflow_error) — even though the merge commit already exists and the gate passed. Result: complete work stranded in an ephemeral sandbox, conductor pass soft-stops, next pass redoes ~2h and ~2 of LLM work.

Agent tool outputs are already bounded (fabro-agent truncation.rs MAX_SERIALIZED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES = limit/2; tool_execution.rs event_body_budget). The workflow-side checkpoint event has NO equivalent bound: whatever it inlines (reports/journal/diff?) can exceed the limit.

Fix direction: bound or blob-offload large fields in checkpoint (and any other workflow-emitted) events before POST, mirroring the agent-side truncation contract; add a regression test that builds a >limit checkpoint event and proves the worker truncates instead of losing the store.

title: fabro/run/* branch pushes rejected by branch protection: finished run work is never persisted remotely
description:
Observed 2026-09-11: run lifecycle pushes of refs/heads/fabro/run/<id> (and possibly fabro/meta/* in some cases) are rejected by GitHub with 'github rejected the ref - likely a branch protection rule or push ruleset' (runs 01M27V69 11:29, 01M2837 15:13). Consequence: when a sandbox dies or a run fails late, the only copy of finished work is the ephemeral sandbox filesystem; salvage requires docker cp from stopped containers.

Fix direction: allow-list fabro/run/* and fabro/meta/* refs in the denkhaus/fabro repo ruleset (ops change), and/or make the engine fall back to a pushable ref namespace on rejection and surface the persistent failure in run notices. Without this, any post-merge infrastructure failure is unrecoverable-by-design.

(1) Live evidence: today's develop/revisor cycle pushed BOTH run branches with the engine's own credentials and merged PRs #133/#134 (heads fabro/run/01M2AQY9… and fabro/run/01M2ARX…; branches auto-deleted on merge per delete_branch_on_merge=true — which is why they are absent from ls-remote).

(3) Root-cause reading: the 2026-09-11 failures (01M27V69, 01M2837) hit the PRE-merge push path (push_credentials.rs re-embedding the checkout token; installation tokens are short-lived and age out mid-run). The #849 merge replaced that path with per-push minted credentials (age-tracked retry). 'likely a branch protection rule or push ruleset' was fabro's generic guess — a misclassification.
Follow-up kernel (not re-filed): if a run-push rejection recurs, capture and surface the RAW git error instead of the protection guess.

title: fabro-llm: 429 reset-deadline prose is parsed as naive-UTC — provider wallclock offsets corrupt the window and can silently disable the park (west-of-UTC)
description: PR #131 (run 01M299PVMSE7Q53ZGPP67AHNMG, seed fabro-a3d8) parses the 429 prose 'Your limit will reset at 2026-09-03 05:35:16' via NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str and compares it against UTC-now (gateway.rs parse_reset_deadline + reset_window). The provider timestamp carries NO timezone; treating it as UTC is wrong by the provider's local offset. Observed offset: ZAI sends Beijing wallclock (2026-09-11 incident, handoff fabro-91bf: 'Reset 13:14:50' was Beijing time; user decision 2026-09-12 for fabro-1f70: provider timestamps are timezone-untrustworthy). Consequences: (1) structured provider_retry_after/long_rate_limit_window durations are off by the offset (telemetry + any future consumer scheduling on them); (2) SHARP EDGE: for providers west of UTC the naive-UTC deadline is often in the PAST -> reset_window returns None -> treated as 'window reopened' -> normal short-window retries burn attempts against a live limit -> hard fail instead of park — the exact failure mode a3d8 was built to eliminate. The a3d8 tests only cover UTC-formatted fixtures so this is untested. Demand: naive (offset-less) prose timestamps must never be used as absolute deadlines — options: require an explicit offset (RFC3339) for authoritative windows; otherwise treat the window as UNKNOWN-ETA (fail-fast + park on prose PRESENCE, report window as unbounded, do not compute a duration); optionally calibrate a per-provider offset empirically. Acceptance: tests with a Beijing-offset sample (+8h) and a US-offset sample (-6h, past-deadline case) prove the park still triggers and no negative/None window disables it. Basis: PR #131 diff (gateway.rs lines ~173-194), run 01M299PVMSE7Q53ZGPP67AHNMG, user session 2026-09-12 ~01:35 Berlin.
closeReason: Fixed in 6fc7e9cb6: ResetDeadline At/Naive split in the gateway parser; naive prose attaches no duration and parks via rate_limit_window_unknown (SoftStop, same as long windows). Acceptance tests cover Beijing (+8) and US-west (past-deadline) naive samples plus RFC3339 measuring. Deploy pending (binary behind HEAD until next just up).

title: Sandbox: in-engine dockerfile pre-pass for docker envs (fork feature, build LATER) — multi-project image-as-config
description:
DECISION 2026-09-12 (user): build as a FORK feature, later; the upstream driver-PR is demoted to a subsequent offer from the proven code. Motivation survives the Daytona rejection: multi-project operation needs per-project run images without operator builds; fabro shall not remain self-serving (no Selbstzweck).

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (fork-side pre-pass, ~1-2 days):
1. New module fabro-sandbox/src/image_build.rs: resurrect the retired autobuild core from git history (pre-merge docker.rs at 409a3e9dd^: runner_image_tag content-hash tagging, build_runner_image, build-stream error folding first_build_stream_error, mtime-correct single-file tar). Self-contained; bollard dep returns to fabro-sandbox.
2. Hook at the SPEC SEAM (not inside provider code): when an environment carries inline image.dockerfile and the effective provider is docker, compute content hash -> fabro-runner-<sha12>; if an image with that tag+label exists, rewrite SandboxSpec source to Image{reference}; else build once via docker.sock (server container mounts it, proven deployment model) and rewrite. Cache check BEFORE build; unchanged Dockerfile = no rebuild.
3. Admission: re-accept docker+inline-dockerfile environments (revert the upstream image_incompatible guard restored in 409a3e9dd + flip the 422 test back to acceptance, now with the pre-pass as the run-time guarantee). fabro-config validate_docker_image_settings stays.
4. Tests: port the unit tests (hash tagging, tag changes with content, stream-error folding, tar mtime) + deploy validation against the toolchain env.
5. Docs: environments.mdx docker section documents image.dockerfile + caching (fork delta over upstream).

WHY MERGE-STABLE NOW: the pre-merge autobuild lived inside docker.rs (substrate Upstream deleted); the new one is one module + 2-3 small hooks at spec construction — minimal conflict surface.

INTERIM until built: just run-images (deploy-time builds, label sh.fabro.toolchain.sha256) stays; retire it once this feature has run stable for a while. LATER UPSTREAM OFFER: port image_build.rs to sandbox-driver-docker (SandboxSource::Dockerfile + content-hash cache, mirroring the Daytona snapshot pattern) and bump the driver rev.
