title: Sandbox: OCI exec 'resource temporarily unavailable' at run finalize kills 54min implementer work (run 01M2D47M)
description:
WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-13, run 01M2D47MQKKSDS3P1V2JM0FYYA): develop run implementing fabro-5082 failed at its FINALIZE DIFF step after 54m of healthy implementer work (planner claimed, implementer produced 409 insertions incl. event/offload.rs) with: 'OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process: error starting setns process: fork/exec /proc/self/fd/6: resource temporarily unavailable' on git diff — the sandbox container could not exec ANY new process (final diff + diff stats both failed with the same OCI error, exit 128). The run went failed; nothing was checkpointed past the planner, so the branch carried no implementer work (salvaged manually from the still-present exited container; WIP secured under .fabro/reports/5082-wip-salvage/). ROOT CAUSE (suspected): process/PID or fd exhaustion inside the run sandbox after a long agent session (54m, many tool execs) — the container itself stayed alive, only new execs failed. FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) probe/exec health check before finalize with a bounded retry after a cooldown; (b) run the final diff through the driver with a fresh exec context or stream it instead of exec; (c) checkpoint implementer work progressively (mid-stage checkpoints) so a finalize failure does not discard the stage's tree. IMPACT: any long agent run can lose all stage work at finalize; same blast radius class as fabro-5082 but sandbox-side. Basis: run 01M2D47MQKKSDS3P1V2JM0FYYA, log /tmp/run-5082b.log (retained), container fabro-run-01M2D47MQKKSDS3P1V2JM0FYYA (kept stopped for forensics).

The sandbox exhausts a process/thread-level resource (suspect: cgroup pids limit under 8-core parallel cargo + agent session + mise shims; cpu was raised to 8 that evening), then EVERY exec (rustc, git add) fails. Same class as the local 01M2D47M finalize-OCI failure. ICE dumps + repair WIP secured under .fabro/reports/274d-wip-salvage/. title: Engine: pebble skill expansion structurally kills agent sessions on unknown mid-text /word tokens in prompts
description: WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-13, first mirtuell conductor fire): conductor run 01M2DFBRB3220NK1BWPCZ8HVQQ failed at the survey stage in 286ms with 'Precondition failed: Agent session failed: expanding a skill reference' (category structural, zero inference). ROOT CAUSE: pebble's expand_skill (skills.rs find_skill_references) binds ANY /<name> token whose slash 'begins the input or follows whitespace' and whose first char is lowercase; the survey prompt legitimately contained the prose token '/merge-upstream' (referring to the user-facing skill/command of the same name), the sandbox skill registry (.fabro/skills = rust-style-guide only) did not know it, and UnknownSkill aborts session start HARD. A prompt that merely MENTIONS a slash command (documentation, instructions like 'use the `/merge-upstream` skill', references to skills that exist in other homes) structurally kills the run before any LLM call. FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) expand only when the input STARTS with the `/name` token (the person-typed-command case pebble documents) and leave mid-text tokens literal; (b) or unknown references stay literal with a warning event instead of a session-fatal error; (c) at minimum make the failure resumable/non-structural so a prompt edit can recover. Affects every workflow whose prompts mention slash commands. IMPACT: any agent-stage prompt containing prose `/word` tokens is a latent run-killer; first seen on the remote production instance. Basis: run 01M2DFBRB3220NK1BWPCZ8HVQQ (mirtuell.net), stage.failed event seq 4, prompt line reverted in df0f40b5a, pebble rev 222d17f skills.rs.

title: Develop workflow: implementer must know self-graph changes apply only to FUTURE runs (bootstrap paradox)

title: Conductor: 13-min orchestration preamble per cycle — move workflow packaging off the agent hot path
description: WHAT HAPPENS (2026-09-13, mirtuell conductor cycle 5, run 01M2DX36QQ): ~13 minutes of orchestration overhead before product work begins, per cycle: survey 2min + file collection 5min (20+ individual shell turns, one LLM roundtrip each) + registration payload 5+min (the whole develop workflow closure ~100-200KB streamed through LLM OUTPUT tokens as tool arguments — slow, stall-prone: every big-payload turn hit a 5-min zai stream stall, expensive on output tokens, fragile: 3 JSON-mangled attempts in cycle 3). title: Engine: stall watchdog (1800s no-activity) kills conductor passes during legal blocking fabro_run_wait (60min design timeout unreachable)
description:
WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-13 20:13, mirtuell conductor cycle 5): pass 01M2DX36QQ died with workflow_error 'stall watchdog: node develop had no activity for 1800s' exactly 30:00 after its develop child (01M2DXVAJB) was created — the develop leg was inside its blocking fabro_run_wait {until: terminal, timeout_ms: 3600000} (60 min by prompt design: 'big seeds legitimately run 90+ min... call again after timeout'). The wait tool emits no run events while blocked, so ANY child longer than 30 min kills its parent pass mid-wait; the 60-minute wait design can never complete. The CHILD survived (independent run) but lost its conductor context: no revise leg, no publish handling, no gate-stuck park. ROOT CAUSE: stall-watchdog activity definition does not count an in-flight tool execution as activity. FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) fabro_run_wait emits periodic activity pings (e.g. a run.notice every few minutes with current wait state — also great UX for the web timeline); (b) the watchdog counts active tool executions as activity (engine knows a tool is in flight); (c) node-level stall timeout override on the conductor develop/revise nodes (the e2e suite names e2e_stall_watchdog_with_explicit_timeout_override — an override mechanism may already exist to wire). IMPACT: every conductor cycle whose develop child runs longer than 30 min — which is the NORMAL case for real seeds — dies at the pass level and needs manual child handling; the serialized line cannot sustain real work. Basis: pass 01M2DX36QQT92MMBD7GYBR6EF8 (run.failed 18:13:13Z), child 01M2DXVAJBY1XBWBSNKNG0M6DM (kept running), develop-leg.md wait design line.

IMPLEMENTED + RESOLVED (2026-09-14, direct agent work, ADR-0021 prerequisite): the loop graphs now pin the graph-level stall attribute `stall_timeout="63m"` (conductor, develop, merge-upstream workflow.fabro) — a legal 60-minute `fabro_run_wait` plus slack can no longer trip the default 1800s watchdog, while genuine agent silence (>63m without events) still dies. Fix direction (c) via the supported engine attribute (graph.rs stall_timeout, 0 disables): no engine code change needed. The engine-generic watchdog behavior for other graphs is unchanged. Evidence: `fabro validate` all three graphs OK; presence pin `line_graphs_pin_stall_timeout_above_the_legal_wait` in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/fork_line_recovery_tests.rs (fork-only file, merge-protected); touchpoints row added. Runtime form (a)/(b) (wait pings as activity, UX for the web timeline) not needed for the line and stays a possible upstream-friendly follow-up, NOT this seed's demand.

title: Engine: parented child runs strand on the parent run branch — explicit-target prompts are the stopgap, engine must own the chain terminus
description: WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-13, pass 01M2E2805XB4 on mirtuell): with the create payload's target omitted, inherit_parent_target (lib/components/fabro-tool/src/create.rs) resolved the conductor children's clone AND PR base to the parent's RUN branch fabro/run/01M2E2805XB4 — a branch with no protection rules, no Dogfood Gate trigger (.github/workflows/dogfood-gate.yml filters branches: [denkhaus]), and enablePullRequestAutoMerge structurally failing ('Protected branch rules not configured' / 'Pull request is in clean status'). PR #138 (fabro-274d work) merged into the run branch only (manual merge by user); revisor PR #139 orphaned open with zero checks. Nothing in the conductor graph merges a parent run branch back to its base — the chain has no terminus. STOPGAP (landed cd2a8ffe2): conductor develop-leg + revise-leg prompts now send an explicit target {kind: git, repo: denkhaus/fabro, branch: denkhaus}; explicit targets win over inheritance, so children gate on denkhaus again. Stranded pass work was merged manually (f497572b5). ENGINE DEMAND: decide and implement real parented-chain semantics — options: (a) inherit_parent_target resolves to the parent's BASE branch (git.branch), not the run branch, when the parent is an orchestration run (PR disabled, run_branch push only); (b) keep run-branch chaining but add a terminus: when a parented child PR merges into the parent run branch and the parent completes, the engine merges the run branch into the base via its own PR with normal gating; (c) reject parented creates with run-branch-enabled parents unless target is explicit, so the contract is loud instead of implicit. ALSO: enableAutoMerge failures on unprotected bases should not be a silent WARN — a PR the engine created and cannot merge is a stuck-gate signal the wait should classify (fabro-bde4 semantics treat it as young forever because mergeable_state stays clean). Evidence: runs 01M2E2NE8DZS (develop child, PR #138), 01M2E4CWJVJ7 (revisor child, PR #139 closed as journal-only), wait logs in fabro logs of both runs, merged_by=denkhaus on #138. SALVAGE POINTER (2026-09-13, run 01M2E7VZYX8V, zai 429 victim): the first implementation attempt is STRANDED but real — run branch origin/fabro/run/01M2E7VZYX8V0RFKJ7PZCTX92D, implementer journal commit da3eaabb3 (final tree 3c5e9e8b0), diff +419/-80 over 19 files incl. lib/foundation/fabro-types (pull_request.rs +33, run_projection.rs, run_event/misc.rs) — the next implementer MUST diff/salvage against that branch before starting fresh (274d salvage-dir precedent: basis-update may cite the branch; if unfetchable in-sandbox, salvage into .fabro/reports/<id>-wip-salvage/ first). Claim lived only on the dead branch; local tracker shows this seed open again — correct.

title: Engine: stage retries and fabro resume re-send the full stage prompt + preamble per attempt (20KB+ x5 on quota failures) — continue the session instead
description:
USER REPORT (2026-09-13, run 01M2E7VZYX8V, zai 429 hard-cut): when an agent stage exhausts its retry budget, each attempt re-posts the ENTIRE initial chat message INCLUDING the preamble — the implementer burned 5 attempts against the exhausted zai window and the preamble (easily 20KB+) went into the chat 5 times. Same shape on fabro resume: resuming a run re-posts the first message with preamble per attempt instead of continuing the existing agent session. Why this is bad beyond the 429 case: (1) input-token cost multiplies with attempt count exactly when the loop is already struggling; (2) context duplication confuses the agent (multiple authoritative preambles); (3) for quota-class errors every retry is doomed until the window resets — Retry-After/backoff cannot fix a hard-cut window, so 5 preambles burn for a guaranteed failure. DEMANDS: (a) stage retry / resume CONTINUES the existing agent session (send a minimal continuation: 'attempt N failed with <error>, continue from your last state') instead of re-sending the stage prompt; (b) quota/hard-cut error class fails the stage FAST (no retry budget burned — one attempt, terminal, the cron/next fire is the reviver; the zai window end is knowable from the error and Retry-After semantics); (c) resume path shares the same continuation semantics. Basis: run 01M2E7VZYX8V (implementer attempts 1-5, planner visit 2 attempts 1-5, 'goal gate unsatisfied', zai window exhausted ~20:38-21:08 UTC, reset 21:31); user observation 2026-09-13 ~23:5x.

FACET RESOLVED FOR QUOTA CLASS (2026-09-14, ADR-0021): usage-window rate limits no longer consume stage retries at all — the engine seam in `error.rs is_retryable` (via fork module fork_line_recovery.rs) fails them non-retryably on the first 429 and the run parks SoftStop; no prompt re-send x5 on quota failures. The REMAINING demand of this seed (generic stage retries re-send the full prompt + preamble for OTHER transient classes; continue-the-session instead) stays open.

title: Design: server-autonomous line recovery — transient failures (quota hard-cut) must self-heal without external triggers (run recovery supervisor vs self-unlatching breaker)
description:
USER DESIGN POSITION (2026-09-13, after the 429 strand + manual scheduler pause): 'der resume muss auf dem server von selbst stattfinden und nicht von extern getriggert werden' — the line's availability must be server-autonomous; today every recovery path ends in an EXTERNAL flip: (1) terminal-failed runs stay dead (fabro resume is an external CLI/API trigger; no server-side auto-recovery exists — verified by grep over fabro-server + fabro-automation 2026-09-13), revival = new cron pass re-doing work with a salvage dance; (2) the schedule breaker LATCHES after 3 consecutive failures and never re-enables itself; (3) quota-class errors (zai 429 hard-cut, KNOWN recovery point from Retry-After/window end) count fully into stage retries (fabro-183f), the breaker, and cron revival waits for external action although the server could know the healing time. DESIGN FORK (user decision, grill-worthy): (A) run recovery supervisor — server watches terminal-failed runs with transient time-bounded failure classes and resumes them server-side at the recovery point (bounded attempts, own breaker, Slack); HARD CONSTRAINT: serialization (ADR-0015) — an auto-resumed develop child must hold/block the automation while it runs (parallel develop = incident); ADR-worthy. (B) self-healing scheduler — quota-class failures exempt from the breaker + breaker unlatches after cooldown (auto-retry); no serialization coupling. (A)+(B) compose: B keeps the line alive through quota bursts, A preserves work (resume not redo). Counterpoint to keep: cron-as-reviver was a deliberate choice because server-side agent auto-resume risks zombie loops/double execution/cost runaway — the fix is not removing latches but making them release on the KNOWN recovery condition. Basis: run 01M2E7VZYX8V (429 victim, work stranded then salvage-pointered), manual scheduler pause 2026-09-13, breaker threshold 3 (fabro-3d97), fabro-183f preamble-repost sibling.

## USER DECISION (2026-09-14, grill session after run-01M2E7CSGDDT forensics)

- NO prose-parsed backoff: the recovery cadence is a FIXED recheck interval of 10 minutes. The server never derives a wait duration from provider prose (RFC3339 or naive); a quota-parked line just rechecks every 10 min until a pass survives. Rationale: prose formats are provider-specific and untrustworthy (zai sends naive timestamps); a fixed probe is simple, bounded, and observable.
- Option B shape NOW (scheduler self-heal), Option A (run recovery supervisor / server-side resume) EXPLICITLY DEFERRED — not rejected: revisit only if redo-cost of parked passes becomes painful. B-first reasoning from forensics: yesterday's terminal failures were classified deterministic (goal-gate + watchdog), so A would not even have fired; and A carries the zombie/double-execution risk class.
- Ordering is the agent's call. Chosen order: (1) fabro-0e11 stall fix (legal 60-min fabro_run_wait must not trip the 1800s watchdog — graph-level stall_timeout covering MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS), (2) quota-class failures park SoftStop with the api_transient|*|rate_limit signature instead of burning stage retries into a deterministic goal-gate failure (this makes runs, breaker, and recheck classifier readable), (3) the 10-min recheck scheduler + breaker exemption.
- FORK-FILE POLICY (user directive 2026-09-14): ALL feature implementations live in fork-ONLY files (modules upstream does not have), wired through minimal seams; every feature gets presence tests in a fork-only test file + a touchpoints row (.agents/skills/merge-upstream/references/touchpoints.md) so upstream merges cannot silently drop them (fabro-8ee1 class).
- Design: recheck state is DERIVED, not persisted — each scheduler tick, when the newest automation-fired terminal run is quota-class and older than 10 min and no run is active, fire a probe pass through the normal scheduled-fire path (on_overlap=skip serializes). Quota-class terminal runs are exempt from breaker counting (neither count nor reset). One Slack notice when recheck mode engages (visibility); no recheck cap (window waits are legitimate; non-quota failures still trip the breaker normally).
- Implementation: DIRECT AGENT WORK (user-assigned in chat 2026-09-14, exception to the executor directive), with the full mechanical gate.


IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (2026-09-14, direct agent work, ADR-0021) — B-shape complete, A deferred as decided:
- fabro-workflow fork module `src/fork_line_recovery.rs` (+ fork-only tests `src/fork_line_recovery_tests.rs`, 5 pins): usage-window 429s (naive prose OR long Reopens) are non-retryable at the engine seam (`error.rs is_retryable`), map to resumable SoftStop with the api_transient|*|rate_limit signature (mapping existed, now actually reached), and the `graph.rs select_edge` seam returns NO edge for park-class failures — no more goal-gate masking.
- fabro-server fork module `server/fork_line_recovery.rs` (+ 6 unit pins + scheduler integration pin `quota_parks_are_breaker_exempt_and_keep_the_schedule_armed`): quota parks breaker-exempt; fixed 10-minute recheck probes fire through the normal scheduled-fire path (on_overlap serializes; in-memory last-probe gate; manual-only automations untouched).
- Prereq fabro-0e11 CLOSED: loop graphs pin stall_timeout=63m.
- Verification: cargo nextest fabro-workflow 1504/1504, fabro-server 936/936; clippy -D warnings green; pinned-nightly fmt clean; fabro validate conductor/develop/merge-upstream OK; fork_seam suite included.
- REMAINING before close: production deploy (just image-release + fabro-tofu apply — engine changes, binary-need fires) and one live validation (next quota park must recheck-probe instead of dying). Upstream breaker test fixtures switched to a neutral transient signature (api_transient|zai|server_error) because rate_limit signatures are fork-semantically exempt — documented in ADR-0021 + touchpoints.

REVISION 2 (2026-09-14, user review of the recheck design): run-based recheck probes REJECTED ("die derzeitige implementation ist keine Lösung") — they create useless run artifacts while the window is closed. Implemented instead: a PRE-FIRE PROVIDER GATE in the server fork module — before every scheduled fire the scheduler runs the basic model test (1-word completion, vault credential, provider-agnostic; zai has no documented usage route and lithos-llm no usage endpoint, verified 2026-09-14) — closed window => NO run is created; closed lines poll probe-only on the fixed 10-minute cadence and fire on reopen (zero runs during an outage). Park classification + breaker exemption stay as mid-flight defense. Fail-open on unresolvable model/client (bounded: one parked run per window). ADR-0021 Revision section documents the change.

## LIVE-EVIDENCE GAP (2026-09-15, run 01M2J1BA2JC4S6SA10YEJHHMVP + pass 01M2J191AG): the run-level park NEVER materializes — the executor's no-edge rewrite destroys the park classification

Deployed build confirmed current (server reports 0.357.0-nightly.0 = denkhaus >= ed0c65857, includes dc16369f5 + 0de9d788b). Morning evidence with the zai 5h window closed (reset prose "18:30:03", stage fail 08:38 UTC):

1. STAGE level works exactly as designed: implementer failed ONE attempt (will_retry=false, no retry budget burned), failure carries `api_transient|zai|rate_limit` + TransientInfra + reset prose. Same on the conductor pass develop node.
2. RUN level does NOT park: both runs ended `failed/workflow_error` with category DETERMINISTIC and message "stage implementer|develop failed with no outgoing fail edge" — not SoftStop, not quota-class.
3. ROOT CAUSE (code, parked tree): `fabro-core/src/executor.rs:331` — the `NextStep::End` path for `OnFailure::Route|Succeed` REPLACES the outcome failure with `Outcome::fail("stage {} failed with no outgoing fail edge")`. The fork seam (`graph.rs select_edge` -> None for park-class failures) relies on the ORIGINAL failure prose reaching `pipeline::finalize` -> `soft_stop_failure_reason` (fork_terminal_taxonomy.rs keys on `reset_window(&failure.message)`); the rewrite deletes the prose, so finalize classifies WorkflowError/deterministic. The seam's own comment ("Returning no edge ends the run with the failed outcome, which pipeline::finalize maps to a resumable SoftStop") is factually wrong for Route/Succeed nodes — the unit seams (select_edge, soft_stop_failure_reason) are green, but no integration test drives stage-fail -> no-edge -> End -> finalize, so the gap survived.
4. DOWNSTREAM DAMAGE: (a) breaker exemption keys on quota-class run failures — a deterministic-counted pass means 3 stranded passes still kill the schedule with nothing re-enabling it; (b) the recheck classifier ("newest automation-fired terminal run is quota-class") sees deterministic — recheck never engages (mitigated only by the rev-2 pre-fire gate, which probes independently); (c) the run is not parked-resumable — exactly the revival the user expected on 2026-09-15 ("diese runs sollten automatisch wiederbelebt werden").

FIX DIRECTION: preserve the park-class failure detail through the executor End path (do not rewrite the message when the original failure is a usage-window park — needs a minimal one-line seam in the upstream fabro-core executor plus classification reuse; fork-file policy applies). Add an INTEGRATION pin: stage fails park-class on a Route-policy node without fail edge -> run MUST end SoftStop with the quota signature (extend fork_line_recovery_tests.rs). Note for the user demand: auto-REVIVAL of the dead run itself remains Option A (deferred 2026-09-14); the pre-fire gate revives only the LINE. With fabro-7627's resume_from_failure (in flight in the very run that died) Option A becomes cheap: server-side resume on window-reopen signal.

- fabro-core: Graph::failure_parks_run default trait method (graph.rs) + guard in executor.rs NextStep::End - the routing-diagnostic rewrite is skipped for park-class outcomes, ALL on_failure policies (Route|Succeed|Exit).
- fabro-workflow: failure_parks_run override on WorkflowGraph (graph.rs) delegating to fork_line_recovery::failure_detail_parks; the select_edge seam now reuses the same predicate (one classification, two seams).
- Pins: fabro-core src/fork_line_recovery_tests.rs (NEW fork-only file, 3 tests: park preserved at end, ordinary failure rewrite unchanged, exit-policy park preserved); fabro-workflow fork_line_recovery_tests.rs extended (failure_parks_run hook wiring + parked_stage_failure_ends_soft_stop_with_quota_signature - full executor->End->classify_engine_result chain that run 01M2J1BA2JC4S6SA10YEJHHMVP broke). title: Conductor: failed develop children skip the revisor — revise-anyway edge for failed children + real backlog signal in survey
description:
WHAT HAPPENS (2026-09-14, pass 01M2G1RTQ5CC survey journal + 2026-09-13 forensics): the revisor only ever reviews develop runs that INTEGRATED (or gate-stuck). A FAILED develop child routes `develop -> exit [kind=soft, "Develop child failed"]` — the pass ends and the revisor never runs, so the failed run's painpoints, tool walls, and failure forensics die unreviewed (yesterday 01M2E7VZYX8V: quota-parked implementer with journal evidence; revisor never saw it because the conductor died — but even a healthy conductor would have soft-exited past the revise leg). Compounding signal gap: the survey's backlog check `fabro_runs_list(workflow=develop)` returned 0 runs although terminal develop runs exist (01M2E7VZYX8V, failed 2026-09-13) — the survey itself journaled 'signal may be scope-limited but reads as no backlog' (created_since bound and/or inspects scope too narrow), so the one detector that could route a revision pass for unrevised FAILED runs is blind.

ROOT CAUSE (graph, .fabro/workflows/conductor/workflow.fabro): no edge from a failed develop child into the revise leg; the only revise entries are 'Develop integrated' and 'Gate stuck — revise anyway'. Plus the survey backlog query's scope hides terminal-but-unrevised runs.

FIX DIRECTIONS:
- (a) GRAPH+PROMPT (ADR-0008, one unit): add `develop -> revise [label="Develop child failed — revise anyway"]` (condition preferred_label) and teach develop-leg.md that a failed child STILL routes to the revise leg naming the failure (an unreviewed FAILED run is worse than a parked PR — same principle as the existing gate-stuck edge, fabro-1dc9); the revise leg's newest-revisable-run targeting already handles which run to review. Soft-park semantics stay: if the revisor child then fails too, the pass still exits soft.
- (b) SURVEY SIGNAL: widen the backlog query so terminal-but-unrevised develop runs are visible (created_since bound from the newest REVISOR run, not the pass start; verify the inspects scope of fabro_runs_list actually covers terminal develop runs of any age); the survey observation must name real backlog ids (`revisor backlog: <ids>`).
Acceptance criteria:
- Graph carries the failed-child revise edge; develop-leg.md names the route and its rationale.
- A pass whose develop child fails still creates+waits a revisor child (evidence: next real failed-child pass journals a revisor run).
- Survey backlog check lists terminal unrevised develop runs by id (evidence: survey observation with real ids, not 'none visible').

Ownership: workflows class — @fabro proposal (vetoable). Basis: run 01M2G1RTQ5CC (survey journal observation + painpoint), 01M2E7VZYX8V/01M2E7CSGDDT (failed child, revisor never ran), user directive 2026-09-14 ('schreibe ein seed für den Fall, dass der Revisor nicht läuft').

title: Conductor survey: bare git fetch floods the shell result (~160KB ref advertisement) and truncates the upstream signals — quiet fetches + targeted signal commands
description:
WHAT HAPPENS (2026-09-14, pass 01M2G1RTQ5CC, survey journal painpoint, verbatim): "First-time `git fetch upstream --prune` in this workspace flooded output with ~90 new branch + dozens of tag refs (~160KB), truncating the survey shell result and nearly hiding the count (1) and newest subject; suggestion: in the survey procedure pipe fetches through `grep -E 'main|denkhaus'` or add `-q` with a follow-up targeted rev-list so the signal lines survive truncation."

ROOT CAUSE: .fabro/workflows/conductor/prompts/survey.md step 1 prescribes the BARE fetches (`git fetch upstream --prune` and `git fetch origin --prune`) in the same shell call that must return the count. Every freshly cloned run workspace pays the full ref advertisement (~90 branches + tags, ~160KB) once — and run workspaces are fresh per container, so this recurs for every new workspace, not just once ever. Shell-result truncation then eats the actual signals (count, newest subject), risking a misrouted survey ("Nothing to do" on real drift).

FIX (prompt, loop asset): survey.md step 1 becomes —
- `git fetch upstream --prune -q` and `git fetch origin --prune -q` (quiet; fetch output is noise, never signal),
- then SEPARATE targeted commands for the signals: `git rev-list --count origin/denkhaus..upstream/main` and `git log -1 --format=%s upstream/main` (each its own shell call so truncation of one never eats the other).
Acceptance: survey.md carries -q fetches + separated signal commands; the next fresh-workspace survey journal contains count + newest subject without a truncation painpoint.

Ownership: workflows class — @fabro proposal (vetoable). This seed exists because survey-stage painpoints have no revisor consumer (the revisor inspects develop runs only, fabro-d43a adjacent). Basis: run 01M2G1RTQ5CC survey journal painpoint; survey.md:5; user directive 2026-09-14.

title: Revisor: extend the candidate pool to conductor runs (inspects += conductor) — survey/leg painpoints have no revisor consumer, the previous pass is the reviewable unit
description:
WEAKNESS (user observation 2026-09-14): the revisor cannot revise its own line — survey/conductor-stage painpoints (e.g. pass 01M2G1RTQ5CC's git-fetch flood, ~160KB truncating the survey signals) have NO revisor consumer, so they die unless a human files them.

CAPABILITY ANSWER (verified in tree): the revisor's checkout COULD read them (the conductor run branch `fabro/run/<id>` carries .fabro/journal/<id>.jsonl; the shell reads it — fs_hide binds file tools only, and Ask-Fabro reads run events server-side). But it is STRUCTURALLY blind:
- .fabro/workflows/revisor/workflow.fabro sets `inspects="develop,merge-upstream"` — the CONDUCTOR workflow is not in scope, so the fabro_runs_list tool gate (workflow must be in inspects) rejects enumerating conductor runs.
- prompts/select.md builds the candidate pool from develop + merge-upstream only.
- Temporal: the revisor's OWN parent conductor run is non-terminal while the revisor runs — the terminal-only rule excludes it BY DEFINITION. The reviewable unit is the PREVIOUS conductor pass (terminal by then).

FIX (ADR-0008, graph + prompts as one unit):
- revisor graph: `inspects="develop,merge-upstream,conductor"`.
- select.md: add the third `fabro_runs_list {"workflow": "conductor"}` call to the candidate pool; freshness baseline derived per workflow as today; EXCLUDE the spawning parent (non-terminal anyway) — target the newest TERMINAL conductor pass.
- Acceptance: the revisor of a pass whose PREVIOUS pass journailed survey painpoints distills them (evidence: a seed citing a conductor run id + node, or an explicit no-findings note naming the conductor pass).
- Note: merge-upstream already models this pattern ('merge runs carry their own revision value: orchestration painpoints') — conductor is the missing third pillar; the standing directive (2026-09-05) names exactly this gap: revisor/conductor/merge-upstream have no revisor of their own.

Ownership: workflows/revision class — @fabro proposal (vetoable). Basis: pass 01M2G1RTQ5CC survey journal painpoint (fetch flood, filed separately as fabro-cc06), revisor workflow.fabro:7 inspects scope, select.md:11 candidate pool, user directive 2026-09-14.

title: Deterministic verification dispatcher: `just verify` decides test/check scope from the calling agent's workflow step + diff (step-env injection fork)
description:
DEMAND (user idea 2026-09-14, after reviewing the implementer verification rules): keep the prompt rules as-is for now, but evolve toward a DETERMINISTIC verification dispatcher — the agent calls ONE just-file task (e.g. `just verify`), and that task conditionally decides WHICH tests/checks to run based on (a) the WORKFLOW STEP the calling agent is currently in and (b) the current diff.

WHY: today the verification scope rules live in prompt prose (implementer.md step 4: full crate suite only for test-file-touched crates, no gate, no workspace suites, crate-scoped fmt/clippy; planner briefs carry cheapest-first command lists per fabro-e137). Prompt-encoded rules are advisory and drift (fabro-0d56, 01M20T9S8 evidence); a deterministic task makes the policy executable once and verifiable.

DESIGN FORKS (decide before implementation):
- STEP SOURCE: cleanest = the engine injects the current node/stage as an env var into agent shell calls (resolve_workflow_env already injects env — e.g. FABRO_STAGE=implementer|tester|reviewer), so `just verify` reads it without trusting an agent-passed argument; alternative = agent passes the step as an argument (simpler, but agent-spoofable and drift-prone).
- DIFF SOURCE: the task derives touched crates from git diff itself (deterministic; same rules as today: test-file-touched vs code-touched crates).
- OUTPUT: machine-readable result (exit code + summary line) so the implementer's inline verification report and the tester's gate verdict can consume it directly.
- SCOPE MIGRATION: prompts shrink to one line ("run `just verify`"); the gate stays the trust boundary and unchanged.

Relation: generalizes fabro-e137 (per-brief command tuning) and the implementer.md step-4 rule set into one executable policy; the ADR-0008 rule applies (justfile + prompts changed as one unit; nu script under scripts/, no inline shell in the justfile).

Basis: user directive 2026-09-14 ("Vielleicht müssen wir in Zukunft eine deterministische Lösung entwickeln, sodass ein Agent einen Just-File-Task aufruft, der dann conditional entscheidet, welche Tests aufgerufen werden anhand des Steps"); implementer.md step 4; scripts/qualitygate.nu as the existing pattern.

Ownership: workflows/engine class — @fabro proposal (vetoable); the step-env fork is the pivotal decision (needs-user input before implementation).

FRESH EVIDENCE (2026-09-15, develop run 01M2K3NQEW0F, implementer journal — the interim scripts/verify.nu is already live): the test-file-touched derivation reported EMPTY for a seed that wrote table-driven tests in an INLINE #[cfg(test)] module inside src/lifecycle/git.rs — the dispatcher only counts tests/ directory files as test touches. verify.nu therefore ran a compile-check instead of the crate suite, weakening the implementer-side test signal. The DIFF SOURCE fork must treat inline #[cfg(test)] modules in touched source files as test-file touches (e.g. detect 'mod tests' / '#[cfg(test)]' markers in the diff hunks of src files), not only tests/ paths. Same-turn line-watch capture; no separate seed (this seed owns the dispatcher).

title: ENGINE: fabro_runs_list returns 0 runs for workflow=develop — intent-created runs invisible to the revisor selector (revisor functionally down, ran as 14s no-op)
description:
INCIDENT (2026-09-14 17:31 UTC, revisor run 01M2G8Q3SEN4, stage select@1): the revisor's fabro_runs_list {workflow: develop} returned 'listed 0 run(s)' — with correct, unbounded args (no created_since) — although terminal develop runs exist (01M2G27BSCZS completed 15:06 UTC same day, PR #140 merged; 01M2E7VZYX8V 2026-09-13). merge-upstream also 0. Result: select@1 routed 'Nothing to revise' and the revisor ran as a 14s no-op — the revisor pipeline is functionally DOWN (no run can ever be selected). The conductor survey hit the same 0-result earlier the same pass ('revisor backlog: none visible — signal may be scope-limited'). SUSPECT: the workflow filter matches a slug/name that intent-created runs do not carry. Basis: revisor run 01M2G8Q3SEN4 tool calls/responses (verbatim in run events), survey journal 01M2G1RTQ5CC, user question 2026-09-14 ('was war der Zweck dieses runs').

ROOT CAUSE: workflow_slug_from_path (lib/foundation/fabro-config/src/project.rs) derives the slug from the entrypoint's PARENT DIRECTORY when the stem is the conventional "workflow" — a bare relative entrypoint "workflow.toml" has no parent, so the fallback returns the stem itself: slug "workflow". Every child created from a survey-registered version with a bare entrypoint got workflow_slug "workflow" — invisible to every workflow=<slug> filter.

FIXED (landed, three commits 2026-09-14/15):
1. Asset (c77a20ab8): conductor survey.md mandates <slug>/-prefixed entrypoint and file keys.
2. Engine (79c8fbde0): fabro_workflow_version_create REJECTS an entrypoint without a directory component, with a teaching error; conductor legs + survey use one canonical collection command (cd .fabro/workflows, find <slug>) so paths arrive slug-prefixed verbatim; docs examples carry the prefix; guard pinned in fork_line_recovery_tests.rs.
3. Placeholder-safety (7573ffd8e): <slug>/ notation in docs and error text; placeholder-shaped paths (<...>) rejected at the tool (WorkflowPath would otherwise accept a verbatim doc copy and register slug "<slug>").
4. Fork pins (0de9d788b): 986b provider window gate seam + 5082 event offload seam added to fork-only pin files (audit follow-up).

REPAIR DECISION (user, 2026-09-14): the two mis-slugged runs (01M2G27BSCZS, 01M2G8Q3SEN4) stay as-is — both terminal with merged PRs (#140/#141), the revisor targets the newest revisable run, and the next pass self-heals via content-addressed re-registration with prefixed keys. No data repair.

title: ENGINE: conductor develop leg dies in 0.3s — 'Agent session failed: expanding a skill reference' (run 01M2GJXV71TD, line DOWN)
description:
INCIDENT (2026-09-14 18:41:15 UTC, conductor pass 01M2GJXV71TDZ93SNRQF5P1WBJ, server 0.356.0-nightly.0): after a successful 11-minute survey (routed 'Work'), the develop stage started and FAILED in 296ms with failure.category=structural, message 'Precondition failed: Agent session failed: expanding a skill reference'.

ROOT CAUSE: pebble slash-expands standalone /name tokens (token = '/' at input start or after whitespace, lowercase name, ending at whitespace) in EVERY stage input — SkillExpansion::Skip is dead code in the pinned rev, no caller passes it, InputSource is ignored. The develop leg's ASSEMBLED input carried exactly one such token: '/tmp', sitting in a survey PAINPOINT ("fs_write blocks /tmp staging for byte-diff verification") that flowed into the next stage via context. One unknown token -> 'Unknown skill: /tmp' -> session death. Deterministic: any journalled prose with a bare slash-word kills the following stage. Prompt hygiene rules existed in survey.md AND the loop prompts ('never write a bare slash-word') — the model violated them, proving prose alone insufficient (fabro-8ee1 lesson again).

FIXED (2026-09-14, commit 356f6188a, direct agent work, user-approved line-down repair): stage sessions run SKILL-FREE by default; node attribute skills="discover" opts in. With no discovered skills, expand_input no-ops and the crash class disappears for every workflow. fabro exec (interactive) builds its own discovery — unaffected. Tests: default stage survives a ' /tmp ' prompt token even with a discoverable skill dir wired in; opt-in loads the skill section; accessor parsing. Scenario fixture updated to the opt-in contract.

FOLLOW-UP (filed separately): pebble upstream should wire InputSource into the expansion decision (External/Agent -> Skip; the enum docs already specify this semantics). Tracked as a task, external dependency.

title: UPSTREAM(pebble): wire InputSource into skill expansion — harness-synthesized input must not expand (SkillExpansion::Skip is dead code)
description:
Pinned pebble rev 69969420c901: runtime.rs run_prompt ALWAYS calls process_input(input, SkillExpansion::Apply) for PromptStart::Input. SkillExpansion::Skip has no caller — dead code. The SkillExpansion enum doc explicitly describes the intended semantics ('Input the harness synthesized is not [expanded]: a subagent's result envelope can hold `/tmp` or a slash-prefixed word of its own'), and CodingInput::with_source/InputSource exists precisely to mark such input — but the expansion decision never reads it.

Impact (fabro side, fabro-4dd8): any application that feeds harness-assembled prompts through prompt() and also configures skill discovery gets session-killing 'Unknown skill' errors from ordinary slash-paths in its input. Fabro worked around it by running stage sessions skill-free by default (skills="discover" opt-in) — correct for us, but the general fix belongs upstream.

PROPOSAL: in run_prompt, choose the expansion from input.source(): Prompt -> Apply, FollowUp/Agent/External -> Skip. This matches the documented semantics, changes nothing for interactive use, and un-breaks application integrations that want both skills and synthesized input.

When pebble ships it: consider re-enabling default skill discovery for fabro stages (revisit fabro-4dd8's default) and drop the workaround. Track upstream: lithoscomputer/pebble.

title: Evidence capture: emit a per-file diff-stat map at the top of evidence.nu output
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/evidence.nu, prepend a compact per-file plus/minus stat map ahead of the full diff so the reviewer can confirm capture completeness inline. reviewer@1 of run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC needed three nu str substring paging reads to reassemble the 55 KB blob capture, and silent python3 -c empty stdout cost extra verification turns before approval (reviewer journal painpoint). Orthogonal to open fabro-020b (churn capping), fabro-3c9d (budget), and fabro-9837 (blob-read protocol) — this adds a completeness summary, not a size cap or read protocol. Effect: fewer reviewer tool turns and less verification uncertainty per review. Basis: run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC, workflow version 4fd3342d2e46ca36d4b0eb600249e5fe5efd7c268e3a0135acc98509a627a903, commit 5f154a8bf642b47ed7311b5c58c2166024183e89

Effect: removes the mis-based diff call on every salvage pass (common after 429 and park failures). Basis: run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC, workflow version 4fd3342d2e46ca36d4b0eb600249e5fe5efd7c268e3a0135acc98509a627a903, commit 5f154a8bf642b47ed7311b5c58c2166024183e89

title: Focused tests beyond the touched-crate classes must name their acceptance bullet

Distinct from open fabro-ad1b, which is about citing bullets in the verification report — this constrains which extra tests may run at all, not how they are reported. Effect: about 5 min saved per implementer pass, redirected to tests that actually catch drift. Basis: run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC, workflow version 4fd3342d2e46ca36d4b0eb600249e5fe5efd7c268e3a0135acc98509a627a903, commit 5f154a8bf642b47ed7311b5c58c2166024183e89

title: Revisor analyst: every recommendation must name a known seed id — runs straddling a fix re-propose closed work
description: Run 01M2GYXX0JVV (revisor journal, analyze node): Ask-Fabro's top-impact recommendation (verify.nu interpolated regex) was already implemented on the base branch minutes before the target run's implementer finished — closed seed fabro-88f2, commit 29510ed. Only the revisor's CLOSED-seed check caught it. 5 of 9 analyst recommendations matched existing tracker seeds (fabro-88f2, fabro-c841, fabro-eaa0, fabro-9967, fabro-699f); without the pre-distill tracker check the file stage would merge duplicates away every pass. Demand: the analyst prompt must require a known seed id (or an explicit new-seed justification) for EVERY recommendation, not just some; dedupe load drops and straddled fixes stop being re-proposed.

title: Engine: expected-absent .codex/instructions.md read logs ERROR twice per session init — downgrade noise
description:

Seen on all runs of pass 01M2GVGMNGEK (develop 01M2GVW7GGGB, revisor 01M2GYXX0JVV, conductor itself). Runs succeed; the file is legitimately absent (AGENTS.md discovery probes the codex convention path). Demand: an expected-absent conventions file must not log ERROR (and not twice); downgrade to debug/info or pre-probe existence. Same log-noise family as fabro-9a42 — the ERROR channel must stay trustworthy for real failures.

Still reproducing 2026-09-15 18:00-18:02Z on pass 01M2K3KMMSET / develop 01M2K3NQEW0F (rootprint severity_number:17 sweep, 8 lines / 2h window; only ERROR source in the window).

Update 2026-09-16 (rootprint, `/iterate` cycle, window 06:30-08:45Z): still the ONLY ERROR source in the window — 62 ERROR lines in 2h (31 session inits x read+read_range pair, provider=zai model=glm-5.3, sandbox_driver_docker::fs, path /workspace/fabro/.codex/instructions.md). Evidence 2026-09-17 (line-watch rootprint sweep, conductor pass 01M2R8D1NZT5 window): still firing at scale — 2x ERROR `sandbox_driver_docker::fs: File "/workspace/fabro/.codex/instructions.md" was not found` per coding_session_initialize on EVERY session of every run (conductor 01M2R8D1NZT5, develop 01M2R8FHE6, revisor 01M2RBF9NGHQ; every ses_* init 17:00-19:00Z). title: Infra: extend mold linker anchoring to the toolchain/run image + CI runners (local-only today)
description:
STATUS (2026-09-15): mold is anchored ONLY on the local dev machine via ~/.cargo/config.toml [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu] rustflags = ["-C","link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold"] (mold 1.0.3 at /usr/bin/mold, verified end-to-end: cc -fuse-ld=mold links and runs, cargo build green). Repo .cargo/config.toml, CI workflows, and .fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain have NO mold (repo-wide grep zero hits) — CI, run-container qualitygates, and cargo-zigbuild release builds still use the default linker. USER DECISION 2026-09-15: anchor locally now, extend to the run image LATER ("auf das Run Image koennen wir das spaeter noch ausweiten").

DEMAND when picked up: (1) add mold to .fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain (apt-get install mold on ubuntu:24.04); (2) decide whether to anchor rustflags repo-wide in .cargo/config.toml (affects ALL builders incl. CI + zigbuild musl builds — musl static linking with mold needs care; may need target-specific scoping to gnu targets only) or per-image via CARGO env in the toolchain/CI images; (3) CI runners (ubuntu-latest) need mold installed or the config must stay conditional. RISK to respect: repo-wide rustflags invalidate every target cache once and break builds where mold is absent — that is exactly the run-container gate if the image is not updated first. ADR-0019 note: Dockerfile.toolchain is an agent-reachable capability surface — user approval required before the line touches it (needs-user stays until then).

title: Upstream merges must audit run-history verification tolerance before release
description: The 2026-09-15 netcup-5 crash loop (third ADR-0015-class occurrence: 01M1MGAPV4 2026-09-05, 01M0NGQXB 2026-09-13, 01M2DDACRP 2026-09-15) came from the v0.357 upstream usage rename (Run.billing -> Run.usage) landing without extending the era tolerance in verify_run_json_field. Policy demand: any upstream merge that renames or reshapes a Run-summary/event field must audit fork_legacy_read normalizers AND the run_summary_store verification tolerances, with a pinned real-row regression test, before the next nightly ships. Also: nightly images build from branch HEAD while reporting the bump commit's version string - the deployed binary cannot be identified from its version alone (image tag sha is the only trace); generalize the diag_replay_real_run test to take FABRO_DIAG_RUN so the run id is not re-hardcoded per incident.

Distinct from open fabro-7f58 (narrows which tests run once detected) and in-progress fabro-6e7f (dispatcher redesign explicitly keeps 'same rules as today', inheriting this blind spot). title: cli: fabro inspect fails with 'Invalid Response Payload' against mirtuell.net run payloads
description:
Basis: run 01M2K3KMMSET (conductor) and 01M2K3NQEW0F (develop child), observed 2026-09-15 ~18:20Z from the local checkout: 'fabro inspect <run-id> --server https://mirtuell.net' errors with 'Invalid Response Payload (b"...")' and dumps the raw server body; the server is version 0.357.0-nightly.0 (provenance.server.version in the payload). fabro ps and fabro events work fine against the same server, so the failure is specific to the inspect payload deserialization — likely schema drift between the local CLI's generated client and the nightly server's run response (candidate fields: provenance/definition_blob/spec_blob block). Iterate Phase 0 and line-watch rely on inspect for run queries. Demand: identify the field that breaks the client's strict parse, fix the client (or realign types via the OpenAPI source of truth), and add a conformance test covering the full run payload shape. Monitor note: until fixed, use fabro ps/events and the web_url for run details.

Evidence 2026-09-17: `fabro events 01M2R8D1NZT5 --server https://mirtuell.net` fails with the same 'Invalid Response Payload' error class while dumping the raw body — the deserialization drift is not inspect-specific; the events-listing path shares it. Conductor run events are unreadable from the CLI (monitoring workaround: read journals from the run branch instead).

title: Carry tool-result errors through the provider protocol instead of stdout text-sniffing
description: In run 01M2K73FA670FSBBYN0WJV0YTE the implementer's failed ml record (seq 108-110) round-tripped without a tool-result error flag — five agent.warning unsupported_control events (seq 113-155, 'this provider protocol does not support the tool result error flag') — so the model only saw failure in stdout text and retried blind. Change the agent-session/provider protocol layer (engine agent session in lib/components/fabro-workflow, pebble Environment protocol) to propagate the tool error flag where the provider supports it, or surface an explicit failure marker where it cannot. Expected effect: deterministic error signaling for failed tool calls, removing one blind-retry class across all agent stages. Distinct from fabro-96bd (prompt-side ml-record flag contract) and fabro-9a42 (log flood): no open seed covers protocol-level error-flag propagation.\n\nBasis: run 01M2K73FA670FSBBYN0WJV0YTE, workflow version ab2ee24a456a34dfd349075bbbf8a38de2d071f30582720402cc4fedd93a2170, commit 62efab0764b33a87b794406141628d4b874e5d03

title: Revisor analyze: fold select-step journal painpoints into revision_findings — upstream stage painpoints die in context
description: Basis: .fabro/workflows/revisor/workflow.fabro line 91 (analyze node context_allow_keys includes 'journal') + prompts/analyze.md inspected 2026-09-15: the analyzer's preamble carries the SELECT step's journal painpoints (engine accumulates the journal key across stages), but analyze.md Step 4 distills ONLY the fabro_ask answer into revision_findings; 'painpoint' appears solely in the analyzer's OUTPUT journal contract. The bookkeeper (file.md Step 1) files seeds exclusively from revision_findings, so select-step painpoints (tool field gaps, stale-evidence detection friction, sandbox-signal issues) never become seeds — they die in context. This is the narrow transport-gap sibling of fabro-6ab7 (conductor runs as revisable units): here the channel already exists, only the instruction is missing. Demand: extend analyze.md Step 4 with an explicit input: journal painpoints already in the analyzer's context from earlier revisor stages (select) are seed-candidate material with the SAME rules as ask-answer findings (tracker search first, one-concrete-change filter, duplicate_of protocol); the analyzer CONTRIBUTES ITS ANALYSIS of each painpoint as a proper revision_findings candidate (title/description/priority, what-where-effect grounded in the painpoint evidence) — not a verbatim relay: distillation judgment stays in the analyze step, mechanical sd search + sd create stay in the file step (existing role split: analyst never files, bookkeeper never analyzes); the finding objects flow to the bookkeeper in the standard shape. Expected effect: revisor-loop stage painpoints get the same seed path as run-diff findings without a new node or graph change (ADR-0008: prompt-only change, no graph/prompt/script unit split needed here).

Expected effect: reviewer anomaly adjudication only sees actual residue/scope-creep, not spec-mandated prompt edits. Related but distinct from fabro-020b (caps loop-churn diff size, does not touch the classification).

title: Develop PROJECT_FACTS: name the merge-target branch (origin/denkhaus) and use it in implementer duplicate preflight
description: What/where: the duplicate-run preflight in .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md hardcodes 'git fetch origin main && git log --oneline origin/main --grep <current_seed_id>' with '(base branch is main)'. But origin/main is the upstream fabro-sh mirror while the seed loop integrates on origin/denkhaus, so the preflight greps a branch that never carries seed merges — the guard is inert in exactly the claim-race class it was built for. Change: add a 'merge-target branch: origin/denkhaus' line to .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/project-facts.md (no branch/merge fact exists there today; anchor after the 'Repo wiring' bullet block, around line 21ff) and reference that fact from the implementer step-1 preflight instead of the main literal. Expected effect: the preflight actually detects duplicates merged to the loop's base branch. Complements fabro-1128 (same wrong-branch confusion fixed only in the revisor prompt). CORRECTION (planner, run 01M2MGAQ4TRWHGEY34P17K2R4D, 2026-09-16): the originally-cited planner 'git remote show origin' per-claim probe NO LONGER EXISTS anywhere under .fabro/workflows/develop/ — that sub-item is already moot and must NOT be attempted; only the project-facts fact line and the implementer preflight rewrite remain. From line-watch addition (fabro-7280, closed as duplicate): also specify the degraded mode when the preflight fetch itself fails (journal the failure and proceed — never dead-end the implementer on a fetch error); and note the silent-failure mode is the dangerous part (git fetch origin main succeeds mechanically because the stale ref exists, so the guard reports healthy while protecting nothing). Basis: run 01M2KC8BDP4AJZ5NR0CY2KF5JZ, workflow version 0a429145a094e46a9426d9a68bbad4a08facc0ea114b9e4840307bc7d7e1265b, commit 549e2a3f.

title: Fix duplicate-run preflight branch: landed implementer.md greps origin/main but run PRs merge into denkhaus - protection is a silent no-op
description: Basis: PR #159 (run 01M2KC8BDP4, seed fabro-5656, merged 549e2a3f8 2026-09-15): the seed spec correctly used a placeholder (git log origin/<base> --grep <seed-id>), but the implementation hardcoded <base> = 'main' with the note '(base branch is main)'. In THIS repo the line merges run PRs into 'denkhaus' (all of #153-#159); origin/main is a stale upstream merge point (#875) that never carries line commits. The preflight therefore ALWAYS finds no match and protects against nothing - the seed's own basis scenario (fabro-6a5a, 731s/USD0.37 burned until a human halted the run) would recur. It fails silently because 'git fetch origin main' succeeds mechanically. Layering defect too (ADR-0013): implementer.md is project-agnostic; a base-branch assumption belongs in PROJECT_FACTS. Fix: (a) add the line branch to PROJECT_FACTS (e.g. 'Line branch run PRs merge into: denkhaus') and reference it from the preflight text; or (b) read the run's base branch from context if the engine exposes it. While at it: the fetch+grep pattern should also cover the case where the fetch fails (degraded mode: journal and proceed, never dead-end). Reviewer and (pending) revisor of run 01M2KC8BDP4 both missed this - prompt text reads plausible, only repo reality contradicts it.

title: Workflow prompts must be seed-id-agnostic — revisor analyze enforces a deterministic literal check (status claims rot, provenance belongs in seeds)
description:
User directive 2026-09-15 (line-watch session): prompts in .fabro/workflows/*/prompts/ must not carry absolute seed-id literals - closed seeds turn them into outdated claims, and every stage re-reads the archaeology each run. Two rot classes measured today (~40 real fabro-XXXX literals across develop/revisor/conductor/merge-upstream prompts): (1) STATUS ASSERTIONS - the worst class: e.g. the just-landed duplicate-run preflight family note says 'the durable engine fixes fabro-6b58 and fabro-9372 remain open' (implementer.md, PRs #159/#160) - true today, silently false the day those close; also 'until fabro-94e8', 'known gap, fabro-c16d'. Prompts must state the RULE semantically ('durable engine fixes for this class are tracked as engine seeds'), never tracker state. (2) PROVENANCE CITATIONS - '(fabro-1dae, 2026-09-02: ...)' lesson archaeology: not lies but token+attention cost on every stage read; the durable home is the seed/journal/ADR. Demand: (a) revisor analyze.md gains a deterministic check: grep 'fabro-[0-9a-f]{4}' over all workflow prompt files, for each hit sd show the id; a literal in a status-claiming sentence OR citing a CLOSED seed is a revision_finding (strip or rephrase semantically); preferred end state is a fully id-free prompt set (strict default, user decision); (b) prefer a small nu lint script the analyzer calls over LLM classification of sentence intent; (c) new prompt edits land without id literals going forward (reviewer/naming check). Exceptions only where the id IS the contract name may be rephrased semantically instead (e.g. the planner superseded-close rule citing fabro-d183 can name the rule, not the id). Basis: PRs #159/#160 (549e2a3f8, bd41cbac4), grep survey 2026-09-15, user session directive.

EXTENSION 2026-09-16 (user directive, `/integrate` pass on PRs #163-#194): the class is BROADER than seed-id literals — incoming prompt changes again polluted workflow assets with PR numbers, run ids, and commit shas (merge-leg.md '(#832 contract)'/'(fabro-e297, #832 run-intent contract)'; planner.md 'run 01M23KJM3SM70S2S6QSSEWSJPY ... seq 111-113', 'run 01M256QJB48JK8BXJE1TVM2HYS ... PR #115 ... fix commit 7ae575c'; implementer.md 'run 01M0WWKAQCWZC0Q0JK019H0ZC7'; develop/workflow.fabro comment '01M2N1G834RTCSZNX7EK40G3SE'; closeout.nu runtime park message 'caught in run 01M23J61HH8Z'). USER GRUND SATZ: workflows stay ABSTRACT and PROJECT-AGNOSTIC without endangering function; every agent that changes a prompt must know that volatile local evidence (run ids, PR numbers, commit shas, dated cost narratives, machine-specific paths) is FORBIDDEN in workflow assets — evidence lives in the seed's Basis line, never in the prompt. ADDITIONAL DEMANDS: (a) extend .fabro/scripts/prompt-lint.nu with a mechanical ban over .fabro/workflows/** (prompts, workflow.fabro, workflow.toml, scripts' user-facing strings; facts carriers facts.md/project-facts.md exempt for PROJECT FACTS but not for evidence archaeology): run-id ULIDs (01[A-Z0-9]{24}), 'PR #<n>' / '(#<n>)' references, bare 40/7-hex commit shas, /home/<user> paths; wire into validate-workflows like the existing checks. (b) Purge existing occurrences: rules keep their normative content, evidence clauses move to the corresponding seeds' Basis/journals; the closeout.nu park message drops the fabro-9967/run archaeology and states the rule only. (c) implementer.md gains the hygiene clause so the rule is enforced at the point where prompts get edited. Basis: `/integrate` 2026-09-16 diff audit d3a04bcc6~65..d3a04bcc6 (grep hits in 6 files); user directive quote: 'jeder agent, der prompts ändert, muss wissen, dass das nicht erlaubt ist und gegen den grundsatz spricht, workflows möglichst abstrakt und projekt agnostisch zu halten ohne die eigentliche funktion zu gefährden'.

## PROGRESS (2026-09-19, agent-executed)

Phase 1 done — provenance-literal class purged and gate-enforced:
- Purged ALL run-id and PR-number literals from every workflow prompt (16
  sites across facts/implementer/planner/reviewer; lessons kept, attribution
  moved to seed bases). Zero remaining (mechanical check).
- prompt-lint.nu gained check 6: run-id literals (prefixed and bare) and
  PR-number references in prompt .md files are ERRORS — red-before proven
  against the pre-purge implementer.md (6 errors), green after.
- prompt-lint is now WIRED INTO scripts/qualitygate.nu's loop-asset tier
  (both gate paths) — it previously ran only via the standalone
  `just validate-workflows`, which nothing invoked on prompt-touching diffs;
  that gap is how 31 volatile references accumulated silently.
- User directives backing this: 2026-09-19 (twice — steer-citation class
  and the 'run 01M0WWKAQCWZC0Q0JK019H0ZC7' class), original 2026-09-15.

Phase 2 REMAINS OPEN: the seed-id-agnostic corpus rewrite (status
assertions like 'fabro-XXXX remains open' must become semantic rules;
~40 literals). The lint's rule 1 still only checks resolvability.

title: Server-side sandbox retention: reap terminal run containers (retention supervisor)
description:
## Demand

Run containers survive their runs forever on the Docker provider: the engine stops the sandbox at run end (sandbox.stop.completed) but never removes it. On prod (netcup-5, fabro-tofu) this filled 188 GB of 503 GB in ~2.5 days (48 exited containers, top ones 38/36.7/18.6/17.3 GB — `/repos` clones + cargo/rustup caches in the writable layer). Manual cleanup on 2026-09-16 freed it back to 25 GB; the policy must make that automatic.

## Design (decided with user, 2026-09-16 session)

1. **Owner: server-side retention supervisor** following the existing spawn_*_supervisor pattern in fabro-server/src/serve.rs (like spawn_pull_request_staleness_supervisor). NOT engine-at-completion (worker can crash before deferred delete), NOT host cron/docker system prune (unscoped, no run-state knowledge). Leave environment lifecycle.auto_stop for Docker unimplemented — do not build two disposal mechanisms.
2. **Policy: time-based base + budget ceiling as emergency brake.** Base: reap sandbox of runs that are terminal AND older than X (default 48h since terminal transition). Ceiling: optional max total container-bytes budget; when exceeded, reap oldest-terminal-first beyond the age floor. Config in server settings ([server.retention] with enabled/terminal_age/budget), default-on with sane defaults for prod.
3. **Protection rules: NEVER reap** non-terminal runs (paused/blocked/HITL may wait for days — evidence: run 01M2DXVAJBY1XBWBSNKNG0M6DM container up 2 days), runs with environment lifecycle.preserve=true, and the active/paused set. Run records, event timeline, artifacts, scratch are NEVER deleted by the policy (user directive: run data must not be deleted — container-only reap).
4. **Reap marking (v1 must-have):** write a run event (sandbox.reaped with timestamp + reason) and a durable flag on the run record. In-place resume/rewind of a reaped run must fail with an actionable error pointing to fork (today initialize.rs gives generic "cannot resume run: run sandbox is missing" / reconnect NotFound). Fork already re-materializes from run data (fork.rs reads checkpoint run_commit_sha, clears projection.sandbox, clones fresh) — it is the sanctioned path.
5. **Scope safety:** only delete through the driver's Ownership scope (labels sh.fabro.managed=true + sh.fabro.run_id), same as delete_run_internal does via reconnect_for_run + sandbox.delete(). Never touch unlabeled containers on the shared host daemon.
6. **Observability:** warn!/info! log per reaped sandbox, count+bytes surfaced via /system/df, journal-free (this is engine side). Follow docs/internal/logging-strategy.md and events-strategy.md before adding events.

## Domain fit

Glossary already models this: a terminal run whose sandbox is gone is a stale-evidence run; revisor select.md disqualifies sandbox_available == false hard-precondition (fabro-8d30a). Reaped runs therefore drop out of revisor selection automatically and audibly (revisor journals "N runs blocked (… no live sandbox)"). IMPORTANT: the conductor line is ACTIVE (user re-enabled it 2026-09-16) — the revisor revises newest-first with bounded passes, so the retention age X (48h) must stay above the revisor catch-up horizon; runs reaped before the revisor reached them are permanently unrevisable by design. Surface reaped-count in /system/df so the backlog trade-off stays visible.

## Acceptance (sketch)

- Supervisor reaps terminal>Xh non-preserve containers on a Docker provider; paused/HITL/running untouched; run records intact.
- Reaped run: event written, sandbox_available=false, resume gives actionable "sandbox reaped — fork this run" error, fork works from checkpoint.
- Budget ceiling evicts oldest-terminal-first only when over budget.
- Unit + conformance tests per docs/internal/testing-strategy.md; e2e via #[e2e_test] where Docker is available.

Basis: user session 2026-09-16 (fabro-tofu disk incident, manual cleanup evidence), repo commit 3e720ed03, docker system df before/after on netcup-5. Conductor active since 2026-09-16 (user re-enabled).

title: Resume re-materialization: rebuild sandbox from run data when container was reaped
description:
Deferred follow-up to fabro-3377 (do NOT start while fabro-3377 is open — the retention v1 marks reaped runs and points users at fork; this seed removes that limitation).

## Demand

Today in-place resume/rewind hard-fails when the sandbox is gone (pipeline/initialize.rs: "cannot resume run: run sandbox is missing", or reconnect NotFound when the record exists but the container was reaped). All durable state to rebuild exists: run record carries CloneRequest coordinates (origin/branch/tag/exact SHA), checkpoints are git commits pushed to the run branch (lifecycle/git.rs push_run_branch; residue quarantine guarantees stage work is committed at cycle boundaries). Fork already materializes a fresh sandbox exactly this way (operations/fork.rs: run_commit_sha + projection.sandbox = None).

## Scope (sketch)

On resume of a run whose sandbox record is marked reaped: re-materialize instead of failing — clone run branch at last checkpoint SHA into a fresh container (reuse the fork materialization path), attach as the run sandbox, proceed. Semantics: state = last checkpoint; uncommitted inter-checkpoint working-tree state and build caches are knowingly lost (perf cost, not correctness). Must only trigger on the explicit reaped marker from fabro-3377, never silently mask provider outages.

Basis: user session 2026-09-16 (question "kann die engine nicht aus run daten einen geprunten container wieder resumen"), repo commit 3e720ed03, depends on fabro-3377.

title: Revisor theme-search discipline: sd search is AND-strict — one keyword per query, sd show for id lookups
description:
Revisor Step 3/file theme searches use `sd search "<theme keyword>"`, but sd search is AND/phrase-strict: multi-word queries like 'acceptance bullet cite' return ZERO hits even when fabro-ad1b's title contains those exact words, and bare id lookups return nothing (title/description text only). Evidence: revisor run 01M2MKZZVHDZZNB54F667Q03N0 (PR #166) Step 3 had to fall back to per-id `sd show`; revisor run 01M2MNVWBY9MKK3SHCGS0K1G8N hit the same class (already noted inside fabro-5ff7's scope for the duplicate check). False zero-hit searches risk duplicate seed filing.

Target: .fabro/workflows/revisor/prompts/analyze.md (Step 3 guidance, ~line 39) and prompts/file.md (~line 15) — pin the query discipline: ONE keyword per sd search; if zero hits, drop to a broader single token before concluding "no duplicate"; for id-cited candidates use `sd show <id>`, never sd search. Optional upstream ask (separate concern, note only): OR-ranked tokenization in sd search.

Expected effect: theme search stops producing false no-match results; fewer duplicate seeds; less per-pass sd show churn. Basis: journal 01M2MKZZVHDZZNB54F667Q03N0 analyze painpoint, 2026-09-16.

title: Tracker: sd close --append-note (upstream) — document the safe body round-trip for reason-closes
description:
Reason-before-close (fabro-02c4) currently requires re-emitting the FULL seed body via `sd update --description` just to append a closure reason: `sd show` prose formatting (title line, spacing) makes the round-trip error-prone and risks clobbering body text. Evidence: revisor run 01M2MKZZVHDZZNB54F667Q03N0 (PR #166) file-node painpoint while closing fabro-2be2 as duplicate of fabro-55a7.

Fix: upstream seeds CLI — `sd close --append-note "<reason>"` or `sd update --append-description`. Interim (this repo, concrete target): docs/agents/issue-tracker.md — document the safe round-trip recipe for agents: `sd show <id> --format json` -> edit the description field -> `sd update <id> --description`, never retype from prose output.

Expected effect: closure reasons stop risking body corruption; one command instead of a fragile full-body rewrite per documented close. Basis: journal 01M2MKZZVHDZZNB54F667Q03N0 file painpoint, 2026-09-16.

title: Revisor stale-evidence gate starves the backlog — version equality only for prompt-bound findings (design fork)
description:
The revisor select rule "revisable = terminal AND live sandbox AND workflow_version_id == newest run's version" starves the revision backlog: on 2026-09-16 08:38Z the pool was 1 selectable of 14 (9 stale-evidence version drift, most also sandbox-less). The loop is self-referential — nearly every landed PR touches workflow assets, so every merge invalidates prior runs as revision targets; production (~1 run/pass) equals drain (1 run/pass) and the backlog structurally never shrinks. The premise "the run's workflow definition is stale => its painpoints are stale" is only true for PROMPT-CONTENT findings; painpoints about tools, journal shape, gate behavior, and the sd CLI are version-independent.

Design fork (needs user decision, ADR-0015 premise): (a) classify findings by version-sensitivity at file time — require version equality only for prompt-bound revisions, treat tooling findings as revisable from any version; (b) relax the pool rule to "terminal + live sandbox" and carry version drift as a warning marker in the revision report; (c) keep as is and accept the starvation (then fabro-52a9's survey wording fix is the honest minimum). Related: fabro-8d30 part b (fresh analyst sandboxes) fixes only the sandbox half; fabro-52a9 (survey wording); fabro-6ab7 (pool extension to conductor runs — orthogonal drain widening). Basis: revisor run 01M2MNVWBY select observations, 2026-09-16; architecture review C5 (session 2026-09-16).

Update 2026-09-16 (escalation, revisor 01M2N6Z6HMP0 / PR #184, beat 23): the blocked share keeps climbing as every landing churns versions — 21 of 22 develop runs now stale-evidence (7 also sandbox-less); exactly 1 selectable. The structural starvation predicted by this seed is now the dominant selector observation; drain depends on each pass landing while the newest run stays unrevised. A user decision on the version-sensitivity classification (a/b/c) is the unlock.

User decision 2026-09-17 (needs-user triage): GO - relax the stale-evidence gate to age-weighted selection so the revisor backlog drains instead of starving on version equality (keep newest-first preference, add age-based fallback).

title: dup-run-check.nu: emit closure=self|foreign from Fabro-Run trailers so self-closures are mechanically distinct
description:
The deterministic duplicate-run preflight (.fabro/scripts/dup-run-check.nu, fabro-8c75 follow-up) reports verdict 'duplicate' for the develop loop's NORMAL success path: when the target run's OWN PR closes its seed, the matched merge commit (e.g. b9d1dcf for fabro-4cd8, PR #169) carries the 'Fabro-Run: <run-id>' trailer proving self-closure, but the verdict JSON exposes no closing-run identity — the revisor had to inspect the commit trailer manually to avoid misreporting a healthy run as a duplicate (revisor run 01M2MS51R7WPT13SZYK9Q9QZ2S, analyze painpoint, 2026-09-16).

Fix: in dup-run-check.nu, read the full commit message of each implementation match (git log --format="%B" or -1 <sha>), parse the 'Fabro-Run:' trailer, and emit closure: self|foreign per match; optionally accept --self <run-id> to auto-downgrade self-closures. Consumers (implementer preflight, revisor analyze Step 3.5) then trust the verdict mechanically: self = the run's own closure (healthy), foreign = real duplicate. Expected effect: no manual trailer adjudication; verdict JSON is sufficient. Basis: run 01M2MS51R7WPT13SZYK9Q9QZ2S analyze painpoint, 2026-09-16.

Update 2026-09-16 (2nd occurrence, revisor run 01M2MV80PF3X0X0G1F26RBNNW7, beat 4): sharper variant — tracker_status 'closed' with EMPTY implementation_matches and 0 filed_only (the closing squash commit 1fbf03c / PR #171 carries the seed id neither in subject nor matchable body), so verdict 'duplicate' came from the tracker alone with NO adjudication evidence in the JSON; the revisor had to dig branch history manually to find the closing commit and its Fabro-Run trailer (self-closure, verdict correctly withheld). The fix must ALSO cover this arm: when the tracker says closed but no landed-PR match is found, resolve the closing evidence (last commit touching .seeds for the id, or sd's closedAt) and classify self|foreign from ITS trailer — the verdict JSON must never leave the consumer without closure identity. Related observation preserved in .fabro/reviews/develop/01M2MTN5MJ17SA67M8N82HZMSE.md.

Update 2026-09-16 (3rd occurrence, revisor run 01M2MWHP97R1Y9PV4727JVTCV9 / PR #174, beat 7): same class on fabro-50c9/#173 (matches present, trailers name the target run) — the painpoint now fires on EVERY revisor pass (3/3 consecutive), each costing a manual trailer inspection before the healthy verdict. Prioritization evidence: this is now a per-pass tax, not an edge case.

Update 2026-09-16 (4th occurrence, revisor run 01M2N0E9MZ5 / PR #176, beat 13): tracker-closed arm again — seed fabro-45bf closedAt 11:21:34Z equals the target run's own closeout; PR #175 merged as 1994233 with the run's Fabro-Run trailer; verdict overridden on trailer evidence. Now 4/4 consecutive revisor passes pay the manual adjudication. Priority raised 2 -> 1 per fabro-11d3 tie-break (observed failure class, per-pass tax).

Update 2026-09-16 (5th occurrence, revisor run 01M2N1RRTKXE / PR #178, beat 15): NEW ARM — tracker status 'in_progress' (not closed) while the run's OWN verification-only PR #177 (d1011ac) matched as a landed-PR implementation -> verdict 'duplicate' although no foreign closure exists; adjudicated by hand from tracker + Fabro-Run trailer. The fix must classify closure identity from the trailer REGARDLESS of tracker status (closed|in_progress|open), and the in_progress-with-own-PR case is exactly the stuck-seed hygiene gap (see fabro-3c9d close this beat).

Update 2026-09-16 (7th occurrence, revisor 01M2N5C6PEK / PR #182, beat 21 — mechanical nuance): the history leg can ALSO return 0 implementation matches when the seed id sits beyond GitHub's squash-subject truncation (the id was in the full PR title, the merged subject cut it) — the fix should fall back to matching the tracker's closedAt evidence (or git log --grep against the full body) when the subject-arm is empty but the tracker says closed.

Update 2026-09-16 (IMPLEMENTED via PR #185, run 01M2N8B4QY43E5JTW3CQ1G39BA; line-watch-verified): dup-run-check.nu now parses Fabro-Run trailers per implementation match and emits trailer_run + closure: self|foreign; --self <run-id> downgrades self-closures to clean with a closure_note; tracker-status independence proven (fake-sd wrapper test); .seeds close-patch discrimination separates closeout merges from seeds:sync commits; empty-match arms resolve closing_evidence. Live verification (beat 25): fabro-4cd8 --self 01M2MRWD9B8 → verdict clean, closure self; fabro-1e9f plain → duplicate, closure foreign (legacy preserved). title: Engine: {{ context.NAME }} interpolation at stage dispatch — narrow second render pass over per-node context
description:
Stage prompts cannot interpolate run CONTEXT values today: TemplateContext (lib/foundation/fabro-template/src/lib.rs) binds only goal + inputs.* (workflow.toml [run.inputs]) + vars.* (server variable store, snapshotted at run CREATE time), all rendered during materialization — by handler time node.prompt_or_label() is final text (handler/prompt.rs:62), and context values reach agents only via the ## Context section (preamble_allow_keys) and the context_read tool.

ASKED CAPABILITY (user, 2026-09-16): a `{{ context.NAME }}` token namespace rendered in a SECOND, narrow pass at stage dispatch (prompt + agent handlers), so prompts can inline values earlier stages produced.

Design constraints:
- ENVELOPE: the token must resolve ONLY against the node's resolved per-node context projection — exactly the preamble_allow_keys set that governs the ## Context section. Anything else is an envelope bypass (a node reading keys its allowlist hides).
- STRICT resolution for context tokens: an unresolved `{{ context.NAME }}` fails the stage with a diagnostic (a typo must not silently render empty); vars/inputs keep their existing materialization-time behavior.
- INJECTION: values are agent-written strings landing inside instruction prose — same trust class as the ## Context section, but inline placement is more injection-prone; document the data-slot discipline (context tokens in command arguments/data lines, not inside instruction sentences).

Immediate loop wins once landed: (1) revisor analyze/file Step 3.5 collapses — `nu .fabro/scripts/dup-run-check.nu {{ context.current_seed_id }}` removes the seed-id recovery sub-step entirely (seed id flows from planner context, not journal grep); (2) revisor prose can name `{{ context.revisor_target_run_id }}` directly; (3) implementer briefs can cite `{{ context.current_seed_title }}`. Note for scoping: static repo facts stay in the facts.md includes — vars are create-time snapshots and do not replace stage-time context. Basis: engine reading session 2026-09-16 (file_inlining.rs, variable_expansion.rs, operations/create.rs template_context, handler/prompt.rs); user request same day.

User decision 2026-09-17 (needs-user triage): GO - toolchain image bake WITHOUT java.

MULTI-ARM CONSOLIDATION (ADR-0022 same-file rule; user decision 2026-09-17: GO, one image rebuild, no java):
