title: Architect workflow: reusable architecture-pass flow self-gated on the deterministic friction score
description:
GOAL (user decision 2026-09-16): a dedicated, REUSABLE architect workflow triggered by a deterministic condition — the systemic-friction score now implemented as `.fabro/scripts/friction-score.nu` (0.0–1.0 from seed+run metrics: drain deficit, backlog stagnation, starvation, stuck claims; verdict normal|grind|architecture-due, JSON out; today's live value 0.35 grind).

DESIGN (ADR-0008: workflow as one unit; self-gating so the automation stays trivial):
1. Assets: `.fabro/workflows/architect/` — workflow.fabro + prompts/{survey,analyze,file}.md + facts.md include (same seam pattern as conductor/revisor) + workflow.toml (revisor-shaped: run_branch/meta_branch push, PR enabled, auto_merge, glm models; NO fabro_tools beyond what analyze needs).
2. Graph: start -> survey (DETERMINISTIC prelude + LLM-lite): run `nu .fabro/scripts/friction-score.nu --threshold 0.6`; verdict < architecture-due OR cooldown marker (.fabro/architecture/<date>.md exists within 48h) -> exit "Nothing to do" (natural). Else build the exploration base: git churn hot spots (`git log --format= --name-only -n <window>` frequency), open-seed digest (sd list label/priority summary), ADR/facts file list -> context keys.
3. analyze (reasoning high): ONE `fabro_ask` call with an architecture-scoped question (interplay/hot-spot/ gap-misconception-optimization axes; grounded in the survey context, NOT a single run) — mirror of the revisor's verbatim-question discipline; answer persisted to `.fabro/architecture/reviews/<date>.md`.
4. file (deterministic bookkeeping, revisor file-node pattern): sd create per finding (--labels revision; capability/design forks -> needs-user), basis lines, cooldown marker `.fabro/architecture/<date>-pass.md`, commit exactly the artifact paths. Self-parking: < 2 candidates -> marker-only pass (nothing systemic left — the natural regenerative stop).
5. Reusable = parameterized: `[run.inputs]` for scope hint + threshold override; prompts project-agnostic (facts include); the score script is standalone (consumed by survey, by line-watch, and by humans).
6. Automation (user registers in UI): dumb daily cron; the workflow's own survey gates on score + cooldown — trigger condition lives INSIDE the flow, so the automation never needs logic.

RATIONALE: the 2026-09-16 manual architecture pass (C1-C6) preceded 4 consecutive zero-seed revisor passes and lifted drain/inflow 0.43->0.79 — empirical support for architecture passes as the systemic-refill lever when the score says grind. Related: fabro-88a4 (open-backlog digest — input to analyze), fabro-11d3 (tie-break failure classes), fabro-0195 (declarative automations), fabro-b11a (Chisel grill). Blindness guard: starvation is a positive-architecture signal (idle capacity), NOT health — the score separates them; the revisor's stale-evidence blindness is tracked separately (fabro-4c02).
Basis: user design session 2026-09-16 (drain/inflow discussion + score requirement); friction-score.nu landed same day; line-watch beats 1-15 metrics.

title: Revisor file stage must not call sd sync — it splits the revision into two commits
description: The revisor file node's bookkeeping ran `sd sync` mid-stage, which auto-commits .seeds as its OWN commit before the artifact commit — splitting one revision into two commits (seeds 6719fcb + marker 781bd9a, revisor run 01M2N40T0HTE, PR #180). title: Engine: automation environment update silently stops schedule evaluation (conductor idle 3h+, enabled:true, no scheduler lines)
description:
After the user changed conductor-fabro's environment_id from 'default' to 'toolchain' via UI (~2026-09-16 17:55Z), the automation scheduler stopped evaluating its */30 trigger: ticks at 18:00/18:30/19:00/19:30/20:00/20:30Z produced ZERO automation_run log lines (previously every tick logged 'Run created' or 'skipped: overlapping'; last created run 01M2NM9E7 at 17:30:05Z, last activity 17:57Z). The API still reports the schedule trigger enabled:true with expression */30; on_overlap=skip; breaker consecutive_count=0. No panics, restarts, or scheduler WARN/ERROR in service logs (rootprint, service_name=fabro, 4h window). Hypothesis: the automation UPDATE path detaches or corrupts the in-memory schedule registration while the persisted view stays enabled — scheduler only recovers on server restart or schedule re-toggle. DEMAND: reproduce (update an automation's environment via API/UI, watch scheduler ticks), fix the update path to preserve/re-register schedule evaluation, add a regression test (update-then-tick), and consider a startup/purge reconcile that re-registers all enabled schedules. Related: fabro-0195 (declarative automations). Basis: rootprint automation_run timeline 15:00-17:30Z vs silence after; GET /api/v1/automations 2026-09-16 ~20:45Z (enabled:true); fabro ps -a newest conductor run 01M2NM9E7 succeeded 17:57Z; user UI action 17:55Z (environment flip).

WITHDRAWN (same day, ~18:05Z): premise error by the reporter — local +0200 timestamps were misread as UTC. Corrected timeline: last tick before the check was 17:30:05Z (run 01M2NM9E7, ended 17:57Z); the check ran ~17:5xZ, BEFORE the next due tick (18:00Z) — ZERO ticks were actually missed. The user then toggled both schedulers off/on, and the 18:00:06Z tick fired normally (conductor run 01M2NP0ANX created, queued, running). No scheduler stall is evidenced; whether the pre-toggle state would also have fired is unknowable (toggle confound), but there is no longer an incident to fix. Residual watch item only: if a future automation environment-update is followed by genuinely MISSED due ticks (log nothing at a due time), re-open this class against the update path.

DEFENSIVE FIX LANDED 2026-09-16 (PR #199, commit 40470d6fc): the line implemented 'preserve cursor timing on revision-only automation updates' while this seed was still open on its base — the update-path guard exists despite the withdrawn premise. The line's own closure carried no closeReason in the record (fabro-02c4 opacity class); this union line keeps both facts: premise withdrawn (reporter clock error) AND the class now defended by #199. Re-open trigger stays the watch condition above.

Update 2026-09-16 ~20:15Z (line-watch, recurrence): the stall RECURRED after the earlier recovery — no automation-created run for slots 19:30/20:00/20:30Z although the last pass went terminal ~19:05Z and NO new env update is known in between (the earlier restart healed only ~75 min). Either a second UI mutation (e.g. the architect-fabro registration window) re-triggered the detach, or the detach has a spontaneous arm — both contradict a pure env-update coupling. API again shows enabled:true/breaker:0; scheduler ticks are INFO (not ingested) so rootprint is silent-by-design. Bridge: line-watch manually created+started a conductor pass (01M2NVVB4KQ8A5XBPBX6GCWNFT, fabro create/start --server mirtuell) per the iterate down-line repair rule; the DEFENSIVE fix from PR #199 is landed but NOT deployed — image-release + tofu apply remains the durable resolution, plus consider seeding an automation watchdog (cron that alerts when automation_runs lag > N slots).
closeReason: withdrawn: reporter timezone error (local +0200 read as UTC) — no tick was due before the check; the 18:00:06Z tick fired normally after the user's off/on toggle (run 01M2NP0ANX). Description carries the corrected timeline + residual watch condition for the automation-update path. | amended: defensive fix landed via PR #199 (cursor-timing preservation); premise error noted; residual watch condition in description.

title: Engine: run-PR squash reverts concurrent landed work (stale workspace tree + tracker-only branch update)
description:
CRITICAL ENGINE DEFECT (incident 2026-09-17, PR #216): a run PR squash-merge SILENTLY REVERTED concurrent landed work on denkhaus. Mechanics, verified in git: (1) revisor run 01M2QD9WWHS8 started 11:21 from pre-push denkhaus (e615466f6); its workspace never contained the engine fix d28750736 pushed at 11:22 (commit b5ccd4dd9's squash base was 39325ff45, but the squashed TREE was the stale workspace). (2) The dirty-branch repair step (452dd28cd "Merge base into run branch: tracker JSONL closed-wins union") unions ONLY .seeds/issues.jsonl - it does NOT bring code changes into the workspace or rebase the run branch. (3) The publish squash then replaced denkhaus content with the workspace tree: DELETED the fabro-986b executor/graph seams + both fork pin files + touchpoints row + mulch record, reverted the iterate skill edits, and dropped 5 tracker records (2 body updates, 3 assignments) via the closed-wins union picking the branch's older snapshot. Restore landed as 800301797 (tests re-verified 121/121 + 15/15). DEMAND: the publish path must not be able to delete files it did not touch - either (a) the branch update performs a REAL merge/rebase of the full base into the run branch (workspace refresh included), or (b) the publish computes a proper diff of run-authored changes only (its own commits) instead of squashing the workspace tree, or (c) the merge gate rejects a run PR whose diff deletes paths outside the run's own change scope. Also harden the tracker union: my body updates and assignments were lost to the branch's stale snapshot despite newer updatedAt. Related but not covering: fabro-a01f (stale tracker snapshot -> claim race), fabro-b4ed (child PRs must base on the line branch), fabro-8c75 (merge-commit matching). Severity rationale: this corrupts the line branch itself - any concurrent push during a run is at risk; the fork-presence pins only red the NEXT build, they do not prevent the revert.

## USER DECISION (2026-09-17, grill in chat): implement (b) + (c)

- (b) Diff-based publish: the run PR carries ONLY the run's own committed changes (its checkpoint commits between run base and run end) instead of squashing the whole workspace tree - what the run never touched, it cannot delete; the defect becomes structurally impossible.
- (c) Gate safety net: the merge gate rejects run-PR diffs that delete paths outside the run's own change scope (e.g. lib/ deletions from a revisor that only wrote .fabro/ files).
- (a) full merge at branch-update deliberately NOT chosen (workspace staleness remains).
- Also harden the tracker JSONL union so newer updatedAt always wins across the squash (my body updates and assignments were lost to the branch's older snapshot).
Assigned @fabro per user approval ('Ich folge deinem Vorschlag').

title: P0: glm-5.3 structured-output degradation truncates planner output (2554 chars) - every develop pass fails soft_stop
description:
P0 LINE-DOWN (2026-09-17 ~14:30, first passes on the 2026-09-17 deploy): every develop pass fails through a structured-output degradation chain, and the conductor breaker was heading for its 3-strike latch (count 1/3, signature park|Conductor|soft_stop) - schedule PAUSED by the agent (emergency action, user informed) to stop the burn; re-enable after the fix.

CORRELATED EVIDENCE (engine events + rootprint, run 01M2QKXJ5JN9 = develop child of pass 01M2QKT08GPG):
1. Planner stage (10.5 min wall, 136s inference) ends SUCCEEDED but emits run.notice event_body_overflow: 'structured output for node "planner" was truncated at the provider output length cap (2554 chars); persisting the best-effort payload with an explicit truncation marker'.
2. run.notice context_update_dropped: output.planner; context_allow_keys_never_emitted: current_seed_brief, current_seed_id, current_seed_title, journal, review_verdict - the seed id never materializes in the workflow context.
3. stage.failed (deterministic): stdin_source 'current_seed_id' was not found in workflow context (the evidence/closeout script node) -> run.failed soft_stop ('run parked at a soft exit'), diff +6/-1 stranded on the run branch (final commit bc63531).
4. ROOTPRINT, same window: WARN fabro_server::run_title_generation: Run title generation failed run_id=01M2QNGW4BB6 error=model zai/glm-5.3 does not support structu[red output] - the deployed build (with the full upstream delta since 2026-09-15, incl. billing->usage rename) now capability-gates structured output and the catalog says glm-5.3 lacks it; title generation degrades to a warn, but the planner path degrades into the truncation chain above.
5. Next pass 01M2QNGW4BB6 + develop child 01M2QNK2FTMBQ8 hit the same title-generation warn at 12:30-12:31 UTC.

HYPOTHESIS (labeled, needs verification): the upstream merge changed structured-output capability detection or request shaping for the zai provider; before the deploy the same model + graph produced full planner JSONs (passes all morning). Fix directions: (a) catalog/capability override so glm-5.3 advertises structured output (or the engine falls back to a non-native JSON-extraction mode that does not hit the 2554-char cap), (b) raise/derive the output cap from the model limits instead of the degraded path, (c) short-term: switch the line model to a provider with verified structured-output support. The 2554-char cap itself is suspiciously small for a planner brief - verify where the degraded path sets max output.

## ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (2026-09-17 ~15:30, direct agent work)

The capability-gate hypothesis was WRONG for the planner path (it only affects complete_object callers: title generation -> fabro-2e57, PR content -> deterministic fallback). The REAL chain, proven from the persisted run data: glm-5.3's final structured messages ended EXACTLY ONE closing brace short (run 01M2QKXJ5JN9, planner outputs 1016/741/633 tokens = the 633-token one is the persisted 2554-char payload that closes every NESTED object but never the outermost brace; direct zai probes through the server's completions API show NO output cap: 3.5k-4k token outputs complete and balanced with plain/tools/streaming/29k-context shapes). So: a model-behavior change on zai's side (near-complete JSON, finish=stop) met the engine's truncation heuristic (has_unterminated_object -> Truncated) and its counterproductive repair advice ("shorten your output" - shortening does not fix a missing brace), burning the retries and dropping the context updates (current_seed_id never emitted -> evidence stdin_source failure -> soft_stop park).

FIX (landed): deterministic brace-completion salvage in fabro-workflow structured_output.rs - validate_response_text wraps the strict validators; on the Truncated error, complete_missing_braces appends the dangling closing braces when the text ends on a clean value boundary (} ] or "), depth <= 8, not inside a string, and the completed text parses; the completed object then validates normally and is marked salvaged (run.notice structured_output_brace_salvage, Info). Genuine mid-string/mid-value cuts keep the truncation path and length-aware repair; a salvage that completes the parse but fails validation returns the REAL verdict, never the stale Truncated error. Regression pins: the exact production shape (outer brace missing, nested closed), deep-nesting, mid-string-cut and mid-number-cut guards, balanced-text no-op. Verification: structured_output suite 49/49, fork suites green, full fabro-workflow failure set identical to the pre-existing fabro-ca1f cluster, clippy -D warnings clean, pinned-nightly fmt clean. + closure note: FIXED and validated in production 2026-09-17 - brace-completion salvage landed as cef227c3e (image 0.357.0-nightly.0-4c8d67580, deployed ~16:40); first two post-fix cycles ran clean (develop 01M2QWF2RX4Q succeeded, PR #217 merged; revisor 01M2QX81JAJA completed, PR #218 merged; zero truncation notices or repairs). Closed by the line-watch agent with the fix evidence.
closeReason: fixed: brace-completion salvage (cef227c3e), validated by two clean production cycles

title: Revisor file stage: filing-balance duty + same-file consolidation into multi-arm seeds
description:

Expected effect: creation couples to drain (155:80 creates:closes over 7d), the Medium prompt-tweak cluster collapses from dozens of seeds to a handful, directly lowering backlog_stagnation 0.709 and drain_deficit 0.484. ADR-0002 untouched — the gate sits at filing, not journaling. needs-user: the user parked this exact decision in fabro-8776 (closed as consumed with the decision left unfiled); searches regulator/intake/anti-circling/consolidation find no open seed owning it. Per ADR-0019 review axis this reshapes agent capability boundaries; implementation awaits explicit user approval.
Basis: architect pass 2026-09-17, friction 0.347/architecture-due, commit 8577492b149bace190b3c5379dac8a2efa24bb88

User decision 2026-09-17 (approved with refinements, ADR-0022): IMPLEMENT.
- Filing-balance duty as proposed: credit = stale/superseded closes by the SAME pass only (implemented closes do not count).
- Overflow semantic (a): surplus findings ride the pass journal observations (named, concrete) and the NEXT pass may re-file them against its own balance - nothing dropped, ADR-0002 untouched.
- Same-file consolidation into multi-arm seeds (fabro-ae74 schema) is UNCONDITIONAL, independent of the balance.
- Exempt from the balance: needs-user items and security closures (not loop demand).
- Sibling options (ii) root-fix quota and (iii) loop-share P3 stay parked with a review checkpoint (>= 1 week post-landing, creation still >= 2:1 over drain -> revisit); (iv) adopted as line-watch NEEDS-USER QUEUE ceremony (queue >= 5 or line-blocked -> propose triage session).
Assignment follows the approval: fabro implements graph+prompt as ONE unit (ADR-0008).

description:
The architect pass 01M2RD68TCQHTQJX17NWT3RN94 (2026-09-17, analyze-stage painpoint, PR #229) injected an open-seed digest whose evidence cluster cited seed fabro-f751, which does not exist in the tracker; the actual open seed is fabro-f759 ('Evidence capture: emit per-criterion check outputs for verification-only runs'). The ask analyst had the correct id, so no wrong finding shipped - but the digest is the analyst's ONLY backlog source (ask analysts have no shell: read_file/grep/glob plus engine run tools only), so an id drift there poisons duplicate-guarding downstream.

Fix: the survey digest generation (architect prompts/survey.md, arch_seed_digest assembly) validates every cited seed id with `sd show <id>` - or builds the digest directly from `sd list` output instead of reconstructing ids - and drops or flags unknown ids before emitting the context key.

Adjacent class: fabro-88a4 (revisor-side open-backlog digest, open) shares the stale-id failure mode; apply the same validation there when it lands.

Basis: architect run 01M2RD68TCQHTQJX17NWT3RN94 analyze-stage journal painpoint, review `.fabro/architecture/reviews/2026-09-17.md`, merged as PR #229.

ARM 2 - digest measurement enrichment (design decision 2026-09-17, keep fabro_ask): the ask analyst has no shell by design (read/grep/glob + run tools only), so the survey digest is its entire quantitative universe. The 2026-09-17 review fell back to seed-recorded drift data because the survey's churn window was too narrow (git log -n 1000 name-only top-5). Extend the survey digest in prompts/survey.md: (a) churn RATIOS per file (touches / total touches in window) alongside counts, (b) a wider window option (e.g. -n 5000 or --since 30d) with per-directory aggregation, (c) keep the whole base within the bounded preamble. Rationale: today's pass proved the ask path delivers architect-grade reviews; its measurement gaps are digest-side and fixable deterministically. Escalation parked: direct in-stage skill invocation (fs_hide loosening + node-level fabro_run_events/fabro_run_get grants + subagents with shell) only if findings ever require live code execution or the enriched digest still yields stale data.

title: Render binary-classified diffs as text in evidence.nu
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/evidence.nu, when a changed file's diff renders as 'Binary files differ' (evidence: run 01M2RDM3AZ's planner-preflight fixture .fabro/scripts/planner-preflight-anchor-fixtures.nu deliberately embeds a NUL byte), fall back to git diff --text (or an escaped rendering) under the same size bounds (fabro-020b caps remain). In that run the reviewer spent 7 of 9 tool calls shell-reading the 93-line fixture and re-running the 17-check battery itself; the fallback removes the per-review workaround and the UNSEEN-item ambiguity that can escalate to Verification blocked. Cross-ref: fabro-020b (diff size cap), fabro-a494 (off-tree deliverables) — neither covers binary-classified rendering. Basis: run 01M2RDM3AZ5BRZXAPE4GT365P0, workflow version f4ab9ff48b6e162ee81f42689c29e27253fba4fe3632992c2e164afa31eb5ca5, commit 5b7e0356a7536b8fe457d78a6dd4660a70bd3ecb

title: Enforce reviewer read-only posture via per-node tool allow-list on the develop graph
description:
Adopt the closed engine feature fabro-47b5 (per-node tool policy attribute) in .fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro: give the reviewer node tools="read_file,grep,glob,shell" with an empty/minimal fabro_tools (consider the same for the implementer minus spawn_agent). Evidence: run 01M2RDM3AZ's reviewer was 'read-only BY CAPABILITY AND POLICY' in prose yet held the entire mutation-capable registry (event seq 391) and invoked fabro_run_interact (seq 440, benign get) — enforcement makes the contract mechanical and shrinks ADR-0019 capability-delta risk to what the diff adds. Capability-affecting (ADR-0019): this changes agent-reachable tool allowlists, so implementation awaits explicit user approval; fix direction is engine-mediated config only (the existing per-node tools attribute, restricting — never extending — capability). Basis: run 01M2RDM3AZ5BRZXAPE4GT365P0, workflow version f4ab9ff48b6e162ee81f42689c29e27253fba4fe3632992c2e164afa31eb5ca5, commit 5b7e0356a7536b8fe457d78a6dd4660a70bd3ecb

title: Engine: run agents discover zero skills - source_dirs=[] disables vendored .fabro/skills and /name expansion
description:
Evidence 2026-09-17: every agent.skills.discovered event in conductor pass 01M2R8D1NZT59Y1CY9Y7FRXSR7 (survey session, 18:00Z) and architect pass 01M2RD68TCQHTQJX17NWT3RN94 (survey + analyze sessions, 19:24Z) reports {"source_dirs": [], "skills": []}. Historical contrast: develop-run reviews (01M22YZBN, 01M23443Z, mid-September) documented the rust-style-guide skill being OFFERED in reviewer context (224 tokens) - discovery worked before and has regressed. Consequences: /name input-start expansion can never fire (no discovered skill exists to expand); every workflow depending on skill activation (rust-style-guide in develop, improve-codebase-architecture in architect) silently loses it.

CORRECTION (planner, run 01M2VAAYWA0H7XN0V8WSRQ29FE, verified against current tree): the engine-side mechanism the seed asks for ALREADY EXISTS and is correct — skill_options in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/llm/pebble.rs (lines 562-575): a node opting in with skills="discover" gets SkillDiscovery searching the user skills dir plus .fabro/skills and skills under the git root. The regression is that NO workflow graph sets skills="discover" on any node (verified 2026-09-18: zero matches in develop/conductor/architect workflow.fabro), so every agent session runs under the skill-free default introduced by fabro-4dd8 and pebble reports source_dirs=[]. The fix is therefore: (1) opt in the agent nodes that need vendored skills — develop implementer + reviewer, architect analyze/ask, conductor agent nodes — via the node attribute parsed by skills_discovery in lib/foundation/fabro-types/src/graph.rs; (2) add the fork-only presence test the seed asks for: a session with .fabro/skills/* under the git root, node opted in, backend skill_dirs left None (NOT the explicit with_skill_dirs the existing tests use), asserts agent.skills.discovered reports > 0 skills. The fabro-4dd8 skill-free default for non-opt-in nodes must be preserved (existing slash-token survival tests stay green).

Fix direction: keep the opt-in mechanism; wire it from the graphs; close the test gap on the convention-dir (None) branch. Distinct from fabro-ac78 (behavioral load contract - satisfied via fallback) and closed fabro-4dd8 (expansion crash on unknown refs).

Basis: run events 01M2R8D1NZT59Y1CY9Y7FRXSR7 + 01M2RD68TCQHTQJX17NWT3RN94 (agent.skills.discovered), architecture review .fabro/architecture/reviews/2026-09-17.md, PR #229.

title: Split the fabro-server server/tests.rs monolith into per-handler-domain test modules
description:
REJECTED by user decision (2026-09-18, integrate session): server/tests.rs is an upstream-owned file (19,264 lines on upstream/main) and upstream's hottest churn target (112 commits/12w per fabro-ab8e). Splitting it makes every upstream change a modify/delete conflict plus manual re-mapping into 19 modules — a permanent recurring merge tax on the worst file. We merge upstream regularly; structural divergence from upstream-owned files without a user decision is out of bounds. PR #242 (run 01M2TS5BSB9ATK2GJGYA3Z2640) was closed unmerged before its armed auto-merge fired; the moves-only work itself was verified clean (0 lines lost, 373/373 test attributes). The correct direction is fabro-ab8e: extract only fork-added tests into fork-owned files. Original demand: lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/tests.rs is 21,876 lines / 373 test functions with zero internal modules — the repo's top product-code churn (59 touches/30d, re-measured via git log). Split into server/tests/<domain>.rs files mirroring server/handler/ domains (sessions, runs, sandbox, lifecycle, pair, events, graph, system) with shared fixtures behind one cfg(test) support module; moves only, no test-content change. Deletion test: re-homing each domain's tests beside its handler concentrates test knowledge locally while cargo nextest discovery (the interface) is layout-agnostic. Expected effect: locality per handler, smaller review diffs, fewer collisions across parallel develop and merge-upstream lines, cheaper agent navigation. Distinct from open fabro-ab8e (fork-footprint extraction from the same file) — coordinate so fork tests land in fork-owned modules per ADR-0021; cross-reference at filing.

Basis: architect pass 2026-09-17, friction 0.354/architecture-due, commit 8254c7006f9415d4656f30270aa3aa9a5186c6e9 + correction (2026-09-18, line-watch): the planner-preflight repeatedly misclassifies this seed as 'duplicate (landed via #232, sha 4f8a254)' - WRONG: #232/4f8a254 only FILED this seed (architecture pass), the demand is NOT implemented (server/tests.rs remains a 21876-line monolith, verified in tree). Preflight verdicts for this seed are false positives - ignore them and claim normally. The misclassification root is filed with fabro-ead4 (preflight duplicate-classification family).

title: Resolve crate-relative seed anchors in anchor_check.nu before flagging missing_file
description:
.fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/anchor_check.nu joins every cited path against repo root only ($root | path join $a.path), so seeds citing crate-relative anchors (target run: fabro-0863's operations/create.rs:556-585, meaningful inside lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/) flag missing_file falsely and planners cannot distinguish 'file gone' from 'wrong base directory' (run-journal observation). Change: when the root-joined path is absent, retry against workspace member roots from Cargo.toml before emitting missing_file, and include the resolved base in the verdict row. Extends landed fabro-7daf content checking with a resolution stage; same ambiguity family as open fabro-1a35 (PROJECT_FACTS guidance, different mechanism) — cross-reference at filing. Expected effect: false missing_file flags disappear as a class; planner laps stop re-deriving path bases by hand.

Basis: architect pass 2026-09-17, friction 0.354/architecture-due, commit 8254c7006f9415d4656f30270aa3aa9a5186c6e9

title: Architect: same-date review file silently overwrites the earlier pass's review
description:
Evidence 2026-09-17: the architect review path is date-named (`.fabro/architecture/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`). Two passes ran the same date (19:28 fabro_ask-based pass on run 01M2RBX7758R, then the 20:13 direct-skill pass on run 01M2RFG6H4); the second analyze stage OVERWROTE the first pass's review prose. No findings were lost only because the first pass's distillates were already seeded (fabro-c77a, fabro-9ec3, fabro-e907, fabro-d9f7) - the review prose itself (its reasoning, its dropped-duplicate rationale) is gone. Forced test passes make same-date collisions routine; the cooldown marker only gates the cron path, not manual/forced runs.

Fix (from the pass's own painpoint): the file stage (or the analyze write) preserves a superseded same-date review BEFORE the new one lands - copy to a timestamped suffix (`<date>-<HHmm>.md`) when the plain-date file already exists, or end the review template with a prior-pass index section linking back. The marker and seed references stay on the plain-date name.

Basis: architect runs 01M2RD68TCQHTQJX17NWT3RN94 (19:24 pass, review 2026-09-17.md v1) and 01M2RFG6H4FC2G6PZE4NPYW5VJ (20:13 pass, analyze-stage painpoint, overwrote v1).

title: Engine: file-based output_schema routes payload under output.<node> - context_updates never merge, downstream stages run blind
description:
Regression evidence 2026-09-17 (PR #233, fabro-9ec3 arm 3): the develop planner node changed output_schema from the built-in "routing" to a file schema (`@schemas/planner-output.schema.json`). With a file schema, the engine routes the validated payload under `output_key: output.planner` (event: response.planner "payload lives in structured context keys", output_key output.planner) and the object's `context_updates` members (current_seed_id, current_seed_title, current_seed_brief, journal) NEVER materialize as individual run-context keys. The implementer's context_allow_keys declare exactly those keys -> run.notice context_allow_keys_never_emitted; output.planner itself was DROPPED (context_update_dropped) because no downstream node declares it. Net effect: EVERY develop pass after #233 claims a seed and runs the implementer BLIND (run 01M2RJSBP8XS, planner claimed fabro-90ae, implementer had no brief; planner journal record wrote empty data because its journal context_update shared the fate).

Hotfix landed same evening (line-watch, workflow assets): planner reverted to output_schema="routing" + the gate-command ban moved to planner.md hard rules; the schema FILE stays for the proper fix.

Proper fix direction (engine): when a file-schema output validates, merge its `context_updates` into run context EXACTLY like the routing kind does (the schema explicitly declares context_updates open for seed keys/journal) - or emit under output.<node> AND document that nodes must then declare output.<node> in context_allow_keys with nested access. Same output_key mismatch class as open fabro-7028 (gatebounce) and relevant to open fabro-e4c4 (evidence node wants file-schema inline delivery - blocked on these semantics).

Basis: run 01M2RJSBP8XSPCKTEACR7E1PYP events (response.planner output_key, run.notice context_update_dropped/context_allow_keys_never_emitted at 21:05:05Z), PR #233 diff (workflow.fabro output_schema line + schema file), hotfix commit on denkhaus.

title: Extend planner-preflight mechanical superseded-close to non-top duplicate candidates and add a verdict legend

Apply the existing closure-note + superseded-close to ANY candidate with an unambiguous duplicate verdict, and emit a one-line verdict legend field in output.preflight (the planner burned a tool round reading the script's 80-line header, seq 40–42, to learn what duplicate means). Adjacent seeds cover other mechanisms only: fabro-a81d (write-pair chaining), fabro-2ade (parse bug), fabro-2afd (degraded-mode mandate), fabro-22fa (closeout sweep); closed fabro-8c75/fabro-d183 cover adjacent mechanisms, not this. title: Count direct single-parent base-branch fix commits as landed in dup-run-check.nu
description: In .fabro/scripts/dup-run-check.nu, the landed set is built from 2-parent merges plus no-merge commits whose subject ends with a (#n) PR suffix only. A direct fix commit whose subject references the seed id but carries no PR suffix (e.g. 47eedbe '(fabro-c42f)') falls into $other, so the preflight returned clean and the planner of run 01M2TE2SYDYKJT37FJKREHBCT1 burned 15 tool calls / 559 s / $0.263 (100% of run cost) re-deriving a close the script was built to do itself (closed fabro-a32f) — the fix commit was the run's own base SHA. Expected effect: this run class (~9.6 min, ~$0.26 each) collapses to a ~30 s zero-LLM preflight exit. Adjacent seeds cover other mechanisms: fabro-ead4 (planner-preflight.nu superseded-close extension), closed fabro-0d48/fabro-8c75 (false-positive narrowing), fabro-a01f (claim race). title: Forbid compile-level probes as Already-landed closure evidence in the planner prompt

title: Lifecycle: 429/quota deaths end as blocked (Kanban-separable from real failures, resumable)
description:
User decision 2026-09-18 (incident session, mirtuell.net line watch): runs that die on a provider 429/quota window should end in a BLOCKED lifecycle status, not failed/soft_stop — the web UI Kanban board then shows them under Blocked, separating \"waiting on quota, resumable\" from genuinely failed work.

Evidence (incident 2026-09-18): develop run 01M2SRK0PCDXG5F8B8TX2TRGFB died at implementer 08:27:45 UTC with \"LLM error: provider zai Usage limit reached for 5 hour. Your limit will reset at 2026-09-18 16:56:19\" (failure category transient_infra, signature api_transient|zai|rate_limit) — terminal lifecycle failed/soft_stop, INDISTINGUISHABLE in the runs list from real failures (the 07:01 engine-skew soft_stop and the 11:31 workflow_error looked identical). Conductor parents 01M2SRF7JB86F0E0F20ZTJKDYT and 01M2SN19BFSJMSC85SBJRY5060 failed the same way as propagation. Diagnosing \"which failures are just quota parks\" required reading stage events per run during the incident.

Existing machinery to build on: is_quota_park (lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/fork_line_recovery.rs, fabro-986b breaker exemption) already classifies quota-class parks; the signature api_transient|<provider>|rate_limit is the deterministic marker; the provider reset timestamp currently lives only inside the error message text (fabro-a3d8 evidence, closed — covered retry/park mechanics, not status surfacing).

Acceptance criteria:
- A run whose terminal failure classifies as quota/rate-limit (429 family, api_transient|*|rate_limit) ends with lifecycle status blocked (not failed/soft_stop); the provider reset time, when parseable, is stored as a structured field on the run.
- Runs list and web UI Kanban board show blocked runs under a Blocked column, separate from Failed.
- Genuine failures (deterministic, workflow_error, non-quota soft_stop) remain failed — classification has a unit test pinning the exact 01M2SRK0PCDXG5F8B8TX2TRGFB failure shape.
- Blocked runs stay resumable/retryable through the existing routes (fabro-7627 semantics unchanged: resume re-runs the failed node).
- fabro-986b breaker behavior unchanged (quota parks never count toward the schedule breaker).
- OpenAPI-first: run lifecycle schema updated in docs/public/api-reference/fabro-api.yaml first, then progenitor types + TS client regen, UI board consumes the new state.

Basis: incident runs 01M2SRK0PCDXG5F8B8TX2TRGFB / 01M2SRF7JB86F0E0F20ZTJKDYT / 01M2SN19BFSJMSC85SBJRY5060 (2026-09-18); user decision in integrate session 2026-09-18 ~14:5x UTC; lineage fabro-a3d8 -> fabro-986b.

title: Planner prose response (no JSON) parks run late at evidence node - 30min implementer cycle wasted

title: Fail-closed startup verify breaks on projection-semantics changes: terminal rows are era-sensitive (3rd incident)
description: CLASS (3rd era incident after workflow_version_id 2026-09-05 and usage-rename 2026-09-15): SQLite run-history activation replays every run's events with the CURRENT projection logic and fail-closes on divergence from stored rows. Any change to projection semantics (PR #240 quota reclassification Failed->Blocked is the current case) makes terminal rows written by older binaries permanently poison startup — CI/local DBs are fresh so gates stay green, production carries the history. Incident 2026-09-18: deploy of merge 15c046bd1 (first binary carrying #240) crash-looped; 4 archived conductor/develop runs (quota-class run.failed events) replayed as Blocked{quota_rate_limit} vs stored failed. Mitigation executed: data patch of 4 rows (status column + summary_json lifecycle.status to the new projection), validated against a prod DB snapshot in an isolated container before patching prod; backup fabro.sqlite3.pre-quota-era-patch.bak on the volume. DURABLE FIX OPTIONS (decide one): (a) startup re-projection migration that converges stale terminal rows to the current projector BEFORE the fail-closed verify (event log stays authoritative; row is a cache), (b) era-tolerance in verify like the two ADR-0015 tolerances (weaker: rows keep displaying stale status), (c) extend the develop gate with a fixture that replays pre-era rows through a newer binary (prevention only, no repair). Constraint from ADR-0021/e566 line: quota parks must survive as Blocked for resume routing. Basis: merge session 2026-09-18 (upstream 170291b9f->22f46031f), prod incident 20:33-20:53 UTC, gate runs that passed #240 did so on fresh DBs.

title: Lint bare slash-tokens in prompts of skills=discover nodes before they kill sessions
description:
Run 01M2VAAYWA0H7XN0V8WSRQ29FE merged PR #246 (fabro-f84f), opting six develop/architect/conductor stages into skills="discover" — re-enabling pebble expansion of bare `/name` tokens in harness-assembled input, the class that killed the conductor line in 0.3s (fabro-4dd8, run 01M2GJXV71TD). Change: add a deterministic lint beside lint-nu in .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/qualitygate.nu (and validate-workflows) scanning prompts and known context-rendered text of opted-in nodes for bare slash-tokens. Existing seeds fix pebble/engine expansion semantics (fabro-26c3, fabro-68d3) and expand_skill parsing (fabro-af22); none provides a fabro-side interim guard. Expected effect: the session-death class is caught by the gate, not by a dead conductor line. Basis: run 01M2VAAYWA0H7XN0V8WSRQ29FE, workflow version 8dafcf4ebc5c1b1a4781f85b7f1e6125f166bfcdef6bbc34414c18e13aa5f3, commit 7cca0142f65d298d4cbaec86c1422def2b4d0ef1

## USER DECISION (2026-09-20, `/integrate` night-window analysis): extend the deterministic prompt-check with BOTH skill-reference arms

The deterministic prompt-lint (.fabro/scripts/prompt-lint.nu — the script that already bans seed-id/run-id/PR/sha provenance literals in workflow assets) must ALSO check for skill references:

(a) INVALID skill references: bare slash-tokens that pebble's find_skill_references would bind as skill references but that are not registered skills. EXACT binding rule from the pinned pebble rev 67c9f48 (skills.rs): token = '/' at input start or after whitespace, first char ascii lowercase, following chars [a-z0-9_-], terminated ONLY by whitespace or end-of-input (a token ending at '/', ',', '`', '*', ')' etc. does NOT bind — that is why /api/v1/* and backticked `/install` are safe while bare `/install ` kills). MORE THAN ONE bound token also fails the session (SkillExpansionError::MultipleReferences).

(b) UNRESOLVABLE skill references: tokens or file references that SHOULD resolve to a skill but cannot because the skill is absent from the discoverable registry (.fabro/skills/) or access fails (fs_hide envelope, missing SKILL.md). Examples: a prompt naming `.fabro/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` where <name> does not exist; use_skill-style mentions of undiscoverable skills.

## EVIDENCE (2026-09-19/20 night window — 5 develop runs killed, all reviewer stage, all soft_stop)

Runs 01M2XSA56X (21:31), 01M2Y052A1 (23:31), 01M2Y1W8YH (00:01), 01M2Y71ZR3 (01:32), 01M2YDXWZQ (03:32): implementer/tester/evidence green, then reviewer session died in <1s, 0 tokens, category=structural, "Precondition failed: Agent session failed: expanding a skill reference". Root cause proven by exact-rule scan: each reviewer prompt carried exactly ONE bound token — `/install` — from the RAW seed description of fabro-b03f ("...only `/install` + static SPA serve...") which the reviewer prompt embeds un-backticked; the planner distills a backticked brief, so implementer survives, but the reviewer's raw-description render re-exposes the token (run 01M2Y71ZR3 additionally lost implementer@1 the same way before planner@2 re-briefed). Static prompt files are already pinned by fork_seam_tests::workflow_prompts_carry_no_expandable_slash_tokens; the DATA arm is unpinned: tracker seed bodies, evidence/tester output, journal text flow into skills=discover sessions unscanned.

## ACCEPTANCE

- prompt-lint.nu (or a sibling deterministic check wired into the same gate paths) implements BOTH arms over static workflow assets.
- A deterministic DATA-side check covers text that flows into skills=discover sessions from outside the prompts: minimally the claimed seed's description (claim-check.nu or planner-preflight.nu) rejects/backtick-escapes bound slash-tokens per the exact rule; ideally evidence.nu output too.
- Red-before proof against the fabro-b03f description body (contains a bound `/install ` token) and green-after.
- Note in the check's output when a token ends at a non-whitespace boundary (safe) so contributors learn the rule, not just the failure.

## USER DECISION #2 (2026-09-20, session): dedicated Nu script, TWO document classes — workflow assets AND seeds

The skill-reference lint is NOT just for prompts: seed descriptions flow into skills=discover sessions too (the reviewer embeds the raw claimed seed body — the proven night-window kill chain). Therefore:

- The check ships as its OWN standalone Nu script (e.g. `.fabro/scripts/skill-ref-lint.nu`), not only an arm inside prompt-lint.nu. It lints DOCUMENTS for wrong skill references in both arms below; prompt-lint keeps its provenance-literal checks and calls or runs beside it.
- Document class A — static workflow assets: the same corpus prompt-lint covers today (`.fabro/workflows/{conductor,develop,revisor}/**` + `.fabro/scripts/*.nu`).
- Document class B — SEEDS: every OPEN seed body in `.seeds/issues.jsonl` (claimable documents). Errors on open seeds; closed-seed hits may stay warnings (inert for claiming, hygiene only). Reading via the sd CLI (`sd list --format json`) where practical; the lint must also catch tokens a planner re-introduces via `sd update --description` (planner bodies are re-emitted wholesale).
- Arms (unchanged from decision #1): (a) INVALID skill references — bound slash-tokens per the EXACT pebble rule that are not registered skills; (b) UNRESOLVABLE references — names/paths that should resolve to a skill but cannot (missing `.fabro/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, unreadable under fs_hide, use_skill mentions of undiscoverable skills).
- Wiring: loop-asset tier of `just qualitygate` (both gate paths, like prompt-lint today) + `just validate-workflows`; DATA-side hooks stay: planner-preflight/claim-check reject or backtick-escape bound tokens in the CLAIMED seed before the reviewer sees it; closeout/revisor filing checks for NEW seed bodies.
- Fix suggestion in output: wrap the token in backticks (the proven sanitizer — a backtick before the slash breaks the whitespace-boundary precondition).
- Red-before corpus: the 17 poisoned bodies sanitized in commit 32240f88d (night window 2026-09-20) + the canonical fabro-b03f incident body; green-after: the sanitized tracker (re-scan via the exact rule = zero).
- The Rust-side static pin (`fork_seam_tests::workflow_prompts_carry_no_expandable_slash_tokens`) STAYS — defense in depth; the Nu script adds seeds + gate-time enforcement the test cannot see.

Interim protection already in place: tracker sanitized (32240f88d); the integrate session's exact-rule Python scanner guards every new agent filing until this script lands.

title: Goal-gate on planner makes deterministic pre-exits crash develop (workflow_error loop)
description:
## Demand

The develop graph has two deterministic exits that bypass the planner and
therefore violate its `goal_gate=true` (present since fabro-5453, merged-world
migration): every terminal reach checks ALL gated nodes, so a run that exits
without a successful planner outcome dies with
`goal gate unsatisfied for node planner and no retry target`.

Affected paths (both latent until 2026-09-19):
- `preflight -> exit [label="Already landed"]` (fabro-a32f, #209) — first
  exercised by runs 01M2WG2Z42N8P2QKX0K7VXT1MC and 01M2WHTHVGK360638W9H9PN2BT
  (identical 18s workflow_error loops, three passes 11:30/12:00 CEST, breaker
  park|Conductor|soft_stop 2/3).
- `tracker_guard -> exit [label="Tracker empty"]` (#276) — never fired yet,
  same class: planner never runs, gate fails.

Secondary effect: because the already-landed run FAILS, the preflight's
superseded-closures (made in the sandbox tracker and pushed to the run branch)
strand on the orphaned branch — the closures never reach base and the next
pass repeats identically (observed: byte-identical preflight blobs 09:31/10:01
UTC closing fabro-29f7 + fabro-6a78 every pass).

## Fix direction (design fork ratified in chat 2026-09-19, integrate pass)

Recommended: REMOVE `goal_gate=true` from the planner node. Rationale:
- The gate predates both deterministic bypass nodes; its invariant ("planner
  must have run for a success") contradicts the graph's own documented edge
  comments ("plain edge, natural completion").
- `retry_target` (the established idiom in smoke/implement-plan/card-game)
  is WRONG here: it would route the gate failure back into preflight/planner
  and burn an LLM lap on every drained/already-landed pass, defeating the
  zero-token goals of fabro-a32f and #276.
- Engine-side path-aware gates are the durable generalization, but develop is
  currently the only workflow with guard pre-exits; defer until a second
  workflow needs it (file separately if the pattern repeats).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run taking `tracker_guard -> exit` (empty tracker) completes with a
   soft/success outcome and ZERO planner tokens (pins #276's goal).

title: dup-run-check counts reopen/verify commits that name a seed as landed implementation
description:
## Demand

The deterministic already-landed classification (.fabro/scripts/dup-run-check.nu,
reused verbatim by planner-preflight.nu) treats every landed-PR commit (true
merge or squash subject ending `(#n)`) whose subject names a seed id as a
landed IMPLEMENTATION of that seed. The filed-only exception covers only
revisor filing conventions (Revisor pass / revise run / file seeds phrasings).

Missing exception class: landed commits that merely REOPEN, VERIFY, or do
tracker bookkeeping for the named seed. Observed 2026-09-19: fabro-29f7 was
matched against e769f791 ("fabro-29f7: reopen gate seed, verify upstream
offers remain unmerged ... (#250)") and auto-closed as duplicate — the cited
commit reopened the seed, it did not implement it (the implementation was
older). fabro-6a78 matched f3c12e03 ("Verify fabro-6a78 fix in-tree; move
seed to in_progress ... (#254)") — same shape: a verify/status commit, not the
implementation.

Consequence: a deliberately reopened seed whose reopen/verify commit merged is
ALWAYS re-closed mechanically by the next preflight pass. The planner never
sees it.

The 2026-09-19 closures happened to match the user's standing closure rule
(fix landed + working -> close), so no damage — but the evidence class is
wrong and will eventually close live work.

## Acceptance criteria

1. classify-filed (or the match pipeline) gains an exception for subjects
   whose seed-id action is reopen/verify/status/close bookkeeping (at minimum:
   `reopen`, `verify`, `move seed`, `close seed` phrasings naming the seed),
   mirroring the conservative filed-only style: when in doubt, route the
   planner (false negative), never auto-close (false positive).
2. Fixture battery case: a landed squash commit "fabro-X: reopen ... (#n)"
   classifies NOT as implementation match.
3. Regression note in the header doc: the incident runs (01M2WG2Z42N8P2QKX0K7VXT1MC,
   01M2WHTHVGK360638W9H9PN2BT, 2026-09-19) as the basis.

## Basis

Integrate pass 2026-09-19; preflight verdict blobs of runs
01M2WG2Z42N8P2QKX0K7VXT1MC / 01M2WHTHVGK360638W9H9PN2BT (close_log cites
e769f791 / f3c12e03); dup-run-check.nu classify-filed (fabro-a32f, fabro-0d48
lineage).

title: Planner-preflight is report-only: no closures, no early exit — planner owns the already-landed decision
description:
## Agreed design (user-ratified 2026-09-19, integrate session)

The planner-preflight becomes a REPORTER. Closure authority returns to the
review-protected path. Rationale (user): a commit subject naming a seed id is
not evidence that the seed's acceptance criteria are met; decisions about
implementation status belong to the planner + reviewer cycle, not to a script.

Measured effectiveness backing the change: in the 34 develop runs since #209
(2026-09-17) the auto-close route fired exactly once — 2026-09-19 11:30/12:00
CEST — with a wrong evidence class (reopen/verify commits matched as landed
implementations, fabro-395b) AND it crashed the line via the planner goal
gate (fabro-92e2). The report table alone achieves the original cost goal
(fabro-a32f: stop the planner re-grepping base history, run 01M2Q2Q2NY,
$0.143).

## Changes

1. planner-preflight.nu: remove the closure side effects entirely (sd update
   note + sd close), remove the `--report-only` flag (single mode now), route
   ALWAYS "Preflight done". Keep: candidate fetch, dup-run-check verdicts,
   in-flight claims, anchor checks, legend, degraded fail-open paths. Drop
   close_log/closed from the report.
2. workflow.fabro: delete the `preflight -> exit [label="Already landed"]`
   edge (report-only preflight never exits early); remove `goal_gate=true`
   from the planner node (fabro-92e2 — the remaining deterministic exit,
   tracker_guard -> exit, must not fail on it; edge topology already forces
   planner-first on every non-deterministic path).
3. prompts/planner.md: the ALREADY LANDED arm (fabro-d183 two-branch rule)
   becomes THE decision point — the table is advisory input, NOTHING was
   closed pre-planner; the planner closes per the two-branch rule itself
   (closure note + superseded-close, self-explaining tracker) and routes
   "Already landed".
4. planner-preflight-anchor-fixtures.nu: drop the --report-only flag from the
   end-to-end case.
5. New graph-contract smoke wired into scripts/qualitygate.nu: develop graph
   must have NO goal_gate on planner, NO preflight->exit edge, and MUST keep
   the tracker_guard->exit edge — the regression pin class of the incident.

## Consequences

- Cost: rarely one planner lap (~$0.02-0.08) for a landed-but-open top seed.
  In exchange: no mechanical closes against deliberate reopen/pending
  decisions, every closure review-protected, the incident's crash class
  structurally gone.
- The overflow finding in .fabro/revisions/01M2VYXTWV18XV8M5MV02TQW49.md
  ("gate report-only route on resolvable sha") is OBSOLETE (only one route
  remains); its "mechanical upstream_gated skip" arm survives as a possible
  future ADVISORY table column, not a route.
- fabro-395b (subject-match false positives) is demoted to a report-accuracy
  demand: a wrong `duplicate` verdict can now only mislead the planner, not
  close anything.

## Basis

User decision 2026-09-19 ("einverstanden, du implementierst"); incident runs
01M2WG2Z42N8P2QKX0K7VXT1MC / 01M2WHTHVGK360638W9H9PN2BT; integrate pass
2026-09-19; related seeds fabro-92e2 (gate), fabro-395b (evidence class),
fabro-ead4/fabro-a32f/fabro-d183 lineage (superseded by this design).

## CLOSE (2026-09-19, agent-implemented per user assignment)

Implemented fully, verification green:
- planner-preflight.nu: closure side effects removed (no sd update/sd
  close anywhere), --report-only flag removed (single mode), route always
  "Preflight done", close_log/closed fields dropped, legend rewritten as
  advisory (duplicate => planner judges acceptance criteria per the
  two-branch rule). Parse-checked; end-to-end dry-runs: nonexistent
  candidate (clean/degraded paths) and fabro-29f7 (verdict duplicate with
  sha e769f791 reported as advisory, route "Preflight done", tracker
  untouched — status stayed closed, no writes).
- workflow.fabro: preflight -> exit [Already landed] edge deleted;
  node comments rewritten (report-only rationale, incident basis).
- prompts/planner.md: the arm is THE decision point — table advisory,
  nothing closed pre-planner, planner owns closures (fabro-395b caveat
  spelled out: a duplicate row does not prove criteria hold).
- Fixture batteries: dup-run-check-fixtures (l)-(n) cases rewritten for
  report-only (duplicates of every shape route "Preflight done", tracker
  rows untouched, no close_log/closed fields); anchor-fixtures --report-only
  flag dropped; both green.
- Gate: graph-contract-smoke.nu added + anchor battery added to
  scripts/qualitygate.nu batteries.
- validate-workflows green; lint-nu green; evidence-smoke dev-checkout
  failure pre-existing (fabro-483d).
Related: goal-gate side in fabro-92e2 (closed same pass); evidence-class
upgrade remains open as fabro-395b; report-only makes the 01M2VYXT
overflow route-gate arms obsolete.

title: Engine: path-aware goal gates — a gate applies only to nodes the taken path routed through
description:
## Demand (deferred by user decision 2026-09-19)

Engine-side generalization of the goal-gate mechanism: at a terminal, a
goal_gate=true node should count as satisfied-or-moot based on whether the
TAKEN PATH routed through it, instead of the current global check (every
gated node must have a successful outcome, fabro-92e2's crash class).

Current semantics (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/graph/routing.rs
check_goal_gates + lib/foundation/fabro-core/src/executor.rs terminal path):
ALL gated nodes are checked at EVERY terminal reach. Any workflow that adds a
deterministic guard exit before a gated node dies with "goal gate unsatisfied
... no retry target" — develop hit this twice (fabro-92e2, fixed graph-side
by removing the planner gate; the preflight early-exit was removed by
fabro-83df).

Deferred because develop is currently the only workflow with guard pre-exits;
the graph-side fix is sufficient there. FILE THE ENGINE WORK when a SECOND
workflow grows a deterministic bypass in front of a gated node, or when the
gate idiom (verify -> retry_target=fixup in smoke/implement-plan/card-game)
starts colliding with soft/guard exits.

## Acceptance criteria (when picked up)

1. Executor/graph: goal-gate check is path-aware (gated nodes not on the taken
   path are moot); conformance tests cover guard-exit + gated-node in one graph.
2. All existing workflows' gate semantics unchanged (smoke, implement-plan,
   card-game/solitaire suites green).
3. The fabro-92e2 graph-contract-smoke stays green (develop's fix is
   independent of this change).

## Basis

User decision 2026-09-19 (Frage 2: "folge deiner Empfehlung, für Lösung B
müsste ein Seed erstellt werden"); incident runs 01M2WG2Z42N8P2QKX0K7VXT1MC /
01M2WHTHVGK360638W9H9PN2BT; related closed seeds fabro-92e2, fabro-83df.

title: Sandbox GC: mirtuell docker host at 90% disk from un-pruned run containers and stale toolchain image tags
description:
## Demand

The fabro docker host on mirtuell is at ~90% disk usage from run-sandbox
artifacts the engine never garbage-collects:

1. Run containers: terminal develop runs intentionally KEEP their sandbox
   containers (the revisable-runs contract, ADR-0011 — a revisor pass inspects
   a terminal run's LIVE sandbox). Nothing ever removes them afterwards, not
   even when the run is no longer revisable (stale-evidence run: workflow
   version superseded, or already revised). Observed 2026-09-19: ~hundreds of
   accumulated fabro-run-* containers after weeks of 30-min conductor passes.
2. Stale toolchain image tags: every toolchain content-hash change pulls a new
   ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain:<sha> (~4-7.7 GB each; 8 tags on the dev
   host alone 2026-09-19); old tags are never removed on the server host.

`fabro system prune` does NOT help: it prunes run RECORDS, not docker
artifacts. No engine-side docker GC exists (searched 2026-09-19).

## Design direction

Engine-side sandbox GC on the server (it already owns the docker socket via
the mounted /var/run/docker.sock):
- When a develop run becomes non-revisable (its revision was filed, OR its
  workflow_version_id no longer matches the registered develop version —
  the stale-evidence definition in docs/lab/CONTEXT.md, OR age > N days),
  remove its stopped container.
- Keep at least the K most recent revisable sandboxes regardless of age.
- Toolchain images: after a run-image refresh lands a new tag, remove local
  tags not referenced by any live environment and older than the current
  content-hash tag (keep current + latest).
- Telemetry/notice when GC frees space (rootprint-observable).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A terminal develop run's container is removed once it can no longer be
   revised (revision filed / stale-evidence / age threshold) — earliest of
   those, with a K-most-recent carve-out.
2. Stale toolchain image tags are removed after a refresh; the current tag
   and `latest` survive; the 30-min toolchain build cache is never
   invalidated (label sh.fabro.toolchain.sha256 semantics from run-images.nu).
3. Unit tests pin the revisable->GC transition using the sandbox
   test_support doubles; an operator-facing summary log line names counts
   and freed bytes.
4. Immediate relief documented: one-off host-side cleanup commands for the
   operator (remove non-revisable fabro-run-* containers + unreferenced old
   toolchain tags) — the 90% condition predates the engine fix.

## Basis

User report 2026-09-19 ("90% des Plattenplatzes durch ungeprunte run images
verbraucht"); ADR-0011 revisor architecture (revisable runs keep live
sandboxes); CONTEXT.md stale-evidence-run definition; run-images.nu content
hash labels; sd search 'prune disk space docker images server' empty
2026-09-19.

## IMMEDIATE RELIEF EXECUTED (2026-09-19, agent via root@netcup-5:2223)

- Removed 202 stopped fabro-run-* containers (kept the 5 newest stopped for
  revisor revisability + all running).
- Removed 6 old ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro server tags (kept the running
  container's image + newest 0.360.0-nightly.0-0f2ae86e8).
- Disk: 434G/503G (90%) -> 26G/503G (6%) — 408 GB freed; fabro server
  healthy throughout.
- REMAINING (deliberate): one RUNNING stale sandbox fabro-run-01M2DXVAJBY1XBWBSNKNG0M6DM
  (13.4 GB writable layer, created 2026-09-13, stale-evidence — engine keeps
  it alive, nothing ever GCs it: exactly this seed's demand); 250 orphaned
  run-workspace volumes (~985 MB total, 9 active); ~2.6 GB dangling image
  layers. All small except the running sandbox.
- Follow-up (same day, user-approved): removed the stale running sandbox
  fabro-run-01M2DXVAJBY1XBWBSNKNG0M6DM (failed workflow_error 2026-09-13,
  version d2f21aa0/9 nodes vs current c850f5e8/12 — stale-evidence, skipped
  by revisor selection by definition). Disk now 14G/503G (3%). Server healthy.

title: Bake libssl-dev into the run toolchain image (ADR-0019: capability-affecting)
description: Run 01M2WZHS implementer@1 hit the openssl-sys 0.9.116 build dead-end first-try: `.fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain` (~line 45) installs build-essential/pkg-config/perl/cmake but not `libssl-dev` (the non-toolchain `.fabro/Dockerfile` has it), so native-tls via reqwest default features of the pinned daytona-sdk cannot build; every Rust-touching run burns ~45s diagnosing it and the `apt-get install -y libssl-dev` fix dies with the sandbox. Change: add `libssl-dev` to the toolchain apt line, or alternatively unify reqwest to rustls-only so native-tls leaves the dependency graph. Expected effect: removes a guaranteed dead-end diagnosis from every Rust-touching run. ADR-0019: this adds a package to an agent-reachable container image surface (.fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain), so it is capability-affecting and stays for user assignment; implementation awaits explicit user approval. Fix direction is limited to baking a build dependency into the existing image — no new tools, credentials, or permissions. Basis: run 01M2WZHS4MZ8FGSGY7R33FXDX9, workflow version 651b1a6e2a981a032674237f71e9a360311e8ba2901832de7fa9b0b3046836b7, commit 6cd6cbcaaade75f301ae51eaf166e47f31ab592e

title: Implementer/reviewer prompt rules from user steering: fork-owned files + presence pins, testing belongs to the tester step
description:

title: Conductor gate-stuck arm drops child_run_id: revise leg fails pass continuity, revisor pass lost
description:
## Demand

The conductor's develop leg has a "Gate stuck — revise anyway" arm: when the
develop child SUCCEEDED but its PR stayed blocked past the bounded merge
waits, the pass routes to the revise leg anyway. That arm does NOT record
`child_run_id` into the pass context — only the normal merged-child path
does. The revise leg then hits its pass-continuity break procedure ("route
'Revisor child failed', no revisor run created") and the conductor soft-parks.

Observed 2026-09-19 (conductor run 01M2X6AT3V4CPSJC08SMCVB172, 18:00 CEST
pass): develop child 01M2X6EC95G76YFNF1YTCJZG7P succeeded (seed fabro-32db,
PR #284), merge waits expired while an unrelated red run PR (#280, agent
branch repair in flight) held the gate busy, arm routed "Gate stuck —
revise anyway", revise@1 failed with loop_failure_signature "pass continuity
broken: 'child_run_id' absent from context — the develop/merge leg did not
record the pass child ... no revisor run was created", conductor parked
soft_stop.

Secondary effect: run 01M2X6EC95 was NEVER revisor-reviewed (reviews cover
01M2X8458M via PR #286 and 01M2X9VECMV via PR #288) — a revisor backlog gap
that no later pass picked up.

## Fix direction

The develop leg's context_updates contract must record `child_run_id` on
EVERY arm that leaves a child behind (merged, gate-stuck, failed) — the
gate-stuck arm knows the child id (it just waited on its PR). The revise
leg then proceeds normally. Alternatively the revise leg's continuity
procedure could recover the child from the pass journal as a fallback, but
the primary contract belongs on the producer.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A conductor pass whose develop child succeeds but whose PR misses the
   bounded merge waits still records `child_run_id`; the revise leg creates
   the revisor child instead of failing pass continuity.
2. Unit/integration test pinning the gate-stuck arm's context_updates
   (child_run_id present), mirroring the normal-path pin.
3. The engine's existing loop_failure_signature for the class stays as the
   safety net (it correctly classified this instance).

## Basis

Conductor run 01M2X6AT3V4CPSJC08SMCVB172 events seq 100-138 (2026-09-19,
agent diagnosis on user request "revise@1 failed?"); child
01M2X6EC95G76YFNF1YTCJZG7P; PR #284/#280 timing overlap; sd search
'child_run_id pass continuity revise' empty 2026-09-19.

title: Deterministic overflow re-filing with idempotent consumption: no finding lost, none filed twice
description:
## Demand (user decision 2026-09-19)

ADR-0022's filing balance parks surplus findings as `overflow:` journal
notes in .fabro/revisions/<run>.md — but their CONSUMPTION is
non-deterministic: a later pass must (a) earn same-pass credit AND
(b) happen to look. Observed 2026-09-19: the memoize-skip-notes finding
(revision file of run 01M2X8458MDWMRVBRVEMDX9W4J, PR #286 "file no seeds")
was still unfiled hours later; a day earlier a multi-arm finding rode the
same path (01M2VZXV3 journal). fabro-27bb already schedules the starvation
measurement for 2026-09-25 — this seed fixes the mechanism instead of
watching it fail.

Two user-mandated properties (verbatim intent: "vor allem muss die
overflow wiedervorlage deterministisch sein und es sollte keine befunde
geben, die doppelt gemacht werden"):

1. DETERMINISTIC re-filing: open overflows are surfaced to the filing
   stage EVERY pass — the revisor's revision_findings input must include
   open (unconsumed) overflow entries from prior revision files, not only
   the current pass's own findings. Zero-credit handling stays per
   ADR-0022 (overflow again), but no finding depends on luck to be SEEN.
2. NO DUPLICATE FINDINGS, in both directions:
   - consumption side: once an overflow is filed as a seed, it is marked
     consumed (append `filed-as: fabro-XXXX` to the overflow entry, or a
     dedicated overflow ledger with open/filed/superseded states) so no
     later pass re-files it;
   - production side: before journaling a NEW overflow, dedupe against
     EXISTING open overflows (same theme), not only against the tracker —
     two passes reviewing adjacent runs currently re-journal the same
     finding as two overflows.

## Design direction

- One deterministic consumer: the revisor file stage (it already owns
  sd-search dedupe; extend its input). The conductor survey REPORTS the
  open-overflow count for visibility (and fabro-27bb's measurement) but
  never files.
- Overflow identity: the overflow entry heading (slug/title) is the stable
  id; consumption marks it in place (append-only, consistent with the
  revision files being append-friendly) or via one ledger file scanned by
  glob — implementer's choice, but the state must be machine-checkable
  from the tree.
- Balance scope: re-filed overflows count against the SAME pass credit
  rule (ADR-0022 unchanged) — the fix is deterministic VISIBILITY +
  idempotent consumption, not a balance change. If starvation persists at
  the fabro-27bb measurement, the balance scope is a separate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A revision file with an open overflow: the NEXT revisor pass sees it in
   its filing input (evidenced by its report naming the overflow), files
   it when credit allows, and marks it consumed.
2. A consumed overflow is never re-filed: a later pass's input excludes it
   (or the report shows it recognized as filed).
3. Two adjacent-run passes that both find the same theme journal at most
   ONE open overflow (second links to the first, e.g. `overflow-dup:`).
4. Unit/smoke coverage: a fixture revision file with open + consumed
   overflows drives the input selection deterministically.

## Basis

User decision 2026-09-19 (integrate session, "nein, lege das als seed an.
vor allem muss die overflow wiedervorlage deterministisch sein und es
sollte keine befunde geben, die doppelt gemacht werden"); revision files
01M2X8458MDWMRVBRVEMDX9W4J.md (open, unfiled memoize finding) and
01M2VZXV34XNAYSYBAFTB30WY8.jsonl (prior multi-arm overflow);
.fabro/workflows/revisor/prompts/file.md filing-balance section (ADR-0022);
PR #286 "file no seeds (overflow memoize-…)"; related open seed fabro-27bb
(measurement, 2026-09-25) — complementary, cross-reference it.

title: Docker sandbox pulls: registry auth for private images (first-use tags 401 on prod)
description:
Product gap: the docker sandbox provider creates containers through the host docker API, and API-initiated image pulls require client-sent registry auth (X-Registry-Auth). The provider settings have no registry-credential keys, so every PRIVATE image tag that is not already present on the host fails on first use with 401.

Evidence: revisor child 01M2XP626TS98ZTKMR2ZKF4719 (2026-09-19) failed in 336 ms — sandbox provisioning pulled ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain:72ea5b4d46e2 (fresh tag, just pinned into the server-managed toolchain environment) and got 'docker error [401]: pulling image'. The host root CAN pull the same tag (tofu ghcr_auth ran docker login there); the fabro server's API pull cannot.

Blast radius: fresh hosts and every newly pushed toolchain tag (run-images.nu pushes per-commit tags). The fabro server image is unaffected because fabro-tofu pre-pulls images_to_pull.

Proposal: add registry credentials to the docker sandbox provider settings (e.g. [server.sandbox.providers.docker.registries.'ghcr.io'] with user/token), send them as X-Registry-Auth on create/pull, credentials from the vault like other server secrets (server-secrets-strategy). Consider offering upstream — private-registry sandboxes are a general operator need.

Interim workaround (landed, do not remove until this closes): merge-upstream skill deploy phase pulls the pinned toolchain tag on the host via SSH right after the environment PUT; mulch engine failure record 2026-09-19 carries the full chain.

## RECURRENCE 2 (2026-09-20 11:00 UTC — line DOWN after release): new toolchain tag 401 on pull, every cron fire dies at sandbox init

Run 01M2Z7J4QR50303DESBATV8PAQ: sandbox.create.failed `docker error [401]: pulling image` (Head ghcr.io/v2/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain/manifests/1e239bc8bb9f -> unauthorized, retryable=false) 2.4 s after start. The 11:00 fire was the FIRST after the 0.361 deploy + toolchain re-pin (1e239bc8bb9f, pushed ~30 min earlier); the previous tag 72ea5b4d46e2 had worked all morning (likely host-cached — the 401 hits only FIRST-USE tags, matching this seed's original thesis). Operator remediation for THIS instance: ghcr.io docker login on the mirtuell host (or package visibility / host credential store). This recurrence BLOCKED the autonomous line for two consecutive fire slots after a routine release — the exact scenario the seed demands a durable fix for: the host's registry credential lifecycle must not be a per-release manual step. Suggest priority bump and folding into the fabro-4f44 pin automation acceptance (a pin that the host cannot pull should be caught by a pre-pin pull check or a post-deploy environment smoke).

## USER DECISION (2026-09-20, recurrence 2 session): manual docker login is a WORKAROUND, not a solution — fix BOTH arms

The host-side `docker login` is unacceptable as the standing mechanism (per-release manual step, invisible to the engine, line stays down when forgotten). Chosen direction, ideally BOTH:
(a) OPS ARM (immediate): make ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain PUBLIC pullable — the line then never depends on host credentials for this image. Note: GHCR visibility is UI-only (PATCH /user/packages/container/fabro-toolchain -> 404, verified 2026-09-20); the flip is one manual action in package settings Danger Zone, then it is durable. run-images.nu docs should state the visibility assumption.
(b) ENGINE ARM (durable): the docker sandbox provider must support AUTHENTICATED private-image pulls through the engine — server-configured registry credentials (per-registry, e.g. ghcr.io) passed to the Docker API on create/pull (X-Registry-Auth), NOT into the sandbox environment. This is an ADR-0019 credential-surface change (engine-held registry read credentials): needs the server-secrets-strategy treatment (where the credential lives, how it is redacted, who configures it) and a capability note in PROJECT_FACTS/docs. Acceptance: with a credential configured, a private first-use tag pulls successfully; without one, the failure message names the registry and says how to configure the credential (not a bare 401 rethrow).
Priority: user raises this to High — two consecutive fire slots lost after a routine release, both to this class.

title: Resume-from-failure: worker dies at 'checkpoint already exists' after fork event replay
description:
Production evidence 2026-09-19: POST /api/v1/runs/01M2XSA56XFSQPH3PAM4KXZCGY/resume returned 201 and correctly created the replacement run 01M2XYEJ9JG8PNZ7E2E0A9NBFD (fork events '...-fork-N' replayed through the evidence checkpoint, source archived with superseded_by set). But the new run's worker exited immediately (run.failed reason=terminated, 'Worker exited before emitting a terminal run event: exit status: 1'), with worker stderr: 'Precondition failed: checkpoint already exists in the run store — did you mean to resume?'

The irony is the contract: this IS the resume path. Hypothesis: the server-side fork path replays checkpoints into the new run's event store, and the worker's first checkpoint write (or its resume-mode checkpoint bootstrap) then collides with a replayed checkpoint instead of recognizing the fork continuation. Timing note: a conductor pass child started the same second; likely unrelated but worth excluding.

Reproduction: any terminal-failed run with committed checkpoints through the failed stage (e.g. soft-stop at reviewer after evidence) via POST /runs/{id}/resume on mirtuell.net.

Scope gap: fork_resume_from_failure tests (operations::fork_resume_from_failure, handler wiring, api conformance) cover the engine operation and wire contract, not the worker-side checkpoint bootstrap against replayed fork events. A regression test should spawn the worker path (or at least the checkpoint-store interaction) after a fork replay.

Source run branch with the rescued content (for reference until the fresh implementation lands): fabro/run/01M2XSA56XFSQPH3PAM4KXZCGY @ 79f2a045.

title: judgment-shadow hook + .fabro/judgments/ stream (ADR-0022 wave 1)
description:
Non-blocking host-side stage_complete hook (shared by develop/revisor/conductor via one [[run.hooks]] entry each, sandbox=false) that never lets the OpenRouter key enter a run sandbox or prompt. On evidence/reviewer stage completion, POST the stage context_updates (evidence capture) to OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13. ONE fan-out call, two question groups: (a) per-file residue adjudication for every file in the anomaly section (changed files NOT named by the seed spec): choice residue|adjacent_repair|scope_creep|harmless_churn; (b) verdict pre-screen: choice approved|changes_requested|verification_blocked. Append ONE JSON line per call to .fabro/judgments/<run_id>.jsonl, schema fabro-judgment-v1: run_id, node, visit, ts, model (versioned), questions_hash, answers, latency_ms, cost_usd, degraded. Fail-open on EVERY error path (timeout/429/5xx/invalid response): degraded line or skip, run never affected. Shadow only: no engine decision consumes the stream yet. Tests run against a scripted twin (extend fabro-test twin_openai pattern or wiremock stub for the decisions endpoint); the quality gate must NOT require live OpenRouter or credentials in the sandbox — live validation IS the shadow phase in production. Key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY from server env only (server-secrets-strategy).

RUNTIME PREREQUISITES (sharpened 2026-09-20, verified against fabro-tofu prod env): in production the fabro server runs CONTAINERIZED (fabro-app tofu module: image + /storage volume + docker.sock; NO host checkout mounted), so a sandbox=false hook executes INSIDE the server container. Consequences: (1) 'nu on the host' means nu IN THE SERVER IMAGE — RESOLVED 2026-09-20: VENDOR the official pinned musl tarball (github.com/nushell/nushell releases, e.g. nu-0.115.0-x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz, sha256-pinned like every other version pin in this repo) through the existing tmp/docker-context staging + COPY to /usr/local/bin — apk is DEAD for parity: alpine 3.23 AND 3.24 AND edge all ship nushell 0.104.1 (package stalled), so no Alpine bump helps. Verified end-to-end: vendored 0.115.0 musl binary runs static on the alpine base and judgment.nu passes the full smoke incl. default logging; as safety net judgment.nu is ALSO compatible with 0.104 (home-dir/home-path fallback) if the vendored binary is ever absent. (2) judgment.nu is unreachable from the container (no checkout mounted): vendor it into the image (COPY, rides the release pipeline like the binary) or seed /storage/scripts via the tofu storage-seed pattern; image-vendoring preferred so script and engine version together. (3) OPENROUTER_API_KEY travels the EXISTING tofu secret_routing table (modules/fabro-app/main.tf secret_routing + data.tf gopass source), channel 'env' — fabro-tofu IS the right lever for the key. (4) Dev/bare-server context (fabro server start on a laptop) needs nothing new: nu + checkout already present. Acceptance includes: hook degrades to fail-open when nu or key is absent (degraded log line, run unaffected).

EXECUTION-PATH CONFIRMATION (2026-09-20, executor.rs): a sandbox=false hook runs as a DIRECT child of the server process via `sh -c <command>` — it bypasses the environment/sandbox-provider layer entirely (the settings' `local` environment is run-stage placement, irrelevant for hooks; prod settings.toml.tpl has local provider enabled but unused). Double fail-open: engine-level, a non-blocking hook's failure decision is IGNORED by the runner (warn log only) — plus the script's own degraded contract. Command runs as the unprivileged fabro user (uid 1000) inside the server container; `sh` (busybox ash) exists in-image today, `nu` does not (image prerequisite stands).
