title: Automate toolchain pin via environments API after deploy (drop manual pinning)
description:
STATUS QUO (2026-09-20): the toolchain run environment is a server-managed environment store entry (GET /api/v1/environments/toolchain returns id/provider/docker image/resources/revision). After each release the user pins it MANUALLY to the freshly pushed ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain:<sha12> tag. run-images.nu already computes and pushes that tag; the server exposes PUT /api/v1/environments/{id} (replaceEnvironment, If-Match = current revision) — verified live against mirtuell (pin currently 1e239bc8bb9f, matching the deployed 0.361.0-nightly image).

DEMAND: automate the pin step so a release sequence needs no manual toolchain pinning:
- A small nu script (e.g. scripts/pin-toolchain.nu, or an arm of run-images.nu behind a flag): read the just-pushed toolchain tag (same sha12 logic), GET the environment for its revision, PUT the updated image.docker with If-Match; auth via the CLI's stored token for the target server (FABRO_SERVER/--server, same pattern install-cli uses for local paths).
- ORDERING RULE (critical, per the 2026-09-16 release-pipeline decision: toolchain must stay in sync with the deployed server binary): the pin advances only AFTER the server deploy (tofu apply) of the matching image, or the script verifies server version/image sha parity before pinning. Pin must never run inside `just image-release` before the deploy.
- Recommended surface: a `just pin-toolchain` recipe the release runbook calls post-deploy (and later the deploy automation itself); image-release stays deploy-agnostic.
- Fail-closed: a 409/If-Match mismatch prints current vs expected revision and exits non-zero; never overwrites a NEWER pin (compare tag sha against deployed server version first).

ACCEPTANCE:
- One command pins the toolchain env on a target server; manual pinning is retired from the runbook.
- Idempotent: re-running with the same tag is a no-op (or prints already-pinned).
- A mismatch between deployed server image and the tag to pin aborts with a clear error.
- Verification: run against mirtuell after the next release; GET shows the new tag and the next develop run's spec carries it.

Analyzer pre-check: sd search 'toolchain pin' found no sibling (run-images.nu changes were 2026-09-16 sync decision; env-store automation untouched). Basis: live API probe 2026-09-20 (GET /api/v1/environments/toolchain, pin 1e239bc8bb9f, revision d3e30a32...), scripts/run-images.nu sha12 tagging, user release sequence 2026-09-20 (image pushed, tofu applied, pin set manually, scheduler on).

## USER DECISION (2026-09-20, #2): the surface is a FABRO CLI COMMAND, not a raw script call

The pin automation must not remain a one-off raw API call (unreusable, untyped, token-handling duplicated). The fabro CLI gains an environments command family that owns this:
- `fabro env list` / `fabro env show <id>` — read the server environment store (image, resources, lifecycle, revision).
- `fabro env update <id> --image <ref>` (and resource/lifecycle flags) — performs the GET-revision + PUT If-Match dance internally, retrying once on revision race, printing old -> new.
- `fabro env pin-toolchain [--tag <sha12>|--from-run-images]` — the release-runbook one-command pin: derives the just-pushed toolchain tag with the same sha12 logic as scripts/run-images.nu (or takes it explicitly), verifies deployed-server/tag parity BEFORE pinning (fail-closed), idempotent when already pinned.
- Ordering + fail-closed rules from decision #1 unchanged; `just pin-toolchain` becomes a thin wrapper over the CLI command (or is retired in favor of the CLI command in the runbook).
- CLI auth/token handling as for every other server command (--server / FABRO_SERVER).

title: CLI: automations command family — scheduler settings, breaker control, fire-drift monitoring
description:
USER DIRECTION (2026-09-20): beyond the environments/pin command (fabro-4f44), the CLI also lacks ANY surface for automations, scheduler settings, and automation monitoring — today every pause/resume/schedule-change/breaker-unlatch/fire is a raw API call or web UI click, which is exactly the non-reusable pattern the user wants retired.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (live, mirtuell 2026-09-20): automations API is full CRUD — listAutomations, createAutomation, retrieveAutomation, replaceAutomation, deleteAutomation, listAutomationRuns, createAutomationRun. Two automations live: conductor-fabro (schedule `*/30 * * * *` enabled, api trigger manual always-enabled, on_overlap=skip, breaker consecutive_count resets visible, last_run_id present) and architect-fabro. The schedule trigger carries an inline breaker (signature, consecutive_count, last_run_id); last_error exists at automation level.

DEMAND — fabro CLI command family `fabro automations` (alias `fabro auto`):
- READ/monitoring: `fabro automations list|show <id>` rendering triggers, enabled state, expression, NEXT fire time (computed client-side from the cron expression), breaker count/signature, last_error, last/next run linkage; `fabro automations runs <id>` for the fire history (wraps listAutomationRuns).
- SETTINGS: `fabro automations set-schedule <id> --cron '<expr>'`, `fabro automations pause|unpause <id>` (schedule-trigger enable/disable via replaceAutomation, If-Match handled internally like fabro-4f44's env update), `fabro automations breaker reset <id>` (explicit unlatch instead of opaque trigger-replace).
- FIRE: `fabro automations fire <id>` — the sanctioned manual trigger (replaces raw POST /api/v1/automations; the 2026-09-18 lesson showed unattributed manual fires from left-running watchers — a CLI surface makes the actor visible and the action auditable).
- MONITORING sugar (the optimization the user pointed at): `fabro automations status --watch` (or a doctor arm) flags FIRE DRIFT: schedule enabled but no successful fire within 2x the cron interval, breaker count > 0, last_error non-null — the silent-stall class that today needs rootprint forensics to notice.
- Docs: the API workflow section in AGENTS.md gains the CLI-first note; raw API calls stay for scripts only.

ACCEPTANCE: the four groups (read/settings/fire/monitor) each land with wire tests against mocked HTTP per the repo testing strategy; pause/unpause round-trips the trigger without dropping unrelated triggers; breaker reset is a no-op when clean; status flags drift with a deterministic rule (cron-interval-based, no LLM). Manual verification against mirtuell once deployed.

Analyzer pre-check: sd search 'automations cli|scheduler setting|breaker unlatch' found no sibling; fabro-986b (line recovery design) is engine-side and orthogonal. Basis: live automations probe 2026-09-20 (conductor-fabro revision 1ba5227e..., schedule trigger + breaker inline), OpenAPI automations endpoints (spec lines 4318-4557), user session directive.

title: Post-upgrade env-store skew: new engine hard-rejects docker disk limit, every run dies at sandbox init
description:
INCIDENT (2026-09-20 10:30 UTC, first cron fire after deploying 0.361.0-nightly): conductor run 01M2Z5V8B8HT687W839P9Q2FXG failed in 16 ms — sandbox.failed causes: `invalid spec: resources.disk_mb: the docker provider does not enforce a writable-layer disk limit` -> run.failed workflow_error, before any stage. Root cause: the server-managed environment `toolchain` carried `resources.disk: \"16GB\"` (accepted/ignored by the previous version); the upgraded engine's spec validation now REJECTS disk limits for the docker provider, turning a stale store field into a guaranteed per-run kill. Line was down between fires until the field was removed via PUT `environments/toolchain` (disk -> null, verified 200).

CLASS: same family as fabro-eec6 (projection-semantics era-sensitivity) — config accepted by version N becomes a hard error under version N+1 with NO upgrade-time signal; the failure only appears at the first run. DEMAND:
- Post-upgrade safety net: on server startup (or `fabro doctor` against a server), validate every environment-store entry against the CURRENT provider capability set and surface incompatible fields as a warning list (start still allowed, but the operator sees the exact fields before the first cron kill) — or auto-strip fields the provider documents as unenforced, with a log line.
- The env-update CLI surface (fabro-4f44 `fabro env update`) makes the repair a one-liner next time; document the incident as its first use case.
- Regression pin: an environment with a disk limit + docker provider must produce the validation error deterministically at CREATE/UPDATE time (fail at write, not at run) — check whether the write path already validates; if it does, the pre-upgrade store entry simply predates it, which is exactly the startup-validation gap above.

Basis: run 01M2Z5V8B8HT687W839P9Q2FXG events (sandbox.failed seq 7), env store GET before (disk 16GB, revision d3e30a32...) and after (disk null), fix applied live 2026-09-20 ~10:35 UTC, fabro-4f44 (env CLI), fabro-eec6 (era-sensitivity family).

## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-09-20, user hypothesis verified against run specs): the UI environment pin INTRODUCED the field

Evidence: develop run 01M2YVNCFP5RDFCFRW9FS42R0B (07:32 UTC, pre-update server) carried environment resources `{cpu 8, memory 8GB, disk null}` in its spec; the env-store GET at ~10:25 UTC (after the user pinned the new toolchain image through the WEB UI, before any fix) showed `disk: "16GB"`. The disk value entered the store exactly with that UI save — the environment editor form supplies a disk field (default/prefilled), the full-object replace wrote it, and the write path accepted it FOR THE DOCKER PROVIDER even though the same engine version hard-rejects it at sandbox creation. So this is NOT a legacy pre-upgrade entry: write-time provider validation is definitively missing.

REFINED DEMANDS (superseding the 'legacy entry' framing):
1. WRITE-PATH validation (the bug proper): replaceEnvironment/create must validate resources against the target provider's capability set and REJECT unsupported fields (docker: disk) with a clear error naming the field — fail at write, never at the first run. Regression pin: PUT with disk on a docker env -> 400.
2. UI: the environment editor must not offer or submit fields the selected provider does not enforce; and a pin-style edit should change ONLY the image field (narrow patch or full-object-minus-unsupported), so a form default can never smuggle an incompatible value into a working environment.
3. The startup/doctor validation net from the original filing stays (defense in depth for any pre-existing rows).
4. fabro-4f44's `fabro env update` / `pin-toolchain` must send only the intended field change — same narrow-patch rule, so the automation structurally cannot reintroduce this class.

title: Grant the develop GitHub App workflows:write so .github/workflows seed deliverables can publish (ADR-0019)
description: Run 01M2ZEHCA127XFV2CMCVSEZDPJ went fully green (gate 107s, reviewer approved, seed closed in-sandbox at 13:25) but every run-branch push 13:22-13:25 was rejected with 'refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/release.yml without workflows permission' - the deliverable stranded (pull_request null, succeeded(publish_blocked)), USD 2.09 / 23 min lost, and the seed was falsely closed in-sandbox while the base tracker still shows it open (aftermath tracked by open fabro-meta-e294). Change (capability-affecting): grant fabro-the-factory[bot] the GitHub App 'workflows' write permission so run-branch pushes touching .github/workflows/** succeed. ADR-0019: this ADDS a permission on an agent-reachable publishing path; implementation awaits explicit user approval. Fix directions stay engine-mediated: the permission grant itself is an operator/App-settings action, and the guard rails (pre-claim preflight flag for .github/workflows-targeting seeds, closeout park-with-note on failed lifecycle push) are filed separately as non-capability script arms (see the overflow entry in .fabro/revisions/01M2ZEHCA127XFV2CMCVSEZDPJ.md). No raw clients, no token provisioning. Not covered by closed fabro-696c (generic PR credentials) or closed fabro-67e5 (server credential probe); open fabro-2e66 (surface PR degradation) is complementary engine-side. Basis: run 01M2ZEHCA127XFV2CMCVSEZDPJ, workflow version 8d3a780e5a0665da9cb87b36306f1ef7e10841bbc767996f563f828c08a277b6, commit 8431c97a4d525dafb07467d31d18c7cb2bf5f8bd

title: Blob markers must advertise byte size AND line count; reviewer pages via read_file offset/limit (supersedes fabro-9837)
description: fabro-9837's mandated reviewer first action (nu -c 'open --raw <path> | str substring') predates the 2026-09-17 reviewer shell denial and is now impossible to execute. In run 01M2ZEHCA127XFV2CMCVSEZDPJ the 48.9KB evidence capture was demoted to a blob; the shell-denied reviewer paged it with 4 read_file calls and still hit output truncation clipping ~28 tokens mid-file inside judgment_shadow.rs - an approval issued over silently clipped evidence. Effect: deterministic blob paging with no approvals over clipped evidence; builds on closed fabro-a0fe (generic read_file advice without line counts - this run clipped anyway). Complementary open seeds: fabro-9a43 (read_file for phrase checks), fabro-8cef (plain-text blob), fabro-cf3e (budget raise) - thematic overlap only. title: fabro_runs_list not repo-scoped: seeds survey saw fabro develop runs as its backlog
description:
First platform-proof finding from the seeds line (ADR-0023): the
fabro_runs_list engine tool is not repo-scoped.

Evidence (2026-09-26): seeds conductor pass 01M2ZPAE25JJJZ3JSDB01MN3MG
(repo denkhaus/seeds), survey stage journaled `revisor backlog:
01M2ZKNKZVPBN3JM24SQDGVGBT (newest develop run, PR 329 ...)` — that run
belongs to denkhaus/fabro's line (fabro's PR #329), not to the seeds
repo. The survey's backfill heuristic listed it because the runs list
the tool returns contains OTHER repos' runs.

Hazard: the seeds revisor's select stage calls
fabro_runs_list {"workflow": "develop"} — with cross-repo results it can
select a foreign repo's develop run, "revise" it against the wrong
clone, and file marker/journal artifacts for a run it does not own
(fabro's own revisor has the mirrored hazard now that two lines share
the server).

Demand: scope fabro_runs_list results to the invoking run's repository
by default, or add an explicit repo filter argument the revisor select
prompt passes; pin with a test that lists runs from repo A's sandbox
and asserts repo B's runs are absent.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (binding, decided in review 2026-09-26):
- Variant (a) is THE fix: default-scope fabro_runs_list results to the
  invoking run's repository. Variant (b) alone (optional filter arg,
  unchanged default) is NOT acceptable — every consumer would have to
  opt in and any forgetful prompt keeps the cross-repo hazard.
  An explicit repo override may exist additionally for admin/debug, but
  the default must be scoped.
- Consumer inventory (all want own-repo semantics; verified 2026-09-26):
  conductor survey backfill, revisor select candidate pool + freshness
  baseline, planner in-flight exclusion (step 4). No in-sandbox consumer
  needs cross-repo visibility.
- DEPLOY SEQUENCING (blast-radius control): the merge alone changes
  nothing for the seeds line — the behavior reaches BOTH lines only at
  the next server deploy. Deploy is the user's gate; no half-state.
- Regression pin: sandbox of repo A lists develop runs, repo B's runs
  absent; plus one revisor-select fixture where a foreign-repo run is
  newest and must not poison the freshness baseline.

CODE-VERIFIED SURFACE (2026-09-26, supersedes the variant-(a)/(b) framing
with a strictly better shape — user direction): the tool is fork-owned
(lib/components/fabro-tool/src/runs_list.rs); the backend ClientBackend
already carries run_scope (the invoking RunId) and the worker holds the
run spec with the target repo. Fix WITHOUT any consumer-facing parameter:

1. Server (fork-owned too): add a `repository` query filter to GET
   /api/v1/runs (OpenAPI-first, progenitor regen) that filters BEFORE
   pagination — client-side after-filtering would break paging.
2. Tool: extend the runs_list backend path with the invoking run's
   repository (from the run spec at worker context construction) and
   pass it on every call automatically. No prompt, script, or loop asset
   in either repo changes; both lines receive the scoping at the next
   server deploy.
3. Regression pins stay: repo-A sandbox lists, repo-B runs absent; and a
   foreign newest run must not poison the revisor select freshness
   baseline.
